rules.description: A Python manifest (`requirements*.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, `Pipfile*`, `poetry.lock`, `uv.lock`) pins `litellm` at a version below 1.83.7. BerriAI/litellm shipped the CVE-2026-30623 fix in v1.83.7 on 2026-04-30. AAK-MCP-STDIO-CMD-INJ-001 already covers the source-side architectural shape; this pin-only rule complements it by surfacing a discrete finding for consumers who run pin-check mode and need an actionable manifest fix. The <1.83.7 floor also flags the LiteLLM MCP-proxy CVE cluster, all in versions below the floor: CVE-2026-12773 (improper authentication in the MCP proxy `UserAPIKeyAuth`, <=1.59.8), CVE-2026-12774 (SSRF in MCP server connection testing, <=1.82.2), and CVE-2026-12798 (SSRF in the MCP OpenAPI spec loader, <=1.82.2). Wired into `aak fix --cve` so the auto-fixer can rewrite requirements*.txt entries to `litellm>=1.83.7`.
rules.limitations: Reads the dependency declarations of the root requirements*.txt, pyproject.toml and Pipfile in their own formats, and reports one whose range admits a release below 1.83.7 (`litellm<1.83.7` included), and the version the root Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock or uv.lock resolves when it is below 1.83.7. A git requirement's dotted release tag is read as its version (`@v1.83.0`); a commit, a branch or a tag with no dot (`@v2`) states none. A declaration that states no version, such as `litellm` alone or a git URL without a release tag, is not reported, and neither is a requirements file in a sub-directory or an `.mcp.json` launcher. A compose file's `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm` image tag is not read. A manifest over 2 MB is not read. A lockfile over 32 MiB is not read.
rules.remediation: Bump `litellm` to >= 1.83.7. `aak fix --cve` rewrites a requirements*.txt pin in place; `pyproject.toml` / lockfile edits should go through the project's normal dependency-update workflow.
rules.title: LiteLLM pin floor for CVE-2026-30623 (<1.83.7)

rules.description: With `scan --llm-scan`, the chosen model read a tool's metadata (an MCP tool's name, description and parameter descriptions, or a skill's instructions) and judged that it tries to manipulate the agent that reads it: an action the user did not ask for, collecting or sending data the tool does not need, hijacking other tools, overriding the agent's instructions, impersonation, deception or concealment. This is a model's judgement, not a pattern match; the evidence quotes its reason.
rules.limitations: Reads only metadata AAK can extract without running anything: inline tools in MCP configs, saved `tools/list` responses (`*tools*.json`), Python tools registered with `@x.tool`, `@tool` or `Tool(name=..., description=...)` string literals, TypeScript/JavaScript `server.tool(...)` and `registerTool(...)` string literals, and SKILL.md. A description a server builds at runtime, concatenates from several strings, or returns only from a live `tools/list` is never seen. The verdict is a model's: it can miss manipulation phrased as ordinary documentation and flag benign text.
rules.remediation: Read the flagged text and the model's reason. Remove any instruction aimed at the agent rather than the user: hidden directives, requests to read or send data the tool does not need, references that steer other tools. If you do not control the tool, stop using it until its publisher fixes the description.
rules.title: Model flagged tool metadata as manipulative

rules.description: `scan --llm-scan` was asked to analyze a tool's metadata and could not: the provider credential is missing, the request failed, the reply was cut off before the verdict, the provider declined to analyze it, or the text exceeded the analysed length. The scan cannot show a clean result for what it skipped, so, like a crashed scanner, this makes the run INCOMPLETE.
rules.remediation: Fix the cause the evidence names and re-run, or pass --allow-scanner-failure to accept the gap. When the model declined to analyze a tool, read that tool's metadata yourself: a refusal is not a clean result.
rules.title: LLM analysis did not cover a tool

rules.description: An agent / LLM application feeds model-generated SQL into a database executor whose connection role holds code-execution or filesystem privileges, turning prompt-injected SQL into remote code execution. Two arms fire this rule: (a) an LLM-output value reaches a SQL-execution sink (`cursor.execute` / `conn.execute` / SQLAlchemy `text(...)` / a TS `.query()`/`.raw()` call) as the query itself — not as a bound parameter — with no allow-list or query-validation step; and (b) a DB connection string / role that grants the dangerous primitives (a superuser connection account, or a literal PostgreSQL `COPY ... FROM PROGRAM` / `pg_execute_server_program`, MySQL `FILE` / `INTO OUTFILE` / `LOAD_FILE`, or MS SQL `xp_cmdshell`) inside an LLM/agent context. CVE-2026-25879 is the documented instance: a text-to-SQL chat agent ran model output on a superuser connection and a prompt-injected `COPY ... FROM PROGRAM` produced a shell. CWE-94 (Code Injection) / CWE-89 (SQL Injection) chained to CWE-78 (OS Command Injection) through CWE-250 (Execution with Unnecessary Privileges). This is distinct from `AAK-TAINT-005`, where the tainted source is a tool *parameter* string-formatted into SQL rather than LLM output landing on an RCE-capable role.
rules.limitations: The flow arm follows model output through assignments into the first argument of a call named `execute`, `executemany`, `executescript` or `exec_driver_sql`; LangChain's `db.run(sql)` is not a sink. Any identifier, import or string in the file containing `sqlglot`, `sqlparse`, `allowlist` or `whitelist` switches that arm off, so `sqlparse.format(sql, reindent=True)`, which only pretty-prints, counts as validation. The privilege arm judges the database role from a literal connection URI or literal SQL text in the source: a DSN read from `os.environ` is not seen.
rules.remediation: Never execute LLM-generated SQL directly. Constrain the model to parameterised, allow-listed queries (validate with `sqlglot`/`sqlparse` and reject anything that is not a single read-only `SELECT` against an approved table set), and run every agent query on a dedicated least-privilege, read-only role that lacks `pg_execute_server_program` / `FILE` / `xp_cmdshell` and cannot `COPY ... FROM PROGRAM`. Treat the DB role as the last line of defence: even a perfect prompt filter must not sit in front of a superuser connection.
rules.title: LLM-generated SQL executed on an RCE-capable database role

rules.description: A vision-language pipeline calls `lmdeploy.serve.vl_engine.*` (or framework-equivalent) preprocessing helpers with a URL argument that is not validated against an allow-list. CVE-2026-33626 (GHSA-only at time of v0.3.6 cut — NVD enrichment pending) documents this exact shape: an attacker submits an image URL that points at a private endpoint, the loader fetches it server-side, and the response is processed by the VL pipeline. Same SSRF class as AAK-LANGCHAIN-SSRF-REDIR-001 but tied to the VL image loader.
rules.limitations: Looks in a Python file that mentions lmdeploy for `load_image(url`, `encode_image(url`, `preprocess_image_url(`, `VLEngine()` or the `lmdeploy.serve.vl_engine.VLEngine` path, and skips the file if it contains an SSRF guard name, `ALLOWED_HOSTS` or `TrustedHostMiddleware`. The argument has to begin with `url`: `load_image(image_url)` is not matched. A Python file over 1 MB is not read.
rules.remediation: Wrap the URL with the same SSRF guard you use for any other fetch: validate the resolved IP against an allow-list, disable redirects, and pin the resolved IP for the actual request. Upgrade `lmdeploy` to >= 0.12.3 and pin it: versions below 0.12.3 are affected (GHSA-6w67-hwm5-92mq). Exploitation was observed within roughly twelve hours of the advisory, so treat an unpinned or older install as urgent rather than routine.
rules.title: LMDeploy VL image loader fetches user-controlled URLs without allow-list

rules.description: A `@tool`-decorated function parameter flows into logger.info / print / sys.stdout.write / console.log without stripping control characters (\r, \n, \x1b) first. CVE-2026-6494 (AAP MCP, CVSS 5.3 MEDIUM, CWE-117) lets an attacker forge log entries and inject ANSI escape sequences to socially engineer an operator. A write to stdout (`print` without `file=`, `sys.stdout`, `console.log`) does more harm in a STDIO server: stdout carries the JSON-RPC stream, which the MCP stdio transport says must hold nothing but valid MCP messages, so caller input written there corrupts it and a whole JSON-RPC line can inject a message. Stripping control characters does not stop that; diagnostics belong on stderr.
rules.limitations: Reads the arguments of `print` (to stdout, or with `file=` set to `sys.stdout`, `sys.stderr`, a bare `stdout` or `stderr` or `None`), of a level method (`info`, `exception` and the rest) of `logger`, `log` or the `logging` module, of any `sys.stdout` or `sys.stderr` method and of `console.<log|info|warn|error>`, in functions whose decorator name ends in `tool` and the functions nested in them. A call inside a tool function nested in another is read for the innermost one only, with its parameters, so a nested tool that logs a parameter of the tool around it is not reported. A logger held as an attribute (`self.logger.info(...)`) is not read: measured on 9,137 Python files from GitHub code searches for MCP servers, it would add 69 findings, only 44 of them (64%) a raw string parameter. Nor is a logger under another name (`_logger.info(...)`). A call to a function whose name contains `sanitize`, `strip_control` or `escape_controls` anywhere in the function clears it, whichever value that touches, and so does sanitising code written anywhere in it, a comment included: `.replace("\r"` or `.replace("\n"`, `.encode("ascii", "ignore")`, or an `re.sub(` whose pattern begins with an escape such as `\r` or `\x1b`. The word `sanitize` in a docstring, a comment or a name that is not called does not.
rules.remediation: Write diagnostics to stderr (`print(..., file=sys.stderr)` or a logger that writes there), never to stdout: stdout carries the protocol in a STDIO server, so caller input there can inject messages. Strip \r\n\x1b (or accept only printable ASCII) before logging anything derived from tool input. Prefer structured logging (JSON/logfmt) so log consumers aren't confused by forged lines.
rules.title: MCP tool logs caller-controlled input without CRLF/ANSI sanitization

rules.description: A manifest pins, a lockfile resolves, a site-packages directory has installed, or an image reference by digest runs a release that the offline malicious-release feed lists: OSV's OpenSSF Malicious Packages (`MAL-`) records for PyPI and npm, GitHub's malware advisories when `aak update` could read them, and image digests from vendor incident reports. Such a release is malware rather than a flaw below a fix, so no version pin catches it: litellm 1.107.0 (21 Oct 2026, OSV MAL-2026-2144) sat above every pinned floor and ran a credential stealer at every Python start. A scan reads the feed `aak update` caches at `~/.agent-audit-kit/malicious_releases.json`, else the copy bundled with AAK, and never touches the network; the SARIF run and the console summary name the copy and when it was generated.
rules.limitations: Reads, anywhere outside AAK's skip directories, requirements*.txt, pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json (not its `scripts`) and the launches in MCP configs (`.mcp.json`, `mcp.json`, `claude_desktop_config.json`, `*.mcp.json`, `*.mcp.yaml`, `*.mcp.yml`) for a declaration that pins one version; the lockfiles uv.lock, poetry.lock, Pipfile.lock, package-lock.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock (v1) for resolved versions; `<name>-<version>.dist-info` directories in the site-packages and dist-packages directories AAK-STARTUP-HOOK-PTH-001's walk reaches; and `@sha256:` image references in Dockerfiles, YAML files and MCP configs. A version matches exactly, PEP 440 normalised for PyPI and as written for npm, so a pre-release beside a malicious release (litellm 1.107.0rc1) is not reported, and npm's `0.0.1-security` placeholder never matches. A range, or a declaration without a version, matches only an entry that lists every release of the package, since a range does not say which release was installed. An image tag never matches, only a digest, and a digest matches whatever registry name the reference gives it. A program an MCP config runs by name names no registry and is not read, nor are `.egg-info` installs, `node_modules`, conda metadata or an image's registry layers. The bundled feed lists only MAL-2026-2144 (litellm 1.82.7, 1.82.8 and 1.107.0) and one image index digest, so without `aak update` nothing else is known. A lockfile that resolves one release more than once is reported once, at its first entry, and an image reference is quoted from at most 256 characters before its digest. A manifest over 2 MB, a lockfile over 32 MiB or an image-reference file over 2 MB is not read.
rules.remediation: Remove the release: pin a version the feed does not list (for litellm, 1.106.2, the version LiteLLM named), re-lock, and rebuild the environment or image from scratch rather than upgrading in place. Treat every environment, host or cluster that installed or ran it as compromised: rotate each credential it could reach and review its outbound traffic. Run `aak update` to refresh the feed.
rules.title: A declared, locked, installed or deployed release is listed as malware

rules.description: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json lacks a signature or integrity hash field. An attacker with write access to the marketplace can replace the plugin bundle with no detection.
rules.limitations: Checks only that each entry in the `plugins` list of a marketplace.json has a key named `signature`, `integrity`, `sha256`, `sigstore` or `publicKey`, not that the value is a signature or that it verifies, so `"signature": "TODO"` passes. Plugins listed as an object instead of a list are not read, and a manifest that is not valid JSON is not checked for a signature at all: AAK-MARKETPLACE-005 reports that it could not be read. A `marketplace.json` over 1 MB is not read, and AAK-MARKETPLACE-005 reports it as unreadable.
rules.remediation: Add a Sigstore signature or subresource-integrity hash to each plugin entry. Verify on install.
rules.title: Unsigned marketplace.json manifest

rules.description: A plugin's manifest grants access to filesystem, network, shell exec, or user-credential surfaces. Broad permissions should be opt-in after a clear user prompt.
rules.limitations: Reads the `permissions` of each plugin entry in a marketplace.json, as a list of `scope:action` strings, one such string, or an object from scope to an action, a list of actions or `true` (every action), and reports a grant that covers `fs:*`, `shell:exec`, `network:*`, `credentials:*`, `env:*` or `*:*`: case is ignored, a `*` on either side stands for every scope or action, and a bare `*` is `*:*`. A narrower grant on one of those scopes (`fs:write`, `credentials:read`), a grant that covers none of the six (`*:read` reads every scope but is not one), a string with no colon (`network`), and permissions declared in a plugin's own `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` are not reported. A `marketplace.json` over 1 MB is not read, and AAK-MARKETPLACE-005 reports it as unreadable.
rules.remediation: Trim permissions to the minimum the plugin needs. Review any 'fs:*' or 'shell:exec' entries.
rules.title: Plugin permission set grants broad access

rules.description: A plugin entry uses a name that is one edit distance from a popular upstream (e.g. 'anthropic', 'langchain', 'mcp'). Typosquatting is the single highest-volume supply-chain attack vector in 2026.
rules.limitations: Compares a plugin name with 13 upstream names (anthropic, claude, claude-code, claude-agent-sdk, mcp, model-context-protocol, langchain, langchain-core, langgraph, openai, openai-agents-sdk, gemini, google-adk) and reports one that is a single insertion, deletion, substitution or adjacent swap away. A name that extends an upstream (`claude-code-pro`, `anthropic-official`) or sits two edits away (`antrhopik`) is not reported. A `marketplace.json` over 1 MB is not read, and AAK-MARKETPLACE-005 reports it as unreadable.
rules.remediation: Rename the plugin or flag it for manual review. Cross-reference against a known-upstream list.
rules.title: Plugin name typosquats a well-known package

rules.description: A plugin entry pins to a branch (main/master) or tag without commit SHA. The maintainer (or an attacker with write access) can silently change plugin behavior post-install — the 'maintainer takeover' pattern from the June 2024 xz incident and its 2026 re-runs.
rules.limitations: Judges a plugin's `source` only when it is an object with a `ref`, `branch` or `tag` that is not 7 to 40 hex characters. A source with no ref at all, which follows the default branch, a source written as a string (`github:acme/tool@main`) and an all-digit tag such as `20260101`, which reads as a short commit hash, are not reported. A `marketplace.json` over 1 MB is not read, and AAK-MARKETPLACE-005 reports it as unreadable.
rules.remediation: Pin to an immutable commit SHA. Re-pin during a reviewed dependency bump.
rules.title: Plugin source pins to a mutable git ref

rules.description: A `marketplace.json` is not valid JSON, is not UTF-8 text, or is JSON whose top level is not an object, so none of its plugin entries could be checked for a signature, broad permissions, a typosquatted name or a mutable source ref (AAK-MARKETPLACE-001..004). AAK reports this rather than skipping the file, which is what it used to do: a manifest the scanner cannot read is not a clean one, and a client that parses more leniently may still install what it lists.
rules.limitations: A `marketplace.json` over 1 MB is reported here as unreadable.
rules.remediation: Fix the manifest so it is a UTF-8 JSON object (a trailing comma, a comment and an unquoted key are the usual causes), then re-run the scan so its plugins are audited. If the file is not a plugin marketplace manifest, rename it.
rules.title: Marketplace manifest could not be read

rules.description: An MCP server uses HTTP transport (url field) without a recognized authentication or access-control header. Recognized schemes are Authorization / Bearer, X-API-Key / Api-Key, the custom credential-header family (X-*-Key, *-API-Key, *_API_KEY, *-Subscription-Key and similar), and the x402 X-PAYMENT gate, declared via an env/template reference (e.g. ${API_KEY}). A custom auth header carrying a hardcoded literal secret still fires — the credential is exposed in the config, so the endpoint is effectively unprotected. A server on a loopback host (localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1, 0.0.0.0) is not reported. Unauthenticated remote servers can be MITM'd or spoofed.
rules.limitations: Reads the `url` field of each server in `mcpServers`, or `servers` in VS Code's `.vscode/mcp.json`, and looks for an `Authorization`, `Bearer`, `X-API-Key` or `API-Key` header, or for one of a fixed family of custom credential headers (`X-*-Key`, `X-*-Token` but not `X-CSRF-Token` or `X-XSRF-Token`, `X-*-Secret`, a name ending in `-API-Key`, `_API_KEY` or `ApiKey`, `*-API-Token`, `*-Access-Key`, `*-Client-Secret`, `*-Subscription-Key`, `X-Auth-Token`, `X-Access-Token`, `X-Payment`) whose value is empty or blank, or contains a `${VAR}`, `$VAR`, `{{VAR}}`, `<VAR>` or `%VAR%` reference, your, change-me (also change_me and change me), changeme, placeholder, redacted, dummy or four x's anywhere, `_here` at the end of a word, or example or sample as a whole word (an underscore joins words, so `example_key` does not count); `"X-Foo-Key": ""` and `"k9f2-example-77a1"` both count as a declared scheme. A remote URL given any other way is not examined: as an argument to a bridge (`npx mcp-remote https://...`) or under another key such as `serverUrl`. A server on a loopback host (localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1 or 0.0.0.0) is not reported, though one that checks no `Origin` header can still be reached from a web page through DNS rebinding. A URL that Node, requests and Rust's `url` crate read differently from curl, httpx and urlsplit, which keep a backslash inside the authority, is judged by the less safe of the two readings, so `http://localhost\@evil.example/`, which curl and httpx send to evil.example, is reported.
rules.remediation: Add OAuth 2.1 bearer token or API key header authentication (reference the secret via an env var, do not hardcode it in the config).
rules.title: Remote MCP server without authentication

rules.description: An MCP server command contains shell metacharacters or shell wrappers (sh -c, bash -c). This enables command injection via argument composition.
rules.limitations: Looks only at the `command` string of each server in `mcpServers`, or `servers` in VS Code's `.vscode/mcp.json`, for one of the characters | ; & ` $ ( ) or a leading `sh -c`, `bash -c`, `cmd /c` or `cmd.exe /c`, after removing any VS Code variable (`${workspaceFolder}`, `${userHome}`, `${env:...}` and the others VS Code documents), which VS Code substitutes itself. The same wrapper split into `command: bash` and `args: ["-c", ...]` is not read by this rule.
rules.remediation: Put only the program in `command` and every argument in `args`. This rule matches `sh -c`, `bash -c`, `cmd /c` and any of `|`, `;`, `&`, `$`, `(`, `)` or a backtick in `command`, so a path such as `$HOME/bin/server`, or one containing parentheses, fires it too. A VS Code variable such as `${workspaceFolder}`, which VS Code substitutes itself, does not.
rules.title: MCP server command runs with shell expansion

rules.description: Hardcoded secrets found in mcpServers env block. Secrets in project-scoped MCP config are committed to git.
rules.limitations: Reads the `env` block of each server in `mcpServers`, or `servers` in VS Code's `.vscode/mcp.json`, and flags a value that is not a bare `${VAR}` when the variable name contains KEY, SECRET, TOKEN, PASSWORD, CREDENTIAL, ANTHROPIC, OPENAI or AWS_. A literal secret in `headers` (`Authorization: Bearer ...`) or inside a connection string under another name (`DATABASE_URL=postgres://user:pass@host/db`) is not matched. A value is taken for a setting or a dummy, and not reported, when it is under six characters, holds a `${...}`, `{{...}}` or `<...>` reference or a placeholder word (your, change-me, placeholder, redacted, dummy, example, sample, `_here`, four x's), is under 40 characters and contains test, demo, password, 1234 or abcd, or sits under a name ending in `_NAME`, `_ID` or `_TOKENS` or containing `TOKENIZER`; so a short real password (`DB_PASSWORD=Kq7#v`) and a 32-character hex key that happens to contain `abcd` pass.
rules.remediation: Replace the literal value with a reference of the form `${NAME}`, set `NAME` in your shell or secrets manager, and rotate the secret if it was ever committed.
rules.title: MCP server environment exposes secrets

rules.description: More than 10 MCP servers in a single config. Large tool surface increases attack surface.
rules.limitations: Counts the entries of one server map (`mcpServers`, or `servers` in VS Code's `.vscode/mcp.json`) in one config file and fires above 10. Servers split across files are not added up: six in `.vscode/mcp.json` and six in the `.mcp.json` beside it, which VS Code's agent host loads together, pass.
rules.remediation: Remove the servers this project does not use until each server map, `mcpServers` or VS Code's `servers`, lists 10 or fewer. The rule counts each map on its own and fires above 10.
rules.title: Excessive number of MCP servers declared

rules.description: The command uses npx, uvx, bunx, or pnpx which fetches the latest version from a registry at runtime, vulnerable to typosquatting and dependency confusion.
rules.limitations: Fires when the first word of `command` is npx, uvx, bunx or pnpx. The same fetch through another launcher is not matched: `pnpm dlx`, `pipx run`, `cmd /c npx`, or an absolute path such as `/usr/local/bin/npx`.
rules.remediation: Install the server ahead of time at a fixed version and point `command` at the installed program (for example `node` with the path to its entry file), so nothing is downloaded when the client starts. Pinning a version in `args` (AAK-MCP-007) lowers the risk but does not clear this rule, which fires on `npx`, `uvx`, `bunx` or `pnpx` as the command.
rules.title: MCP server uses npx/uvx to fetch and execute remote packages

rules.description: The command uses a relative path that can be hijacked via PATH manipulation.
rules.limitations: Fires on a `command` that is not an absolute path, except for a fixed list of common launchers (node, python, python3, npx, uvx, bunx, pnpx, docker, deno, bun, cargo, go, java, ruby). Those are resolved through PATH in the same way and are never reported.
rules.remediation: Use absolute paths for MCP server executables.
rules.title: MCP server command uses relative path

rules.description: Package name in args lacks @version suffix when using npx/uvx. Unpinned packages can silently update to malicious versions. Not reported for a launch AAK-SUPPLY-001 reports in the same scan.
rules.limitations: Looks for a package argument after npx, uvx, bunx or pnpx that has no `@version` suffix. Any suffix counts as a pin, including the floating tag `@latest`. The same package fetched through `cmd /c npx` is not checked.
rules.remediation: Pin with @x.y.z suffix, e.g., @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem@2025.1.1
rules.title: MCP server lacks version pinning in args

rules.description: The headersHelper field executes arbitrary shell commands to generate headers. A malicious repo can exfiltrate data via header generation.
rules.limitations: Reads the `headersHelper` field of servers under `mcpServers` (or `servers`) in `.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.continue/config.json`, `.gemini/settings.json` and other `*mcp*.json` files. Servers declared inline in a Claude Code plugin manifest (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`) are not read.
rules.remediation: Avoid headersHelper in project-scoped configs. Use static headers or OAuth flows instead.
rules.title: MCP server headersHelper executes arbitrary commands

rules.description: The MCP server URL contains a private-range address (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x), a `.local` name, or a loopback address (localhost, 127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0, ::1) somewhere other than its own host, such as a proxy target in the query, which may expose internal services (SSRF pattern). A server whose own host is loopback is not reported.
rules.limitations: Looks in the server `url` for the 10.x, 172.16-31.x and 192.168.x ranges, a `.local` name, or the text localhost, 127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0 or ::1, and reads its host as a client does, so `http://10.1/`, `http://0xa.0.0.5/` and `http://%31%30.0.0.5/` are 10.x too; a URL whose own host is loopback (localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1 or 0.0.0.0) is not reported. A URL that Node, requests and Rust's `url` crate read differently from curl, httpx and urlsplit, which keep a backslash inside the authority, is judged by the less safe of the two readings. Other internal addresses are not matched: a name such as `mcp.corp.internal` or the shared range 100.64.0.0/10.
rules.remediation: Confirm you run and trust the server at that address. If it should not be there, remove the entry or point `url` at the intended public HTTPS endpoint. If it is deliberate (a dev server on your LAN or a sidecar), accept it by listing `AAK-MCP-009` under `exclude-rules` in `.agent-audit-kit.yml`, with a comment saying why. The rule matches RFC 1918 private addresses, `.local` hosts, and a loopback address anywhere in the URL except its own host.
rules.title: MCP server URL contains an internal network address

rules.description: An MCP server is configured with filesystem root (/) or home directory access, allowing unrestricted file operations.
rules.limitations: Fires when an argument is exactly `/`, `~`, `/home`, `/Users`, `/etc` or `/var`. A home directory written as a specific path (`/Users/alice`), as `~/` or as `${HOME}` is not matched.
rules.remediation: Restrict filesystem access to specific project directories only.
rules.title: MCP server config allows arbitrary filesystem root access

rules.description: A remote MCP server exposes an HTTP handler with no authentication check. Per MCP spec 2025-11-25 all remote servers must require OAuth 2.1 or an equivalent bearer credential. Matches the CVE-2026-33032 pattern where /mcp_message was exposed without the auth middleware that /mcp used.
rules.limitations: Looks for a FastAPI handler declared as `@app.post("/mcp...")` (or get, put, patch, delete) directly above a `def` whose parameter list holds no parenthesis, in a file that names an MCP server class, with no `Depends(` or `@require_auth` in the 200 characters before it. The same handler declared on an `APIRouter` (`@router.post("/mcp")`), with another decorator between the route and the `def`, with a default such as `= Body(...)`, or the FastMCP app mounted with `app.mount("/mcp", mcp.streamable_http_app())`, is not matched.
rules.remediation: Apply the same auth middleware to every MCP HTTP route. Do not branch on method or path before enforcing auth.
rules.title: Remote MCP server handler lacks authentication middleware

rules.description: An MCP server's IP allowlist configuration defaults to an empty list, which its middleware interprets as 'allow all'. This is the exact CVE-2026-33032 root cause. Tight-by-default is required.
rules.limitations: Looks for `ip_allowlist`, `allowed_ips` or `cidr_allowlist` (underscore optional, any case) assigned a literal empty list, `None`, `null` or `""` directly. A type-annotated default (`allowed_ips: list[str] = []`) or another name for the same list (`ip_whitelist = []`) is not matched.
rules.remediation: Default to deny-all; require explicit allowlist entries. Reject empty allowlists at startup.
rules.title: MCP server default IP allowlist is empty (allow-all)

rules.description: An MCP HTTP endpoint sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin to '*' while also returning credentials/tokens. This allows hostile origins to read MCP responses from a victim browser session.
rules.limitations: Looks in one file for the header name `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` followed by a quoted `"*"` and the name `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` followed by `true`. The usual framework options (`CORSMiddleware(..., allow_origins=["*"], allow_credentials=True)`, `cors({ origin: "*", credentials: true })`) do not contain those names and are not matched.
rules.remediation: Restrict CORS to an explicit origin allowlist. Never combine '*' with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true.
rules.title: Wildcard CORS on MCP endpoint

rules.description: An MCP client or server expects authentication tokens in URL query parameters. Query parameters land in server access logs, browser history, and referer headers, making this a token-leak vector.
rules.limitations: Looks for `?token=`-style text, `query_params.get("token")` and `req.query.token` with the names access_token, api_key, token, auth or bearer. Other ways to read a credential from the query string, `new URL(req.url).searchParams.get("token")` or Flask's `request.args.get("token")`, are not matched.
rules.remediation: Pass tokens in the Authorization header, never in query params.
rules.title: Auth token transmitted via URL query parameter

rules.description: An MCP server exposes a resource/file handler that passes user-supplied paths to open()/fs.readFile without normalization or allowlist checks. 2,614 MCP implementations surveyed; 82% had this class of issue. In a TypeScript tool handler it also follows a destructured tool argument through `path.join` / `path.resolve` to an fs read or write with no containment check in between, the shape of CVE-2026-94044.
rules.limitations: Regex and proximity, not data flow. The TypeScript arm follows one `path.join` / `path.resolve` from a destructured tool argument to an fs read or write within one handler-sized window, so a path assembled through helper functions is missed. It stays silent on a containment check it recognises (`startsWith`, `path.relative`, `realpath`) and on any `if` naming the joined path that throws or returns, by design, so a weak check can silence it; `path.basename()` around the argument counts as sanitizing.
rules.remediation: Resolve the requested path, reject '..' components, and verify the final path is under an explicit root directory.
rules.title: Path traversal in MCP resource or tool file handler

rules.description: An MCP endpoint written in Go (net/http, gin, echo, chi) or Python (FastAPI/Starlette, Flask) reads the whole request body (`io.ReadAll(r.Body)`, `json.NewDecoder(r.Body)`, gin's `ShouldBindJSON`, echo's `Bind`, `await request.json()`, `request.get_json()`) and nothing in the server limits its size. None of these frameworks sets a limit of its own, so one request can hold as much memory as it likes, and the prompt or tool arguments it carries reach the model at any length (token-cost denial of service).
rules.limitations: Reads Go handlers (a function taking `*http.Request`, `*gin.Context` or `echo.Context`) and Python functions registered as FastAPI, Starlette or Flask routes, and only those that serve MCP: registered in the same file on a route whose path ends in an `mcp` segment (`/mcp`, `/api/v1/mcp`, `/mcp/message`, `/mcp/tools/call`) with no settings segment before it (`/admin/mcp` and `/api/config/mcp`, under `admin`, `config`, `configs`, `configuration`, `settings`, `setting` or `preferences`, are taken for a settings API and not read), or dispatching on a method only MCP has (`case "tools/call":`, `method == "resources/read"`; in a Go `case` list the method's string must start within 160 characters of `case`). A handler that dispatches only on `initialize` or `notifications/initialized`, which a language server's handshake shares, counts only in a file that names one of those methods too, so a bridge that answers the handshake and forwards every other method is missed. It is silent when the handler tests Content-Length or calls a helper named for a body limit, when a Python handler tests the length of what it read (a Go handler that compares `len(body)` after reading the whole body is still reported), and when the project's non-test code sets a limit anywhere (`http.MaxBytesReader`, `http.MaxBytesHandler`, echo `BodyLimit`, chi `RequestSize`, gin's `RequestSizeLimiter`, a `.Body =` reassignment through `io.LimitReader`, a Go `ContentLength >` test whose `{` opens on the comparison's own line within 80 characters and answers 413 within 300 characters after it with no `}` between, so a 413 written after a map literal (`writeJSON(w, map[string]string{...}, 413)`) does not count, Flask `MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH`, a Starlette middleware that answers 413 or compares Content-Length), so a limit on another route, or in another project of a monorepo, silences it too. Not read: TypeScript and JavaScript servers (Express and Fastify parse bodies with a default limit; Hono and Next.js depend on the runtime), a Python file that imports aiohttp, Django, Tornado, Quart, Sanic, Litestar, Falcon or Bottle, even one that uses it only as a client (a FastAPI server that calls an API through aiohttp), a body read in a helper the handler calls, a server that hands the request to a library that reads it whole (mark3labs/mcp-go's `StreamableHTTPServer` reads it with `io.ReadAll` and no limit), test files and mock or fake servers, files over 1,000,000 bytes, and a limit enforced only by a reverse proxy or the hosting platform (nginx `client_max_body_size`, an ingress annotation).
rules.remediation: Bound the body before reading it. In Go, `r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, 1<<20)` in the handler or `http.MaxBytesHandler(mux, 1<<20)` where the server is built (echo: `middleware.BodyLimit("1M")`; chi: `middleware.RequestSize(1<<20)`). In Flask, set `app.config["MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH"]`. Starlette and FastAPI have no setting: add a middleware that answers 413 when Content-Length is over the limit and counts the bytes of a chunked body. A limit set only in a reverse proxy (nginx `client_max_body_size`) covers only traffic that passes through it; if that is where yours lives, accept the finding under `exclude-rules` in `.agent-audit-kit.yml`.
rules.title: Unbounded prompt/argument size on MCP endpoint

rules.description: An MCP server configuration binds to plain HTTP without TLS. MCP spec 2025-11-25 requires Streamable HTTP over TLS for remote servers.
rules.limitations: Examines only files that contain `@tool`, createServer, McpServer, createMcpHandler, mcp.ServeHTTP, FastMCP or Server.run_streamable_http. In them it looks for a call to listen, bind or serve whose first argument is an `http://` URL that contains a digit or a dot. A server started the usual way, without a URL string (`uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=8080)`, `app.listen(8080)`), and the same call in a file that names none of those, are not matched.
rules.remediation: Bind only to HTTPS. Terminate TLS at a trusted proxy or use the server's native TLS support. Reject plain-HTTP binds in production mode.
rules.title: MCP server accepts HTTP (non-TLS) in production config

rules.description: An MCP server endpoint does not declare rate limiting. Unrestricted access allows credential stuffing and enumeration attacks.
rules.limitations: Fires on a file that names an MCP server class and contains the text `/mcp` but none of the words ratelimit, rate_limit, throttle or limiter. A server that never writes `/mcp` is not examined, and the word in a comment (`# TODO: add rate_limit middleware`) counts as rate limiting.
rules.remediation: Add per-IP and per-token rate limits to the server that declares the `/mcp` route, and answer bursts with 429. This check looks for `ratelimit`, `rate_limit`, `throttle` or `limiter` in the same file as the route, so a limit enforced only at a gateway or reverse proxy is not seen; in that case accept the finding under `exclude-rules` in `.agent-audit-kit.yml`.
rules.title: Missing rate limiting on MCP endpoint

rules.description: A Go MCP HTTP handler looks a resource up by something the caller sent (a path, query or form parameter), answers a miss with "not found" straight away, and checks the caller's credential only after that, answering 401 or 403. A caller with no credential tells the two answers apart and learns which resources exist, and the lookup runs for every caller.
rules.limitations: Reads Go handlers only (net/http, gin, echo); TypeScript, JavaScript and Python handlers are not read. It reports one form of the claim: a lookup on a receiver (`store.Get`, `db.QueryRow`, `repo.FindByID`) among the handler's own statements, whose argument is a path, query or form parameter the handler read from the request (seen in the argument's first 200 characters), answered "not found", with a `return`, by the `if` that holds it or the `if` on the next line, before one of the handler's top-level `if` statements calls a function named for authentication with the request and answers 401 or 403; the call may sit in an `if` nested inside it. Each `if` is read for its first 1,000 characters, so a not-found answer, a `return`, an auth call or a 401 or 403 further into one is not seen. Other work before the check (dispatching the MCP request, an outbound call, a write) is not reported, nor is a miss answered with another status, a key taken from the request body, a lookup inside a nested block or a helper, a gate that is not a top-level `if` (one inside a `for`, `switch` or plain `else` block, or in a helper), or a credential compared inline rather than through a function. An `if` counts only when its keyword starts the line that holds its `{` within 400 characters before it, and the `if` on the next line answers the miss only when the lookup starts within 200 characters of its line's start, only blanks follow it on its line and that line ends within 200 characters of its `)`, and the `if` starts within 200 characters after that line ends. The handler must be registered in the same file, on a route with no auth middleware or wrapper and no group or router-wide auth, so one registered in another file is not read, and the handler's name or body must mention MCP: `mcp` in any case, or `tools/call` or `tools/list` (a JSON-RPC handler that does neither is not read). A route's middleware and handler arguments are read for their first 200 characters; an inline handler that only calls a named handler is matched to it only when its `{` opens within 200 characters of its parameter list, while one that does the lookup itself is read wherever its `{` opens on its line; a Go group counts only when it is assigned (`g := r.Group(...)`) within 200 characters before the call, and files over 512,000 bytes are not read.
rules.remediation: Check the caller's credential before the handler looks up anything the request names. Where the credential to check depends on that resource (a per-adapter auth setting), answer an unknown name and a refused credential the same way, with one status and body, so the response does not reveal which names exist.
rules.title: MCP auth check runs after a resource lookup

rules.description: Two HTTP routes registered in the same Go or TypeScript/JavaScript file reach the same MCP handler, and only one of them applies authentication: an auth middleware on the route, or the handler wrapped in an auth function. The other route serves every tool the first one protects, with no credential. This is the CVE-2026-33032 bypass: nginx-ui's `/mcp_message` ran the same `mcp.ServeHTTP` as `/mcp`, behind an IP allowlist that was empty by default and nothing else.
rules.limitations: Reads gin, echo, chi and net/http routes in Go, and Express-style route calls (`app.post(path, ...middleware, handler)` and its `get`, `put`, `patch`, `delete` and `all` siblings, as Express, Hono and Koa Router write them) in TypeScript and JavaScript; Python servers are not read. Two routes are paired only when they sit in the same file and the same block, have different methods or paths, run the same handler value (or inline functions whose only statement is the same call handing on the request), and one path is an MCP endpoint (`/mcp`, `/api/v1/mcp`, `/mcp/message`) or an SSE or message path in a file that builds an MCP server. So routes registered in two files or two functions are not paired, a path held in a constant (`app.get(MCP_PATH, h)`) is not read, and inline handlers that do more than delegate are not compared. An unauthenticated route that carries a middleware the check cannot name (auth, a body parser, CORS, logging, rate limiting or an IP allowlist) is skipped, since that middleware may be the authentication, and auth on a whole router anywhere in the file (`app.use(auth)`, `r.Use(auth)`, a group made with auth, the mux handed to an auth wrapper) covers every route on it, whatever the registration order. Test files and mock servers are not read. A route AAK-MCPWN-001 reports is left to that rule, so a scan restricted to AAK-MCP-020 does not list it. Bounds that keep it linear: files over 512,000 bytes are not read; a middleware argument is read for its first 200 characters (an auth word further in is not seen), a handler argument longer than 200 characters that is not an inline function is not compared, and an inline function counts only when its `=>` or `{` comes within 200 characters of its parameter list; a Go group counts only when it is assigned (`g := r.Group(...)`) within 200 characters before the call; and in TypeScript and JavaScript a regex literal must close within 512 characters of its `/`, or it is read as division and a backtick in it can hide the routes after it.
rules.remediation: Put the authentication where no route can miss it: on the router or group every MCP route is registered on (`r.Use(AuthRequired())`, a gin group made with the middleware, `app.use("/mcp", requireAuth)`), or inside the shared handler. If another route has to stay open, such as a health check, give it a handler of its own that reaches no tool.
rules.title: MCP handler shares routing with an unauthenticated path

rules.description: `@1mcp/agent` (npm; 1mcp-app/agent) serves several MCP servers behind one endpoint and, with OAuth on, limits a token to the servers whose tags its `tag:<name>` scopes grant. 0.20.0 added the advanced `tag-filter` parameter, a boolean expression over tags, and the scope check validates only the tags the expression names. So a token granted one tag can send `not <granted-tag>`, which names only that tag, passes the check, and selects every other backend server, whose tools it can then list and call (CVE-2026-108586, CVSS 3.1 5.4, CWE-863). 0.19.0 has no `tag-filter`, and 0.39.0, the newest, still validates the tags extracted from the expression. There is no fixed release, so this pin reports every version from 0.20.0.
rules.limitations: Reports `@1mcp/agent` from 0.20.0 where a package.json, lockfile or MCP config states the version, and an unpinned reference such as `npx -y @1mcp/agent`, which resolves to an affected release. The bypass needs the HTTP transport with OAuth on; the pin reads versions, not how the agent is started, so a stdio-only setup is reported too. The unscoped npm `1mcp` is another project and is not matched, and the release binaries state no version AAK reads. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: There is no fixed release. Until one ships, do not rely on tag scopes to keep backends apart: run one 1MCP instance per trust boundary. Pin the first fixed release once it ships.
rules.title: 1MCP Agent from 0.20.0: a negated tag filter reaches servers outside an OAuth token's tag scopes (no fixed release)

rules.description: 9Router (`9router`) before 0.5.2 exposes MCP routes without authentication and reaches command execution: `src/proxy.js` did not protect `/api/cli-tools/*` and `/api/mcp/*`, allowing unauthenticated customPlugin registration and command execution through the MCP bridge (CVE-2026-46339, CVSS 10); the `isLocalRequest()` gate trusts spoofable Host/Origin headers (CVE-2026-49353); and unvalidated MCP plugin args reach `child_process.spawn()` for RCE via `/api/mcp//sse` (CVE-2026-62312). CVE-2026-63732 (CVSS 9.9) re-reports the same default-credential (`123456`) + spoofed-Host LOCAL_ONLY bypass + unvalidated `child_process.spawn()` plugin-registration chain on 0.4.59, also remediated by the 0.5.2 floor. Treat < 0.5.2 (and unpinned) as exposed.
rules.limitations: Reads `9router` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. rules.description: AgenticMail gives AI agents real email addresses. rules.description: Apache Answer, a self-hosted Q&A platform, serves MCP tools over SSE from 2.0.0, behind an API key and a site switch that a fresh install turns on. Its answer tool lists the answers to whatever question id it is given and checks only each answer's own status, not whether the question is public, so whoever holds a global API key reads answers to hidden, deleted and pending-review questions (CVE-2026-71563, CWE-862). Checked in the source: `internal/controller/mcp_controller.go` is absent at 1.7.1 and arrives in 2.0.0-RC1, and `MCPAnswersHandler` reads the same way through 2.0.2. 2.0.3 (63a67542, "fix: constrain MCP content access") returns nothing unless the question is shown and available or closed, and puts the same check on the question-detail and comment tools. MEDIUM follows the ASF's own rating, moderate; neither NVD nor the CVE record gives a CVSS score.
rules.limitations: Reads `apache/answer` tags from 2.0.0 below 2.0.3 in compose files, Kubernetes manifests, Helm values, Dockerfiles and MCP configs. A release candidate reads as its release, so 2.0.3-RC1, built from the 2.0.3 commit, is not reported. `latest` was a 2.0.3 build on 2026-10-19, fixed, and the compose file and Helm chart in Answer's repository use it, so an untagged or `latest` reference is not reported. It reads the version, not whether MCP is switched on or an API key exists. An install from the release binaries or the Go module is not read, nor is the `docker.io/apache/answer` spelling, and an MCP client config names the endpoint by URL, which states no version.
rules.remediation: Upgrade the `apache/answer` image to 2.0.3 or later and pin the tag. Until then, turn MCP off in the admin settings, or give a global API key only to someone who may read hidden, deleted and pending-review content.
rules.title: Apache Answer image 2.0.0 to 2.0.2: the MCP answer tool returns answers to hidden, deleted and pending questions

rules.description: Two defects in the Apify MCP server (`@apify/actors-mcp-server`), both of them a host check that trusts a string instead of a parsed origin. Before 0.9.21 the `fetch-apify-docs` allowlist is validated with `String.startsWith()` rather than hostname comparison, so attacker URLs such as `https://docs.apify.com.evil.com/` or `https://docs.apify.com@evil.com/` pass the `ALLOWED_DOC_DOMAINS` check and return arbitrary fetched content to the LLM (CVE-2026-46341, CVSS 6.1, SSRF). Before 0.10.11 `getActorMCPServerURL` in `src/mcp/actors.ts` concatenates the trusted Actor standby URL with the Actor-supplied `webServerMcpPath` without re-checking the resulting origin, so a userinfo-style authority (`@evil.host`) in a malicious Actor definition redirects `connectMCPClient` to a third-party host — and the `call-actor`, `fetch-actor-details` and `actor-mcp` paths hand that URL to transports in `src/mcp/client.ts` that attach the victim's `Authorization` bearer token, disclosing the Apify API token and with it access to Actors, stored datasets and billable compute (CVE-2026-50143, CVSS 8.1, CWE-918). Exploiting the second requires only that the victim invoke or inspect the attacker-published Actor. The floor is the later of the two: treat < 0.10.11 (and unpinned) as exposed.
rules.limitations: Reads `@apify/actors-mcp-server` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `@apify/actors-mcp-server` to >= 0.10.11 and pin it. Allow-list by parsed URL hostname (exact / suffix match), never `startsWith` on the raw URL, and re-parse any URL built from a partly-untrusted path before attaching credentials to it — comparing the parsed origin against the expected one is what catches a userinfo authority that string concatenation does not.
rules.title: Apify MCP host-validation defects: docs-allowlist SSRF and Actor path-authority token leak (`@apify/actors-mcp-server` < 0.10.11)

rules.description: An MCP Apps (SEP-1865) `text/html` UI resource is rendered in an `<iframe>` with no `sandbox` attribute, or with a self-defeating `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin"` (which lets the framed document script the host origin). MCP Apps UI is server-controlled, untrusted content running next to the user's agent session; without a restrictive sandbox it executes in the host context (XSS / token theft / tool invocation).
rules.limitations: Reads `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.html`, `.htm`, `.vue` and `.svelte` files that carry an MCP Apps marker (`ui://`, `@mcp-ui/`, `createUIResource` and similar). A sandbox value is judged where it is written as a literal: in an `<iframe>` tag, in `setAttribute("sandbox", ...)` or in `frame.sandbox = ...`. A value held in a variable, or added with `frame.sandbox.add(...)`, counts as a sandbox whatever it grants, and a sandbox set anywhere in a file counts for every iframe the file creates in script.
rules.remediation: Render MCP Apps UI in a sandboxed iframe. Set an explicit `sandbox` and do NOT combine `allow-scripts` with `allow-same-origin`; drive tool calls over `postMessage` with origin checks rather than granting host-origin access.
rules.title: MCP Apps UI iframe rendered without a hardening sandbox

rules.description: An MCP Apps (SEP-1865) UI writes content to the DOM through a raw-HTML sink (`innerHTML` / `outerHTML` / `insertAdjacentHTML` / React `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` / Vue `v-html` / Svelte `{@html}`) with no sanitizer (DOMPurify / `sanitize*` / escaping) in the file. Server- or tool-provided content reaching an unsanitized HTML sink is DOM XSS — the injected script runs in the app frame with access to its postMessage tool bridge.
rules.limitations: Looks for `innerHTML =`, `outerHTML =`, `insertAdjacentHTML(`, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `v-html` and `{@html`; jQuery's `.html(content)`, `document.write` and `iframe.srcdoc =` are not sinks here. Any mention of `sanitize`, `DOMPurify`, `escapeHtml`, `xss` or `purify` clears the whole file, an import that is never called included.
rules.remediation: Sanitize all server/tool-provided content before rendering (e.g. DOMPurify), or render as text. Never pass untrusted content to innerHTML / dangerouslySetInnerHTML / v-html without sanitization.
rules.title: MCP Apps UI content rendered without sanitization (DOM XSS)

rules.description: `argocd-mcp` (npm; argoproj-labs/mcp-for-argocd), the Argo CD MCP server, puts the `applicationName` tool argument into Argo CD API paths unencoded, and its HTTP client resolves each path against the base URL with `new URL`, which collapses dot segments. So a `delete_application` call whose name is `../repositories/<repo>` sends an authenticated `DELETE` to `/api/v1/repositories/<repo>`, and the same reaches clusters and projects, within the API token's RBAC. An agent that reads untrusted text can be steered into that call (CVE-2026-108585, CVSS 3.1 5.4, CWE-22). Every published version builds the path this way (0.0.1, the first, through 0.9.0, the newest), there is no commit after 0.9.0, and there is no fixed release, so this is a presence-only pin.
rules.limitations: Reports a reference that names `argocd-mcp`: a package.json or lockfile entry, or the package in an MCP config, such as the README's `npx argocd-mcp@latest stdio`. Presence-only: every version is reported, a future fixed one included, until the pin gets a floor, and `MCP_READ_ONLY` is not read. `argocd-mcp-server` and `mcp-argocd` are other projects and are not matched. The project's images (`ghcr.io/argoproj-labs/mcp-for-argocd`, `quay.io/argoprojlabs/mcp-for-argocd`) are not read. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: There is no fixed release. Set `MCP_READ_ONLY=true`, which turns off the tools that change or delete resources, or give the server an Argo CD token whose RBAC has no delete permission on repositories, clusters or projects. Pin the first fixed release once it ships.
rules.title: argocd-mcp builds Argo CD API paths from tool arguments, so delete_application can reach repositories and clusters (no fixed release)

rules.description: A command / argv buffer is approved against an allow/deny list and then reassigned, re-split (`shlex.split` / `.split()`), re-joined, concatenated, `.extend()`/`.push()`-ed, or otherwise rebuilt before it is passed to a process-spawn sink (`subprocess.run`/`Popen`/`call`, `os.exec*` / `os.system`; Node `child_process.spawn`/`exec`/`execFile`, `execa`) — with no re-validation between the mutation and the spawn. The executed command shape therefore differs from the one that was approved, so an attacker-controlled argv can pass the allowlist check and still reach the shell. Anchor: CVE-2026-53822 (CVSS 8.8) — OpenClaw before 2026.5.18 contained a command injection where the shell wrapper argv could change between approval and execution. CWE-77 (Command Injection) chained to CWE-367 (Time-of-check Time-of-use Race Condition). Detected as an ordered approve -> mutate -> exec data flow on the same command variable; distinct from `AAK-SSRF-TOCTOU-001` (a URL allow-list DNS-rebind TOCTOU, not command spawn).
rules.limitations: In Python a spawn is recognised by its spelling: `subprocess.run`, `call`, `Popen`, `check_call` or `check_output`, or `os.system`, `os.popen`, `os.exec*`, `os.spawnv`, `os.spawnl` or `os.spawnvp`. A function imported by name (`from subprocess import run`) or a module alias (`import subprocess as sp`) is missed. In TypeScript only the first argument of `spawn`, `exec`, `execFile`, `execa` or their Sync forms is followed, so an argv array passed second (`spawn(bin, args)`) and changed after the check is not.
rules.remediation: Validate the exact argv array that will be executed, and execute that same immutable buffer — never re-parse, re-split, re-join, or append to the command after the allowlist check. If a transform is unavoidable, re-run the allowlist/deny check on the final argv immediately before spawning, pass an explicit argv list (never a shell string) with `shell=False`, and freeze the approved value (e.g. a tuple) so it cannot be mutated. Pin OpenClaw >= 2026.5.18.
rules.title: Argv re-built after allowlist approval before spawn (command-injection TOCTOU)

rules.description: NVD records CVE-2026-27825 (CVSS 9.0, CWE-22 + CWE-73) as fixed in mcp-atlassian 0.17.0: `confluence_download_attachment` writes to a caller-supplied `download_path` with no directory boundary, and the caller also controls the content through a Confluence attachment, so writing a cron entry runs code with no restart. This rule reports a declared `mcp-atlassian` below 0.17.0. It also reports a related class in the user's own code, which is not the CVE's code path: a Jira/Confluence field (`issue.fields.*`, `issue.description`, `comment.body`, `page.content`) reaching `subprocess`, `os.system` or `os.popen` without validation, in a file that uses an Atlassian client, the shape the 2026-04-22 public reporting described.
rules.limitations: The pin reads requirements*.txt, pyproject.toml and Pipfile at the project root and judges only a version it can parse: an unpinned install and a lockfile's separate name and version lines are not reported. The source pattern is same-file co-occurrence of an Atlassian client, a Jira/Confluence field and a sink, not data flow, and it never reads mcp-atlassian's own code. The `ghcr.io/sooperset/mcp-atlassian` image is read at a version tag (a `docker run` argument in an MCP config, an `image:` value, a Dockerfile `FROM` or Helm values); an untagged, `latest` or digest reference is not reported. A Python file over 512 KB, a manifest over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read.
rules.remediation: Pin `mcp-atlassian>=0.17.0` (0.22.0 or later also clears the upload_attachment pin). For the source pattern, allow-list or `shlex.quote` every Jira/Confluence field before it reaches a subprocess, and pass argv lists rather than a shell string.

rules.description: NVD records CVE-2026-27826 (CVSS 8.2, CWE-918) as fixed in mcp-atlassian 0.17.0: with no Authorization header, two custom HTTP headers make the server send requests to any host, reaching cloud instance metadata and internal services. 'w')`, `Path.write_text`, `shutil.move/copy`) without validation, in a file that uses an Atlassian client, so whoever writes the field chooses what lands on disk.

rules.description: MCP Atlassian (`mcp-atlassian`), an MCP server for Confluence and Jira, before 0.22.0 passes the client-supplied `file_path` argument of `confluence_upload_attachment` straight to `open(file_path, "rb")` inside `_upload_attachment_direct()` in `src/mcp_atlassian/confluence/attachments.py`, without routing it through `validate_safe_path`. An authenticated MCP client can therefore read any file the server process can reach and exfiltrate it to Confluence as an attachment. Because the tool is agent-callable, untrusted content that induces an agent to call it reaches the same primitive, disclosing server environment material such as `CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN` and other credentials (CVE-2026-73498, CVSS 7.7). Fixed in 0.22.0.
rules.limitations: Two arms. The pin reads `mcp-atlassian` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version; it is not read when declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in `pdm.lock`. The `ghcr.io/sooperset/mcp-atlassian` image is read at a version tag (a `docker run` argument in an MCP config, an `image:` value, a Dockerfile `FROM` or Helm values); an untagged, `latest` or digest reference is not reported. The source arm reads Python files that define a `confluence_upload_attachment` or `_upload_attachment_direct` handler and open `file_path`, `filepath`, `attachment_path` or `path` in `rb` mode with no path-validation call, so a copy that opens the path under another name (`abs_path = os.path.abspath(file_path)`, then `open(abs_path, "rb")`) is not reported. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A Python file over 512 KB is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `mcp-atlassian` to >= 0.22.0 and pin it. If you vendor or reimplement the attachment path, validate the caller-supplied path against an allowed root before opening it (the fix's `validate_safe_path`), and treat any tool argument that reaches `open()` as untrusted.
rules.title: mcp-atlassian < 0.22.0 (confluence_upload_attachment arbitrary file read)

rules.description: `atomic-agents-stack` before 1.1.0 accepts cleartext `http://` schemes in the HTTP MCP server-registry backend factory. A network attacker in the path rewrites the catalog response and injects arbitrary `command` and argument values, which `MCPClientPool` then spawns as local subprocesses — so a transport weakness becomes code execution on the agent host without any parsing bug in between (CVE-2026-91988, CVSS 8.1, CWE-319). The same distribution appears in this project's 2026-08-16 ledger section for an unrelated dashboard path traversal that never received a CVE id; this is a different defect in the same package. Fixed in 1.1.0.
rules.limitations: Reads `atomic-agents-stack` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock and uv.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`) or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `atomic-agents-stack` to >= 1.1.0 and pin it. Require `https://` for any registry or catalog the agent reads, and treat a catalog entry as untrusted input even over TLS: allowlist the commands a pool may spawn rather than executing whatever the catalog names.
rules.title: atomic-agents-stack < 1.1.0 (cleartext registry catalog reaches a local subprocess)

rules.description: An MCP server entry in the agent/host config is dispatched without any of: a referenced signed clearance assertion, a `/.well-known/mcp-clearance` (or configured) URI, or a pinned trust root. Deny-by-default server admission is unenforced, so the server's self-declared tool list is implicitly trusted at dispatch time.
rules.limitations: Fires on an entry of `mcpServers` (or `servers` in VS Code's `.vscode/mcp.json`) with a `command` or `url` that has none of 13 attestation keys (`attestation`, `clearance`, `clearance_url`, `clearance_uri`, `clearance_document`, `clearancedocument`, `mcp_clearance`, `wellknown_clearance`, `well_known_clearance`, `trust_root`, `trustroot`, `trust_anchor`, `pinned_trust_root`; any case, `-` for `_`) and no header named like `MCP-Clearance` or `MCP-Attestation`. A key only has to exist: `"attestation": ""` satisfies it, a top-level `trust_root` key silences every server in the file, and so does the text `.well-known/mcp-clearance` anywhere in the file; no clearance document or trust root is ever checked.
rules.remediation: Add an `attestation` (or `clearance`) field on the server entry pointing to a signed clearance document, expose it at `/.well-known/mcp-clearance`, and pin a `trust_root` in the host config that the host verifies before any tool dispatch. See Metere 2026, arXiv:2605.24248 — wire format, verification algorithm, and RFC-2119 conformance vectors.
rules.title: MCP server admitted without attestation

rules.description: MCP server authentication code concatenates or `os.path.join`-es an untrusted token / bearer credential into a filesystem path that is then used for a session existence / read check, without rejecting path separators / `..` or resolving-and-containing the result. Because the caller controls the token, they control the path: a value like `../../etc/passwd` or `../<another-user-session>` escapes the intended session directory, turning an auth check into arbitrary-file access and cross-session takeover. Anchor: CVE-2026-52830 (CVSS 9.4, CWE-22 Path Traversal) — `fast-mcp-telegram` before 0.19.1 joined the caller-supplied bearer token straight into the session file path used to test whether a session existed, so a crafted token traversed out of the session directory; fixed in 0.19.1. The Python detector is a stdlib-`ast` taint flow (token source -> path construction -> `exists`/`open` sink, suppressed by a separator/`..` reject or a resolve-and-contain guard); TS/JS/Rust use the analogous concat-into-path regex. Distinct from `AAK-MCP-015` (a resource-handler path traversal on a request *path* parameter) — here the tainted source is the auth *token* itself.
rules.limitations: In Python it treats any of `secure_filename`, `is_relative_to`, `relative_to`, `normpath`, `realpath`, `abspath`, `os.sep`, `sep`, `commonpath`, `commonprefix`, `..`, `startswith`, `resolve(` or a `split("/"` (any case, so `startsWith` counts) in the same function as a guard against traversal; in TypeScript, JavaScript and Rust files it is anywhere in the file. The `startswith("Bearer ")` that extracts the token is enough to silence it, though it checks nothing about the path.
rules.remediation: Reject path separators and `..` in the token before it touches the filesystem; resolve the constructed session path (`os.path.realpath` / `Path.resolve()`) and verify it is inside the intended session directory (`startswith` / `Path.is_relative_to`) before use; prefer a hashed / opaque session id over the raw token as a filename. Upgrade `fast-mcp-telegram` to >= 0.19.1.
rules.title: MCP bearer-token joined into a session file path (path traversal)

rules.description: `auth-fetch-mcp`, an MCP server that fetches authenticated web pages for assistants, blocks private and loopback destinations in `assertSafeUrl()` (`src/security.ts`), but its `isPrivateV6()` check misses IPv4-mapped IPv6 loopback addresses in hex-normalised form. A URL such as `http://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]:PORT/` is silently normalised by the Node WHATWG URL parser to `[::ffff:7f00:1]`; because `net.isIPv4('7f00:1')` is false, the private-address check does not fire and the URL reaches the browser or HTTP client, so an MCP tool call reaches loopback services the guard exists to protect. Exploitable under the default configuration with no special environment variable (CVE-2026-49857, CVSS 7.4). GHSA-pvrj-8cg3-j5f8 records the affected range as <= 3.0.1 with 3.0.2 the first patched release — note the NVD text's claim that 3.0.1 patches the issue is contradicted by the advisory's own version data.
rules.limitations: Reads `auth-fetch-mcp` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `auth-fetch-mcp` to >= 3.0.2 and pin it. When validating a destination, resolve the host and test the resulting address, rather than pattern-matching the textual form: normalise IPv4-mapped IPv6 (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`, including its hex form) to IPv4 before the private-range check, and re-check after any redirect.
rules.title: auth-fetch-mcp <= 3.0.1 (IPv4-mapped IPv6 loopback bypasses the SSRF guard)

rules.description: The AWS API MCP Server (`awslabs.aws-api-mcp-server`) added OAuth authentication in 1.3.0 (`AUTH_TYPE=oauth`, which the README says is on by default in HTTP mode unless `AUTH_TYPE=no-auth` is set). Before 1.6.0 it did not check a token's audience, so a local user holding an access token that the same identity provider issued to another application could call the server and run AWS operations with the server's configured AWS credentials (CVE-2026-115413, CVSS 7.8, CWE-346; GHSA-4prq-p2x5-w9fh). 1.6.0 adds `AUTH_AUDIENCE` and `AUTH_CLIENT_ID`, matched against the token's `aud` and `client_id` or `azp` claims, and requires one of them in OAuth mode (awslabs/mcp#4865).
rules.limitations: Reports `awslabs.aws-api-mcp-server` from 1.3.0 below 1.6.0 where a version is stated: a requirements*.txt entry at any depth, a pyproject.toml, Pipfile or lockfile entry at the project root, or a `uvx` launch in .mcp.json, mcp.json or claude_desktop_config.json, reporting a range that admits an affected version. `latest` was 1.6.0 on 2026-10-28 and states no version, so the README's own `uvx awslabs.aws-api-mcp-server@latest` is not reported. It reads the version, not the transport or `AUTH_TYPE`, so a server run over stdio, which has no OAuth mode, or with `AUTH_TYPE=no-auth` is reported too. The ECR image `public.ecr.aws/awslabs-mcp/awslabs/aws-api-mcp-server`, which the README runs at `latest`, is not read. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `awslabs.aws-api-mcp-server` to 1.6.0 or later and pin it, then set `AUTH_AUDIENCE` to the server's own audience, or `AUTH_CLIENT_ID` for a provider whose access tokens carry no `aud` claim, such as Amazon Cognito. Until then, run it over stdio, or keep its HTTP port to the one client that should reach it.
rules.title: AWS API MCP Server 1.3.0 to 1.5.x: OAuth mode accepts tokens issued to other applications

rules.description: The AWS API MCP Server (`awslabs.aws-api-mcp-server`) from 0.2.13 through 1.3.46 improperly handles a startup initialization failure: when the security policy enforcement data fails to initialize, the policy check is skipped for the entire lifetime of the process, so an actor can execute AWS API operations the user-configured policy was set to deny or gate. The IAM permissions on the configured credentials still apply, but the extra deny/gate layer the operator relied on is silently absent (CVE-2026-16584, CVSS 7.0). Fixed in 1.3.47; treat 0.2.13–1.3.46 (and unpinned) as exposed.
rules.limitations: Reads `awslabs.aws-api-mcp-server` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, reporting a range that admits an affected version and a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `awslabs.aws-api-mcp-server` to >= 1.3.47 and pin it. Fail the server closed when security-policy initialization fails rather than continuing with policy enforcement disabled, and scope the configured IAM credentials to the minimum operations required.
rules.title: AWS API MCP Server security-policy bypass on init failure (0.2.13–<1.3.47)

rules.description: Amazon awslabs postgres-mcp-server (`awslabs.postgres-mcp-server`, PyPI) before 1.1.7 carries two defects in the same SQL validation component, both cleared by one floor. CVE-2026-87911 (CRITICAL 9.6): the read-only enforcement does not stop a crafted `COPY ... TO PROGRAM` statement, so an unauthenticated actor who can place content that an authenticated user later processes executes operating-system commands on the host of a self-managed PostgreSQL server, in the server's default configuration. CVE-2026-85787 (MEDIUM 6.5): the disallowed-input list is incomplete, so crafted SQL reaching the same path modifies data beyond the server's read-only scope. The command-injection reading is the load-bearing one — a read-only *scope* bypass and OS command execution are different threats, and the remediation below addresses the latter. Fixed in 1.1.7; treat < 1.1.7 (and unpinned) as exposed.
rules.limitations: Reads `awslabs.postgres-mcp-server` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `awslabs.postgres-mcp-server` to >= 1.1.7 and pin it. Enforce read-only access with a least-privilege database role rather than relying on the server's own statement filtering: a role without `pg_execute_server_program` cannot run `COPY ... TO PROGRAM` even if the statement filter is bypassed.
rules.title: awslabs postgres-mcp-server: COPY TO PROGRAM command injection and SQL validation gap (< 1.1.7)

rules.description: AWS Security Agent MCP server (`awslabs.security-agent-mcp-server`, PyPI) before 0.2.0 does not verify that the S3 bucket it writes scan output to is owned by the caller's own account (CVE-2026-87913, MEDIUM 5.9). The bucket name is derived from a publicly known account identifier, so a third party who pre-registers that name receives the private source archive of every scanned workspace — including any credentials and infrastructure state the archive contains. Fixed in 0.2.0; treat < 0.2.0 (and unpinned) as exposed.
