A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `flyto-core` to >= 2.26.6 and pin it. Restrict `llm.chat` `base_url` to an allow-list of trusted provider hosts, and never forward environment-sourced provider keys to a caller-supplied endpoint. Until the upgrade, do not expose the HTTP API, whose `/mcp` route runs modules without authentication from 2.26.2 to 2.26.3, beyond localhost.
rules.title: Flyto2 Core forwards provider API keys to a caller-controlled base_url, and its HTTP MCP route runs modules unauthenticated (<2.26.6)

rules.description: `mcp-from-openapi` (npm; agentfront/mcp-from-openapi) builds MCP tools from an OpenAPI spec it fetches with `fromURL()`. Two flaws are fixed in 2.9.0. CVE-2026-115750 (2.5.0 to 2.8.x): `safeFetch()` carries the caller's `Authorization` and `Cookie` headers to another origin when the spec host redirects there, so a spec host or an open redirect can send the request to an attacker's origin and collect bearer tokens or cookies. CVE-2026-115751 (2.2.0 to 2.8.x): a hostname with a trailing dot (`blocked.example.invalid.`) is not matched against `ssrf.blockedHosts`, so a spec URL or redirect target reaches a host the operator blocked (CVSS 3.1 3.7 each, CWE-522/CWE-184, GHSA-ff5q-5r4v-fw4v). 2.9.0 keeps caller headers on their origin and normalizes hostnames before every host-list check.
rules.limitations: Reports `mcp-from-openapi` from 2.2.0 below 2.9.0 where a package.json, lockfile or MCP config states the version, reporting a range that admits an affected version. 2.2.0 to 2.4.x carry only CVE-2026-115751: `safeFetch()`, and with it the redirect leak, first ships in 2.5.0. `latest` was 2.9.1 on 2026-10-24 and states no version, so an unversioned reference is not reported. Releases below 2.5.0 also fire `AAK-MCP-FROMOPENAPI-CVE-2026-59973-001`. PyPI's `mcp-from-openapi` is another project and is not read. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `mcp-from-openapi` to 2.9.0 or later and pin it. Until then pass no credentials to spec fetches from hosts you do not control, and list the trailing-dot form of each blocked host in `ssrf.blockedHosts` as well.
rules.title: mcp-from-openapi from 2.2.0 below 2.9.0: spec credentials follow a cross-origin redirect, and a trailing dot slips past blockedHosts

rules.description: `mcp-from-openapi` (npm) from 2.3.0 until 2.5.0 forwards untrusted OpenAPI `url` and `spec` inputs, and `loadOptions.refResolution`, from `loadOPENAPISpec()` in `libs/adapters/src/openapi/openapi.adapter.ts` into `OpenAPIToolGenerator.fromURL()` and `.fromJSON()`. The external `$ref` guard compares parsed hostname strings without resolving addresses, pinning the validated address, revalidating redirect targets, or normalizing IPv4-mapped IPv6 forms. An authenticated user who can import or configure an OpenAPI specification in a hosted or multi-user deployment therefore causes backend-origin requests to internal services via DNS-to-loopback resolution, redirect-to-loopback behaviour, or `::ffff:` loopback forms, exposing internal administrative APIs, metadata-like services and other private endpoints (CVE-2026-59973, CVSS 8.5, CWE-918). The same defect ships in `frontmcp` and `@frontmcp/adapters` on their own 1.x line, where that package's existing 1.5.7 pin floor already covers the 1.5.0 fix; this rule exists because `mcp-from-openapi` runs a 2.x line that floor cannot express. Impact is lower where only a trusted local administrator can configure specs, and disabling external reference protocols prevents the request outright.
rules.limitations: Reads `mcp-from-openapi` in package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles at the project root only, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`) or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `mcp-from-openapi` to >= 2.5.0 and pin it (the sibling `frontmcp` and `@frontmcp/adapters` packages to >= 1.5.0). Disable external `$ref` resolution unless you need it. Where you must resolve remote references, resolve the hostname, reject private, loopback, link-local and IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses, pin the validated address for the connection, and revalidate every redirect target rather than trusting the first hop.
rules.title: mcp-from-openapi < 2.5.0 (external $ref guard does not resolve or pin addresses — SSRF)

rules.description: `frontmcp` before 1.5.7 exposes live host Zod schema instances to the sandboxed `codecall:execute` tool through `getTool()`; because Zod v4's `_zod` is a non-configurable, non-writable own property, the Proxy invariants force the security membrane to return the raw host object, letting a script reach `_zod.constr.constructor` (the host Function constructor) and run arbitrary code as the server user. One `tools/call` is sufficient, and the framework's default public auth mode serves it to unauthenticated callers (CVE-2026-67531). A pinnable npm artifact (latest 1.6.0) the pin scanner resolves from `package.json` / lockfiles / `.mcp.json`.
rules.limitations: Reads `frontmcp` and `@frontmcp/adapters` in package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles at the project root only, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`) or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `frontmcp` to >= 1.5.7 and pin it. Do not run the code-execution tool in public auth mode; require authentication and treat tool output / fetched content as untrusted so an indirect prompt injection cannot trigger it.
rules.title: FrontMCP sandbox escape via Zod schema proxy reaches RCE (< 1.5.7)

rules.description: The Amazon `mcp-gateway-registry` before 1.0.13 improperly neutralizes a caller-supplied `table_name` in the metrics-service retention-policy component: the value is interpolated directly into an SQL statement in identifier position, so an authenticated remote user can execute arbitrary SQL against the gateway's metrics store (CVE-2026-14471, HIGH CVSS 8.1, CWE-89, published 2026-07-06). A project that depends on the gateway registry at a version below 1.0.13 (or unpinned) is exposed.
rules.limitations: Reads the dependency declarations and launchers of the project root's requirements*.txt, pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and *.mcp.yaml/.yml files, and reports one whose range admits a release below 1.0.13 or that states no version (a git requirement's dotted release tag is its version; a commit, a branch or a tag with no dot, `@v2`, states none), every `agentic-community/mcp-gateway-registry` git or image reference whose tag is below 1.0.13 or missing, a command line that runs `mcp-gateway-registry` without fetching it, and the version the root Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock or package-lock.json resolves when it is below 1.0.13. A mention of the name that is none of these, such as a server's name or a URL, is not read, and neither is an image published under another name, such as the project's own `public.ecr.aws/p3v1o3c6/registry`. It does not read a sub-directory, including a requirements file there, `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or a `pdm.lock`, `yarn.lock` or `pnpm-lock.yaml`. A file over 2 MB is not read. A lockfile over 32 MiB is not read.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `mcp-gateway-registry` to >= 1.0.13 and pin it explicitly. Never interpolate a request-supplied value into an SQL identifier position; validate `table_name` against a fixed allow-list of known table names, or quote it with the driver's identifier-quoting API rather than string formatting.
rules.title: Amazon mcp-gateway-registry < 1.0.13 (SQL injection)

rules.description: genieacs-mcp before 0.3.2 starts an unauthenticated Streamable-HTTP `/mcp` listener (`cmd/server/main.go`) on the default `MCP_LISTEN_ADDR` of `127.0.0.1:8080` whenever `MCP_AUTH_TOKEN` is unset, and the `httpSrv.Start(addr)` path validates neither `Host` nor `Origin` (CVE-2026-55637). Binding to loopback is not the boundary it looks like: a malicious website resolves its own name to 127.0.0.1 and the browser sends same-origin-looking requests to the local server, so DNS rebinding reaches the tool surface of a TR-069 ACS bridge. rules.description: `@zereight/mcp-gitlab` (npm), an MCP server for GitLab, carries three disclosures that share one pin at the highest fix floor. Before 2.1.27, SSE transport mode (`SSE=true`) exposes every MCP tool with no authentication, and the `upload_markdown` tool reads arbitrary files from the server's filesystem through an unsanitised `file_path` parameter and uploads them to a GitLab project; together an unauthenticated network-reachable caller reads `/proc/self/environ`, recovers `GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN` and takes over the GitLab account. That is the default configuration for Docker deployments (CVE-2026-61560, CVSS 9.8, CWE-22). Also before 2.1.27, setting `ENABLE_DYNAMIC_API_URL=true` makes the server read the `X-GitLab-API-URL` request header and use it as the base URL for outbound GitLab API calls, validating only that it parses as a URL, with no allowlist or hostname restriction, while still attaching the victim's `Private-Token` to every such request — so any caller who reaches the transport receives the token at a host of their choosing (CVE-2026-61559, CVSS 9.6, CWE-918). Before 2.1.30, the Streamable HTTP endpoint has no effective Host or Origin allowlist, so a malicious web page uses DNS rebinding to route a browser's requests to a victim's local MCP listener while preserving an attacker-controlled `Host` and `Origin`, and the server reaches MCP initialization instead of rejecting the request at the HTTP boundary (CVE-2026-61568, CVSS 9.6, CWE-350). 2.1.30 is the highest of the three fix versions and is the floor this rule pins.
rules.limitations: Reads `@zereight/mcp-gitlab` in package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles at the project root only, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `@zereight/mcp-gitlab` to >= 2.1.30 and pin it — 2.1.27 closes the unauthenticated-SSE and dynamic-API-URL paths but not the DNS-rebinding one. Do not run the SSE transport on a reachable interface without an inbound credential, leave `ENABLE_DYNAMIC_API_URL` unset unless you allowlist the hostnames it may resolve to, and treat any `GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN` exposed to an affected deployment as compromised: rotate it rather than relying on the upgrade alone.
rules.title: @zereight/mcp-gitlab < 2.1.30 (unauthenticated SSE + arbitrary file read, header-controlled API base, DNS rebinding)

rules.description: `mcp-grafana` before 1.1.0 lets a caller-supplied `X-Grafana-URL` request header control the destination of the server's outbound requests, and the `grafana_api_request` tool lets the caller also choose the HTTP method, path, and body. Because the destination is not restricted to the configured Grafana instance, a caller can point requests at internal, loopback, and link-local services (including cloud metadata endpoints) and read the responses: server-side request forgery (CVE-2026-19516, CVSS 9.1). This is the incomplete-fix follow-up to CVE-2026-15583, whose fix stopped the configured service-account token from being sent to unintended destinations but did not restrict the destinations themselves, so the correct control is destination restriction, not token handling. mcp-grafana is a Go server but ships a resolvable PyPI wrapper (`uvx mcp-grafana`), so the pin scanner resolves it from `.mcp.json` / `requirements.txt` / `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock`; the archived ledger note that it was unpinnable is now superseded. Fixed in 1.1.0, which restricts the destination to the configured instance.
rules.limitations: Reads `mcp-grafana` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. rules.remediation: Upgrade `mcp-grafana` to >= 1.1.0, which restricts outbound requests to the configured Grafana instance. Do not let a caller-controlled `X-Grafana-URL` header choose the destination, and do not expose `grafana_api_request` to untrusted callers.
rules.title: Grafana mcp-grafana SSRF via caller-controlled X-Grafana-URL destination (< 1.1.0)

rules.description: The AWS HealthOmics MCP server (`awslabs.aws-healthomics-mcp-server`) before 0.0.36 improperly limits pathnames in its linting tools, so an actor who can influence the MCP agent can write actor-controlled content outside the intended workflow-bundle directory via directory-traversal sequences in the `workflow_files` input (CVE-2026-15415, CVSS 5.5, CWE-22). Treat < 0.0.36 (and unpinned) as exposed.
rules.limitations: Reads `awslabs.aws-healthomics-mcp-server` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `awslabs.aws-healthomics-mcp-server` to >= 0.0.36 and pin it. Resolve and contain every `workflow_files` path under the bundle root before writing.
rules.title: AWS HealthOmics MCP workflow-bundle path traversal (< 0.0.36)

rules.description: heym, a self-hosted workflow platform with MCP nodes, is on neither PyPI nor npm and ships as the container image `ghcr.io/heymrun/heym`. Before 0.0.109 its Slack, Discord and Crawler workflow nodes send HTTP requests to URLs taken from user-created credentials (`webhook_url`, `flaresolverr_url`) through an HTTP client without the SSRF egress guard that already covers the HTTP, WebSocket and MCP nodes, and the credential API checks only that the URL is non-empty. Any registered user can point a credential at a loopback, private, link-local or cloud-metadata address and run a workflow (CVE-2026-100858, CVSS 3.1 6.8, CWE-918, GHSA-39j3-6x3x-8rcr).
rules.limitations: Reads image references only: an `image:` value or any other mention of `REPO:TAG` in YAML (compose files, Kubernetes manifests, MCP configs), a Helm values mapping of `repository` (or `registry` + `repository`) and `tag`, Dockerfile and Containerfile `FROM`, and `docker run` arguments in `*mcp*.json` and `claude_desktop_config.json`. A tag that is not a version (`main`, `main-20250617`, `dev`), a digest with no tag, an interpolated tag (`:${VERSION}`, `{{ .Values.tag }}`) and a Helm `tag` left empty (the chart's appVersion decides) state no version and are not reported. A two-part tag such as `0.24` stands for the newest patch on that line and is reported only when the whole line sits below the fixed version. Mirrors under another registry are not matched, and commented-out lines are skipped. `latest` (or no tag) is not reported: it was 0.0.123 on 2026-10-03. heym's own compose file builds a local image (`heym-backend:local` unless `HEYM_BACKEND_IMAGE` is set), which states no version.
rules.remediation: Run `ghcr.io/heymrun/heym` at 0.0.109 or later and pin that tag (or its digest). Until then, run the backend where internal and cloud-metadata addresses are unreachable.
rules.title: heym image below 0.0.109 fetches workflow-node URLs past its SSRF guard

rules.description: A repository publishes an MCP server over HTTP / SSE / Streamable-HTTP (an `/mcp` route handler, or an `SSEServerTransport` / `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` / `--http` setup) with no inbound authentication marker on the handler, while also binding to all interfaces (`0.0.0.0` / `::`) or serving a wildcard `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. The result is a mutation-capable RPC endpoint, backed by the operator's own tokens, reachable without credentials by any network (or, with wildcard CORS, any cross-origin browser) peer. This is a recurring 2026 class: GitLab MCP Server (CVE-2026-44895), Nocturne Memory (CVE-2026-44830), and AgenticMail (CVE-2026-50287) all shipped auth-less HTTP/SSE MCP transports on `0.0.0.0` with wildcard CORS. Generalises the Azure-only `AAK-AZURE-MCP-NOAUTH-001` to any published MCP HTTP server (the Azure rule still owns Azure-MCP repos; this rule defers to it there). Beyond server source, this also flags the launch surface: MCP config files (`mcp.json`, `claude_desktop_config.json`, `*.mcp.yaml` `command`/`args`), Docker `--host 0.0.0.0` / `-p 0.0.0.0:` publishes, and MCP Inspector / FastMCP startup args that bind a non-loopback interface (`0.0.0.0` / `::` / a routable IP) with no token / `requireAuth`, or with the Inspector kill-switch `DANGEROUSLY_OMIT_AUTH` set. CVE-2026-23744 (MCP Inspector, CVSS 9.8) is the motivating exemplar of the launch-bind variant; Censys counted ~12,520 MCP services exposed on the public internet in this shape. Two further 2026 instances of this exact class: CVE-2026-49257 (mcp-pinot <= 3.0.1, CVSS 10.0) defaults to an HTTP MCP server bound to `0.0.0.0:8080` with no authentication, exposing SQL execution as a confused deputy; CVE-2026-48989 (Windows-MCP < 0.7.5, CVSS 8.9) exposed the MCP control plane over HTTP without auth while enabling wildcard CORS. CWE-306 (Missing Authentication for Critical Function).
rules.limitations: Source files are checked for a literal `0.0.0.0` or `::` bind or a wildcard CORS setting, so a Node server that calls `listen(3000)` with no host, which binds every interface, is not treated as exposed. In compose, Dockerfile and JSON or YAML launch files, any `api_key`, `bearer`, `Authorization` or `--token` text counts as inbound authentication, including the server's own outbound `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
rules.remediation: Require an inbound credential on every `/mcp` route / SSE handler (bearer/JWT/mTLS/API-key middleware) and fail closed when the credential is unset — never bypass auth when an `API_TOKEN` env var is empty. Bind the listener to `127.0.0.1` (or behind an authenticating reverse proxy) instead of `0.0.0.0`, never pass `--host 0.0.0.0` to the MCP Inspector / FastMCP without a token, never set `DANGEROUSLY_OMIT_AUTH`, and replace wildcard CORS with an explicit origin allowlist (see AAK's wildcard-CORS rule).
rules.title: Published MCP HTTP/SSE server exposes an unauthenticated network-bound endpoint

rules.description: CVE-2026-23744 (CVSS 9.8): MCPJam Inspector (`@mcpjam/inspector`) 1.4.2 and earlier listens on 0.0.0.0, and a crafted HTTP request makes it install and run an MCP server, so anyone who can reach the port runs code. The preset-only entry from v0.3.5 caught configured presence; this rule catches a copy of the package in the tree, installed under `node_modules/@mcpjam/inspector/` or vendored in a `*mcpjam-inspector*` directory, and judges it by the version its own package.json states. It also reports the `inspectorServer.handle(...)` call shape anywhere else.
rules.limitations: Reports a copy of the package, a `node_modules/@mcpjam/inspector/` directory or one whose name contains `mcpjam-inspector` holding .ts, .tsx, .js, .mjs or .cjs files, once per copy, unless the copy's package.json names `@mcpjam/inspector` at 1.4.3 or later. A copy with no such package.json (a fork renamed to its own numbering, or none at all) is reported at any version. Outside a copy, a file is reported only when it calls `inspectorServer.handle(`, which the published package does not contain. It never reads a dependency declaration, a lockfile or an `npx` launcher, so `@mcpjam/inspector` 1.4.2 declared as a dependency, the case the remediation tells you to bump, is not reported when the code is not in the scanned tree. A TS/JS file over 512 KB is not read.
rules.remediation: Bump `@mcpjam/inspector` to >= 1.4.3 in package.json AND remove any vendored copies. Do not patch in-tree — rebase onto the published patched release.
rules.title: Vendored mcpjam-inspector fork carries CVE-2026-23744

rules.description: The MCP Java SDK's Servlet-based server transports (`HttpServletSseServerTransportProvider`, `HttpServletStreamableServerTransportProvider` and `HttpServletStatelessServerTransport`) read a POST body line by line into a `StringBuilder` with no size limit. An unauthenticated client that can reach one can stream an arbitrarily large body, chunked or not, until the JVM runs out of heap (CVE-2026-108395, CVSS 3.1 7.5, CWE-770). The transports are in `io.modelcontextprotocol.sdk:mcp` from 0.8.0 to 0.12.1 and in `mcp-core` from 0.13.0, and the `mcp` bundle depends on `mcp-core` at its own version. Checked in the source: the SSE provider reads without a limit from 0.8.0, where it arrives, and all three do at 0.12.1, 0.13.0, 0.18.3, 1.0.0-RC3, 1.0.2, 1.1.3, 2.0.0-M1, 2.0.0-RC1 and 2.0.0. 0.18.4, 1.1.4 and 2.0.1 read through a bounded `readBody`, and the 1.0.x line has no fixed release.
rules.limitations: Dependency-level detection on JVM manifests only: `build.gradle`, `build.gradle.kts`, `gradle/libs.versions.toml` and `pom.xml`. Reports `io.modelcontextprotocol.sdk:mcp` and `mcp-core` from 0.8.0 below 0.18.4, from 1.0.0 below 1.1.4, and at 2.0.0, where a version resolves in the file, directly or through an `mcp-bom` in the same file. 1.0.0-RC3 reads as 1.0.0 and the 2.0.0 milestones as 2.0.0, and both are affected. It reads versions, not code, so a server that uses only stdio, or has a body-size limit in front of it, is reported too. The SDK that Spring AI's starters or `spring-ai-bom` pull in is not read, and neither is a dynamic version or a `version.ref` to a catalog outside the scanned tree. 0.7.0's older `HttpServletSseServerTransport` reads the body the same way, but the CVE record starts at 0.8.0, so 0.7.0 is not reported.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `mcp` or `mcp-core`, or the `mcp-bom` that sets their version, to 0.18.4, 1.1.4 or 2.0.1 or later on your release line, or to 2.1.0, the newest. On 1.0.x, move to 1.1.4. Until then, put a reverse proxy or gateway that limits the request body size in front of the server.
rules.title: MCP Java SDK 0.8.0 to 0.18.3, 1.0.0 to 1.1.3 and 2.0.0: the Servlet HTTP server transports read request bodies of any size

rules.description: `@jshookmcp/jshook`, an MCP server exposing JavaScript-analysis and security-research tools to agents, at 0.3.1 enforces its central SSRF authorization policy — which blocks private, loopback, link-local and reserved targets unless an authorization object explicitly permits private network access — only on the raw HTTP / TCP / TLS round-trip tools. The ICMP probe and traceroute tools resolve the caller's target and invoke the native ICMP / traceroute sink directly, skipping the policy. An MCP client holding an active network domain can therefore probe internal addresses even with local SSRF access disabled for every other raw network tool, yielding an internal reachability and route-mapping primitive from the server's network position (CVE-2026-49856, CVSS 4.3). Fixed in 0.3.2; GHSA-c5r6-m4mr-8q5j records 0.3.1 as the only affected release.
rules.limitations: Reads `@jshookmcp/jshook` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `@jshookmcp/jshook` to >= 0.3.2 and pin it. Route every network tool, including ICMP and traceroute, through the same SSRF authorization policy rather than gating only the raw HTTP/TCP/TLS paths.
rules.title: @jshookmcp/jshook 0.3.1 (ICMP/traceroute tools bypass the SSRF authorization policy)

rules.description: Junie CLI is JetBrains' coding agent for the terminal, published on npm as `@jetbrains/junie` and earlier as `@jetbrains/junie-cli`. It reads MCP servers from the project's `.junie/mcp/mcp.json` as well as from the user's own configuration. Before 26.8.3, an untrusted project's MCP server configuration could run code on the machine of a user who started Junie in it (CVE-2026-111091, CVSS 3.1 7.8, CWE-829). The npm package is a launcher that installs the Junie build named in its `junieVersion` field, and its version is that build number: 26.8.3 is build 2548.5, published to npm as 2548.5.0 on 2026-08-03. Checked in the builds: 888.112, the oldest `@jetbrains/junie` release, and 2470.4, the last npm release before the fix, read the project's `.junie/mcp/mcp.json`, and 2548.5 adds a trust prompt that previews the project's MCP servers.
rules.limitations: Reports `@jetbrains/junie` and `@jetbrains/junie-cli` from 888.0.0 up to 2548.5.0 where a project states the version in a package.json or lockfile entry. An unpinned reference resolves to the newest release and is not reported. Junie is usually installed globally, by its install script, Homebrew or `npm install -g`, which no file AAK reads. The launcher installs one build, and Junie's shim can fetch and run another (`--use-version`, or a channel's latest build), so a stated version does not prove which build runs. `@jetbrains/junie-cli` releases below 888.0.0, which install the EAP builds of August 2025 to February 2026, and its empty 1.0.0 are not reported. A project's own `.junie/mcp/mcp.json` is not read. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `@jetbrains/junie` to 2548.5.0 (Junie 26.8.3) or later and pin it. `@jetbrains/junie-cli` stopped at 1468.30.0, so move to `@jetbrains/junie`. Until then, do not start Junie in a repository you do not trust, and read its `.junie/mcp/mcp.json` first.
rules.title: JetBrains Junie CLI before 26.8.3 (npm build below 2548.5.0): an untrusted project's MCP server configuration runs code

rules.description: Grafana's `mcp-k6`, an MCP server for the k6 load-testing tool, has a `convert_playwright_script` prompt that takes a script path. From 0.3.0, when the prompt arrived, until 0.7.0, a caller could pass a bare path and get back any file the server's user can read, SSH keys and cloud credentials included, and a symlink inside the working directory took an `@`-prefixed path outside it (CVE-2026-89039, CVSS 3.1 6.5, CWE-22/CWE-424). It is a Go binary, and its recommended install is the Docker Hub image `grafana/mcp-k6`. In 0.7.0 a bare value is script text, never a path, and an `@` reference must name a `.js`/`.ts`-family file inside the working directory, read through a handle that will not leave it, links included (grafana/mcp-k6#191).
rules.limitations: Reads `grafana/mcp-k6` image references from 0.3.0 up to 0.7.0, and an untagged or `latest` reference, because `latest` was the 0.6.1 image on 2026-10-06. That needs revisiting once a 0.7.0 image is pushed. Tags 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 predate the prompt and are not reported. The bare Docker Hub name is matched, so `docker.io/grafana/mcp-k6` is not read. A Homebrew install or a release binary states no version AAK reads.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `mcp-k6` to 0.7.0 or later. Docker Hub had no 0.7.0 image on 2026-10-06, so until one is pushed, run the 0.7.0 release binary or build the image from the v0.7.0 tag, and do not expose the prompt to untrusted callers.
rules.title: Grafana mcp-k6 0.3.0 to 0.6.1: the convert_playwright_script prompt reads any file

rules.description: `mcp-server-kubernetes` before 3.9.0 has an argument-injection flaw in its structured tools (`kubectl_get`, `kubectl_describe`, `kubectl_delete`): `resourceType` / `name` parameters with leading dashes bypass the `assertNoDangerousFlags` check, so an attacker can inject `--server` to redirect kubectl at an attacker-controlled API server, exfiltrating the operator's bearer token and enabling full cluster compromise (CVE-2026-61459, CVSS 9.8 CRITICAL). Fixed in 3.9.0.
rules.limitations: Reads `mcp-server-kubernetes` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). The `flux159/mcp-server-kubernetes` image tag is not read, in a compose file or in an MCP config that starts it with `docker run`. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `mcp-server-kubernetes` to >= 3.9.0 and pin it. Reject tool arguments beginning with `-` and pass a `--` end-of-options separator before caller-supplied values to any spawned `kubectl` command.
rules.title: mcp-server-kubernetes < 3.9.0 (argument injection → kubectl --server redirect)

rules.description: Kimi Code (`@moonshot-ai/kimi-code`), Moonshot AI's coding agent CLI, through 0.31.0 loads the MCP configuration of the workspace it is opened in (`agent-core-v2/src/agent/mcp/config-loader.ts`) and spawns the STDIO servers a repository's `.mcp.json` declares before asking whether the workspace is trusted, so opening a cloned repository runs commands its author chose (CVE-2026-95660, CVSS 3.1 6.3, CWE-77/CWE-78). 0.31.1 adds the trust prompt and resolves `fd` and `stty` to absolute paths, so an untrusted workspace can no longer plant bare-name executables on `$PATH` before confirmation either.
rules.limitations: Reports the package where a manifest pins it. Most installs are global (`npm i -g`) and leave no file in a project, so this catches a project that declares Kimi Code as a dependency, not every machine that runs it. The project-side half of the attack, the `.mcp.json` a hostile repository ships, is what the MCP config rules read. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `@moonshot-ai/kimi-code` to >= 0.31.1 and pin it. Until then, do not open untrusted repositories with Kimi Code, and read a repository's `.mcp.json` before opening it.
rules.title: Kimi Code up to 0.31.0 starts a workspace's MCP servers before the trust prompt

rules.description: knowns (`knowns`, npm — knowns-dev) before 0.30.0 does not validate filesystem paths supplied in MCP tool arguments, so an attacker-controlled path containing directory-traversal sequences reads, creates, overwrites or deletes files outside the project directory (CVE-2026-86439, CVSS 8.8). NVD scopes the read reach to "arbitrary Markdown files accessible to the server process", which follows from where the defect sits: the document and memory stores (`internal/storage/doc_store.go`, `internal/storage/memory_store.go`) are Markdown-backed. Fixed in v0.30.0. CVE-2026-88938 (MEDIUM 6.5) then reopened the same class on a different tool: `knowns` **through 0.33.0** does not confine the `path` argument of the `code.find` MCP tool to the project root, so an agent session supplies an absolute path or traversal sequence and retrieves full file contents from anywhere the server process can read. Its advisory (GHSA-5cj9-fcqq-g2h7) names no patched version, and the releases published since 0.33.0 are not confirmed fixed, so **there is no fix floor to upgrade to** and this pin is presence-only: it fires on any referenced version. That holds until upstream names a fixed release, and is not a placeholder — the same shape as the `postgres-mcp` and `mcp-florence2` pins in this table.
rules.limitations: Reads `knowns` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, and reports every version from 0.1.1 on, a future fixed one included, until the pin gets a floor. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). The npm release 0.1.0 is affected too but is not reported, because the same number belongs to an unrelated PyPI package of that name. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: No release is confirmed fixed. Until upstream names one, run `knowns` against a directory that contains nothing the agent session should not read, or drop it. When a fixed release is named, upgrade to it and pin it. The upstream fix has to resolve every path taken from a tool argument and reject any result that escapes the project root before opening it.
rules.title: knowns MCP doc/memory and code.find tools: path traversal outside the project directory (no fixed release)

rules.description: Kortix (kortix-ai/suna, the platform NVD calls Kortix Suna) is a self-hosted AI agent platform whose API server ships as the Docker Hub image `kortix/kortix-api`. A connector takes a base URL, an OpenAPI or Postman source, or an MCP server URL, and from 0.10.7, when `apps/api/src/shared/ssrf-guard.ts` arrived, an `isPrivateIp` check refused private destinations. It did not decode IPv6 6to4 (`2002::/16`) or Teredo (`2001::/32`) addresses, which carry an IPv4 address, so a user holding `project.connector.write` could point a connector at an internal service or a cloud metadata endpoint and read the response (CVE-2026-108115, CVSS 3.1 4.9, CWE-918). 0.13.52 reads the IPv4 address out of a 6to4 address and refuses Teredo (fix commit `9c949e4`, in v0.13.52 and not v0.13.51).
rules.limitations: Reads `kortix/kortix-api` image references from 0.10.7 up to 0.13.52 in compose files, Kubernetes manifests, Helm values, Dockerfiles and MCP configs. The bare Docker Hub name is matched, so `docker.io/kortix/kortix-api` is not read. A `kortix self-host` stack names the image `${API_IMAGE}` in its compose file and keeps the tag in its `.env`, which this reader does not read, so such an instance is reported only where a manifest states the tag. `latest` was 0.13.53 and `stable` 0.13.52 on 2026-10-11, both fixed, so an untagged or channel reference is not reported. Commit-hash tags, such as every tag of `ghcr.io/kortix-ai/kortix-api`, state no version.
rules.remediation: Upgrade the `kortix/kortix-api` image to 0.13.52 or later and pin its tag. Then check connector base URLs and MCP URLs for 6to4 (`2002:`) or Teredo (`2001:0:`) addresses set before the upgrade.
rules.title: Kortix API image 0.10.7 to 0.13.51: IPv6 6to4 and Teredo addresses get past the SSRF guard

rules.description: The MCP Kotlin SDK server module (`io.modelcontextprotocol:kotlin-sdk-server`, which the `kotlin-sdk` umbrella pulls in) has an `Application.mcpWebSocket` extension that installs Ktor's `WebSockets` plugin with no `maxFrameSize`, so Ktor's default of `Long.MAX_VALUE` applies. A remote client can send small frame headers that declare payloads near 2 GiB, over one or a few connections, and force the server to allocate them until the JVM runs out of heap (CVE-2026-108714, CVSS 3.1 7.5, CWE-770). Checked in the source and on Maven Central: the extension is absent at 0.7.2, arrives in 0.7.3 and is unchanged through 0.15.0, the newest release, and nothing on `main` sets a frame limit, so there is no fixed release.
rules.limitations: Dependency-level detection on JVM manifests only: `build.gradle`, `build.gradle.kts`, `gradle/libs.versions.toml` and `pom.xml`. Reports `kotlin-sdk-server`, `kotlin-sdk` and their `-jvm` variants from 0.7.3 where a version resolves, and not `kotlin-sdk-core` or `kotlin-sdk-client`, which do not carry the extension. Every version from 0.7.3 is reported, a future fixed one included, until the pin gets a floor. It reads versions, not code, so a server that uses only stdio or SSE, or installs `WebSockets` with its own `maxFrameSize`, is reported too. A dynamic version or a `version.ref` to a catalog outside the scanned tree is not reported.
rules.remediation: There is no fixed release. Do not use `Application.mcpWebSocket`: install `WebSockets` yourself with a `maxFrameSize` sized to your largest legitimate message, and register the endpoint with `Route.mcpWebSocket`, which does not install the plugin. Or keep the WebSocket transport off untrusted networks. Pin the first fixed release once it ships.
rules.title: MCP Kotlin SDK from 0.7.3: Application.mcpWebSocket accepts WebSocket frames of any size (no fixed release)

rules.description: LangBot at 4.10.7 and earlier applies no adequate authorization boundary to the Extensions MCP configuration: in `src/langbot/pkg/provider/tools/loaders/mcp.py`, `StdioServerParameters` takes the configured command and arguments and starts a server-side subprocess, so anyone who can sign up or obtain an account executes arbitrary commands with the privileges of the LangBot service (CVE-2026-54449, CVSS 3.1 8.8). This is a **presence-only** pin because no fix exists: [GHSA-3pvh-63gf-j9mw](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3pvh-63gf-j9mw) records no patched version, NVD states none is available, and 4.10.8 -- published 31 minutes after the advisory -- is a media-delivery patch whose release notes claim no security fix. Treat every published version as exposed until upstream states otherwise.
rules.limitations: Reads `langbot` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, and reports every version, a future fixed one included, until the pin gets a floor. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`) or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A compose file's `rockchin/langbot` image tag is not read. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: No upgrade resolves this, so do not wait for one. Close the account boundary instead: disable open sign-up, and restrict the Extensions MCP configuration surface to operators rather than any authenticated user. If the deployment cannot enforce that, take the STDIO MCP configuration path out of the reachable UI, since the subprocess runs with the service's own privileges. Re-pin to a version floor once upstream ships a release that states it fixes this.
rules.title: LangBot lets any authenticated user configure an STDIO MCP command (no fix)

rules.description: `@langchain/mongodb`'s `MongoDBChatMessageHistory` keeps agent conversations in MongoDB, keyed by session id. Through 1.3.0 it put the session id into its `findOne`, `updateOne` and `deleteOne` filters as given, without enforcing the documented string type, so a structured id was read as a query condition. Where several users' histories share one collection, a caller who controls the id can read, change or delete another user's conversation (CVE-2026-106119, CVSS 4.0 6.0, CWE-943, GHSA-m6rx-h84q-8r95). An application that passes only authenticated, server-controlled string ids is not affected. 1.3.1 rejects a non-string id and wraps it in `$eq` (langchainjs#11672).
rules.limitations: Reports `@langchain/mongodb` below 1.3.1 where a package.json, lockfile or MCP config states the version, taking the lowest version a range allows. `latest` and other tags state no version and are not reported. It reads the version, not where the session id comes from, so a project that passes only server-side string ids is reported without being exposed. The Python `langchain-mongodb` is a different package and is not read. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `@langchain/mongodb` to 1.3.1 or later and pin it. Until then, give `MongoDBChatMessageHistory` only a session id your server derives as a string, never one taken from a request.
rules.title: LangChain.js MongoDB chat history through 1.3.0: an object session id reaches another user's conversation

rules.description: `@langchain/redis` is LangChain.js's Redis vector store. Before 1.1.1 it put filter values into RediSearch queries unescaped, in the structured TAG and TEXT filters, and only partly escaped in the older string-array filter, so injected RediSearch syntax could change or widen the query. An application that builds a tenant or document-access boundary from a filter an attacker can influence can then return indexed documents outside that boundary (CVE-2026-105799, CVSS 4.0 2.3, CWE-943, GHSA-5x6v-p487-7qh2). 1.1.1 escapes every filter value (langchainjs#10701).
rules.limitations: Reports `@langchain/redis` below 1.1.1 where a package.json, lockfile or MCP config states the version, taking the lowest version a range allows. `latest` and other tags state no version and are not reported. It reads the version, not the filters, so a project whose filters never carry user input is reported without being exposed. The Python `langchain-redis` is a different package and is not read. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `@langchain/redis` to 1.1.1 or later and pin it. Until then, do not build a tenant or access boundary from a filter value a user controls, or enforce the boundary outside the vector search.
rules.title: LangChain.js Redis vector store below 1.1.1: unescaped filter values widen a RediSearch query

rules.description: IBM Langflow OSS (`langflow`) from 1.0.0 through 1.10.1 is vulnerable to unauthenticated remote code execution through its MCP stdio launcher: the `DANGEROUS_ENV_VARS` blocklist in `src/lfx/base/mcp/util.py` omits `SHELLOPTS`, `BASHOPTS`, and `PS4`, so an unauthenticated attacker can inject those environment variables into a launched stdio MCP server process and achieve arbitrary code execution (CVE-2026-12940, CVSS 9.8). The same 1.11.0 floor also remediates five further Langflow OSS CVEs disclosed for 1.0.0–1.10.3: CVE-2026-17623 (command-field RCE in MCP server configurations), CVE-2026-17626 (host-file read/modify via unfiltered Docker volume-mount and device-mapping args), CVE-2026-8446 (MCP composer OAuth authentication bypass), CVE-2026-9077 (writing arbitrary MCP server configurations into host IDE config files), and CVE-2026-7646 (`resources/read` path traversal reading the JWT signing secret, the SQLite DB, and process env). A seventh, CVE-2026-9186, raised the floor past those: Langflow OSS 1.0.0–1.11.2 trusts a spoofed `X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1` header to satisfy its localhost-only guard on MCP-config installation, so a remote authenticated attacker writes arbitrary IDE configuration files (`~/.cursor/mcp.json` and siblings) — which 1.11.0, 1.11.1 and 1.11.2 are all exposed to. Three further IBM advisories then moved the floor again, all scoped 1.0.0 through 1.11.5: CVE-2026-85025 (CRITICAL 9.8) — unauthenticated arbitrary code execution and access to other users' chat sessions through publicly shared MCP project endpoints, because public-flow security restrictions and session isolation are both enforced improperly; CVE-2026-78575 (HIGH 8.8) — a remote authenticated attacker executes arbitrary commands through improperly validated command-line arguments in the MCP stdio server configuration; and CVE-2026-81941 (HIGH 8.8) — a non-administrative authenticated user runs OS commands at the application's privilege level by building a flow whose MCP Tools component uses a local stdio subprocess transport, bypassing both `LANGFLOW_CUSTOM_COMPONENT_ADMIN_ONLY` and `LANGFLOW_BLOCK_CODE_INTERPRETER_COMPONENTS`. Those are fixed in 1.11.6. CVE-2026-101861 (CVSS 4.1) then moved the floor to 1.12.0: from 1.0.16 through 1.11.6, an authenticated caller's Tool-Mode input options reach `eval()` in `schema.py` when a component is converted into a LangChain tool through `ComponentToolkit.get_tools()`, a custom-component save through the API included, so an option object with a crafted `__repr__` runs code (GHSA-33p4-w7j3-33mw). Treat < 1.12.0 (and unpinned) as exposed; 1.11.6 is exposed to that one alone. Three more advisories sit under that floor: CVE-2026-105697 (CVSS 9.9) and CVE-2026-105740 (CVSS 9.9), the MCP stdio transport running a configured command through `bash -c` with no allowlist (fixed in 1.10.3 and 1.9.0), and CVE-2026-105741 (CVSS 7.1), a spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` on the MCP-config install endpoint from 1.5.0 (fixed in 1.10.3). So does CVE-2026-105699 (CVSS 4.0 7.1): from 1.6.8, a project-scoped MCP connection's `resources/read` returned another user's flow files without checking that the flow belonged to the caller (fixed in 1.9.1). The same code ships as `langflow-base` and `lfx`, which reach 1.12.0 in the same release, so both are read at the same floor. Pre-1.0.0 releases of `langflow` predate the MCP stdio launcher and are not in the affected range.
rules.limitations: Reads `langflow`, `langflow-base` and `lfx` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock and uv.lock lockfiles, reporting a range that admits an affected version and a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`) or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A compose file's `langflowai/langflow` image tag is not read. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `langflow` (or `langflow-base` / `lfx`, where those are installed directly) to >= 1.12.0 and pin it. Do not pass an attacker-influenced environment through to a launched stdio MCP server; blocklist (or, better, allowlist) the process environment, including `SHELLOPTS`/`BASHOPTS`/`PS4`. Derive the client address from the socket, not from a caller-supplied `X-Forwarded-For` header, when gating localhost-only operations.
rules.title: Langflow MCP stdio launcher env-var-injection RCE (1.0.0–<1.12.0)

rules.description: `langgraph-api` before 0.10.0 lets a run or cron name a *relative* webhook target, delivered over an in-process loopback transport that the authentication middleware treats as internal: the external auth context is never applied. In a deployment that separates threads and runs by per-user authorization, an authenticated user can aim a webhook at the server's own thread and run routes and create a run on, or modify, another user's thread, pulling some of the targeted thread's metadata into the created run record (CVE-2026-55235, MEDIUM CVSS 5.9). Fixed in 0.10.0. The fix does not make loopback delivery safe in general: a deployment that deliberately re-enables it still carries unauthenticated webhooks and must restrict them to controlled same-process routes.
rules.limitations: Reads `langgraph-api` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`) or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `langgraph-api` to 0.10.0 or later. If loopback webhook delivery is re-enabled deliberately, restrict the targets to a controlled same-process allowlist and do not treat a transport being in-process as an authorization decision.
rules.title: langgraph-api < 0.10.0 (loopback webhook bypasses per-user authorization)

rules.description: `langgraph-checkpoint-postgres` and `langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite` persist hierarchical namespaces as a dot-joined string, which twice let one tenant reach another's stored items. Before 3.1.1 a read was scoped by matching that string as a simple prefix pattern, so a read scoped to one namespace also matched a sibling whose flattened form shares the same leading characters, or a label holding unescaped pattern metacharacters, through an ordinary scoped search or `list namespaces` call (CVE-2026-71433, CVSS 5.3; the Postgres/SQLite sibling of the langgraph-checkpoint-mongodb checkpoint leak). Before postgres 3.1.3 and sqlite 3.1.2, `PostgresStore`, `AsyncPostgresStore`, `SqliteStore` and `AsyncSqliteStore` still joined labels with `"."`, while the base store validated labels only for `put` and `aput`, so a dotted label passed to `get`, `search`, `delete`, `list_namespaces`, their async forms or a direct `batch` resolved to another tenant's namespace and read, overwrote or deleted its items (CVE-2026-115883, CVSS 4.0 6.0, CWE-20/CWE-863, GHSA-6hmw-9432-67qq). `InMemoryStore` compares namespace tuples and is not affected. Treat a release below either floor, or an unpinned reference, as exposed.
rules.limitations: Reads `langgraph-checkpoint-postgres` and `langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. Each package is judged against its own floor, 3.1.3 for postgres and 3.1.2 for sqlite, so postgres 3.1.1 and 3.1.2 and sqlite 3.1.1, fixed for CVE-2026-71433, are reported for CVE-2026-115883. The base `langgraph-checkpoint` package, where the shared label check lives, is not read. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`) or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `langgraph-checkpoint-postgres` to 3.1.3 or later and `langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite` to 3.1.2 or later, and pin them; both validate every namespace label before an operation reaches the store. Until then reject a namespace label holding a `.` before it reaches the store, for every operation, not only writes.
rules.title: LangGraph Postgres and SQLite stores leak across tenant namespaces (postgres below 3.1.3, sqlite below 3.1.2)

rules.description: The LangGraph CLI (`langgraph-cli` on PyPI; langchain-ai/langgraph) builds and deploys LangGraph agents. From 0.4.15, `langgraph deploy` logs in to the deployment's image registry by passing a temporary push token to `docker login --password-stdin`, and with `--verbose` its subprocess helper prints each command's input, token included. Anyone who can read the CI log or a terminal recording within the token's 12-hour life can pull the deployment's images or push to its image repository; the token alone cannot point the deployment at a pushed image (CVE-2026-115885, CVSS 4.0 4.1, CWE-532, GHSA-8prr-f582-jqq3). Deployments without `--verbose`, and remote image builds, are not affected. 0.4.32 runs that `docker login` with verbose output off.
rules.limitations: Reports `langgraph-cli` from 0.4.15 below 0.4.32 where a requirements*.txt (at any depth), or at the project root a pyproject.toml, Pipfile, Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock or uv.lock, or an MCP config's `uvx` launch states the version, reporting a range that admits an affected version. It reads the version, not how the CLI is run, so a project that never deploys with `--verbose`, or only builds remotely, is reported too. `latest` was 0.4.38 on 2026-10-24 and states no version, so a bare `langgraph-cli` is not reported, and neither is a CLI installed globally or into a CI image, which no project file names. npm's `@langchain/langgraph-cli` is another package and is not read. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `langgraph-cli` to 0.4.32 or later and pin it. Until then run `langgraph deploy` without `--verbose` in CI, and treat any log from a verbose deploy as holding a live registry credential until 12 hours have passed.
rules.title: LangGraph CLI from 0.4.15 below 0.4.32: `langgraph deploy --verbose` prints the registry push token

rules.description: `@langchain/langgraph-checkpoint-mongodb` (the LangGraph.js MongoDB CheckpointSaver) at 1.3.0 and below passes checkpoint identifiers (`thread_id`, `checkpoint_ns`, `checkpoint_id`) from `config.configurable` into MongoDB `find()` queries in `MongoDBSaver.getTuple()` without type enforcement. An attacker who supplies an object payload (e.g. the MongoDB operators `$gt` / `$ne`) instead of a string has it interpreted as a query operator, bypassing thread scoping and leaking checkpoints, including pending writes, across tenants (CVE-2026-48121, CVSS 6.7). Fixed in 1.3.1; treat <= 1.3.0 (and unpinned) as exposed.
rules.limitations: Reads `@langchain/langgraph-checkpoint-mongodb`, `langgraph-checkpoint-mongodb` and `langgraph-store-mongodb`, each against its own fix floor, in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`) or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `@langchain/langgraph-checkpoint-mongodb` to >= 1.3.1 and pin it. Coerce checkpoint identifiers from `config.configurable` to strings before they reach a MongoDB query, so an object payload can never be read as an operator.
rules.title: LangGraph MongoDB checkpoint saver NoSQL injection leaks checkpoints across tenants (< 1.3.1)

rules.description: `langgraph-sdk` (PyPI) supplies the custom-auth decorators a LangGraph server deployment uses to authorize access to threads, assistants and crons. From 0.1.45 until 0.4.4, `@auth.on.threads`, `@auth.on.assistants` and `@auth.on.crons` accepted an `actions` argument and registered the handler for every action on the resource anyway. That wildcard handler is chosen before broader fallback handlers, so an authenticated user can get past fallback action, ownership or permission checks and read, update or delete another user's thread, assistant or cron (CVE-2026-104873, CVSS 4.0 7.6, GHSA-fvww-7h3r-vfhp). Only a Python deployment that passes `actions` to one of those decorators is exposed, and one whose handler checks every action it receives stays protected. 0.4.4 registers the handler for the named actions only.
rules.limitations: Reports a reference that names the PyPI package `langgraph-sdk` from 0.1.45 up to 0.4.4: a requirements, pyproject or lockfile entry, or the package in an MCP config, where an unpinned reference is reported. It reads the version, not the auth handlers, so a project that uses the SDK only as a client, or never passes `actions` to these decorators, is reported without being exposed. The JavaScript `@langchain/langgraph-sdk` is a different package and is not read. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `langgraph-sdk` to 0.4.4 or later and pin it. Until then, make every handler registered with `actions` enforce the checks for all actions on its resource, or register it through `@auth.on(resources=..., actions=...)` or a per-action decorator such as `@auth.on.threads.create`, which honor the action.
rules.title: LangGraph SDK 0.1.45 to 0.4.3: resource-scoped auth decorators ignore `actions`

rules.description:
`letta` — the agent server formerly known as MemGPT — carries four disclosed vulnerabilities across its 0.4 to 0.16 line, none of which names a fixed release in NVD:
  - CVE-2025-51482 (HIGH): `run_tool_from_source` in `letta.server.rest_api.routers.v1.tools` lets a remote caller execute arbitrary Python and system commands through a crafted payload to the `/v1/tools/run` endpoint. Affected at 0.7.12.
  - CVE-2026-4964: `_convert_message_create_to_message` in `letta/helpers/message_helper.py` mishandles the File URL Handler. Affected at 0.16.4.
  - CVE-2026-4965: `resolve_type` in `letta/functions/ast_parsers.py`, explicitly recorded as an **incomplete fix** for CVE-2025-6101. Affected at 0.16.4.
  - CVE-2025-6101: `function_message` in `letta/interface.py`, reachable through the `function_name` / `function_args` arguments. Affected up to 0.4.1.
The floor is set at 0.16.5, the first release published after the highest affected version — an inference from release ordering, not a vendor fix statement, since every one of the four CPE entries names an exact version with no `versionEndExcluding` and all four GHSA records are `unreviewed` with no curated version range. Treat it as "past every version known to be affected" rather than "vendor-confirmed patched". The pin targets the PyPI `letta` server distribution only: the vulnerable code lives in `letta/...` module paths, while `letta-client` and npm `@letta-ai/letta-client` are separate client SDKs on their own version lines, and npm `@letta-ai/letta` is a 0.0.1 placeholder.
rules.limitations: Reads `letta` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`) or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A compose file's `letta/letta` image tag is not read. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `letta` to >= 0.16.5 and pin it. Because no vendor fix statement exists for any of the four, also treat the server as untrusted at the boundary regardless of version: do not expose `/v1/tools/run` beyond loopback, and require authentication in front of it — CVE-2025-51482 is remote code execution reachable through that endpoint. CVE-2026-4965 being an incomplete fix for CVE-2025-6101 is a reason to verify the behaviour yourself rather than rely on a version number alone.
rules.title: Letta (MemGPT) <= 0.16.4 (four CVEs: /v1/tools/run RCE, file-URL handler, AST parser)

rules.description: The source tree contains a Stainless auto-generation marker — either the in-file banner `File generated from our OpenAPI spec by Stainless.` (verified verbatim against github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python on 2026-05-19) or a `stainless.yml` / `.stainless/` config-as-code shape at the project root. Stainless is the API-spec-to-SDK / CLI / MCP-server generator [Anthropic acquired on 2026-05-18](https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropic-acquires-stainless). This rule is **provenance, not vulnerability** — severity INFO. It surfaces the generator lineage so procurement teams and SBOM tooling can answer 'which of our MCP servers / SDKs are generator-produced vs hand-authored.' The Anthropic announcement makes **no** mention of winding down the generator or of pre-vs-post-acquisition default differences; AAK does not fabricate either claim. If a future CVE class lands against a specific Stainless generator version, this rule will be re-targeted to fire only on the affected lineage.
rules.limitations: Looks for the banner `File generated from our OpenAPI spec by Stainless` or `Code generated by Stainless` in the first 8 lines of .py, .ts, .tsx, .js, .mjs, .cjs, .go, .java, .kt, .rb, .cs and .php files outside .git, node_modules, dist, build, .venv, venv and __pycache__, and for a `stainless.yml`-style config file or a `.stainless/` directory at the project root. A banner below line 8 (under a long licence header), a generated SDK installed as a dependency under node_modules, and a config file in a sub-directory are not reported.
rules.remediation: No action required for the rule fire itself — this is a lineage data point. For SBOM / supply-chain attestation, record the Stainless lineage alongside the package's own version metadata. `INFO` findings are not shown by default, since `aak scan` reports from `low` up; `aak scan --severity info` shows them. To suppress the rule even then, list its id under `exclude-rules` in `.agent-audit-kit.yml`, or run `aak scan --exclude-rules AAK-MCP-LINEAGE-STAINLESS-001`.
rules.title: Stainless-generator provenance / lineage (informational)

rules.description: LiteLLM (`litellm` on PyPI; BerriAI/litellm), the LLM gateway proxy, sealed UI and CLI session tokens with `encrypt_value_helper`, the helper that seals its secrets at rest. From 1.87.0 the key API seals a key's `callback_vars` metadata with the same helper (#27141), and per the advisory the API-key flow returns what it sealed, so an authenticated `internal_user` can put a forged `proxy_admin` session in that metadata, have the proxy seal it, and present the result as a bearer token: the proxy opens it, trusts the forged administrator, and grants administrative access, including commands run through its MCP stdio endpoint (CVE-2026-114612, CVSS 3.1 9.9, CWE-269/CWE-345/CWE-441, GHSA-7hp6-4w63-5g45). 1.87.0 to 1.90.x accept such a token only when `EXPERIMENTAL_UI_LOGIN` is turned on; from 1.91.0 they accept it unless that variable is explicitly false. 1.100.4, 1.101.3, 1.102.2, 1.103.1 and 1.104.0rc2 seal session tokens through `encrypt_bearer_token`, under a prefix that is also the AES-GCM associated data, so a sealed secret no longer opens as a session.
rules.limitations: Reports `litellm` from 1.87.0 below 1.100.4, and 1.101.0 to 1.101.2, 1.102.0 to 1.102.1 and 1.103.0, where a requirements*.txt (at any depth), or at the project root a pyproject.toml, Pipfile, Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock or uv.lock, or an MCP config's `uvx` launch states the version, reporting a range that admits an affected version (`litellm>=1.100.4` admits 1.101.0). `latest` was 1.106.2 on 2026-10-23 and states no version, so a bare `litellm` is not reported. It reads the version, not the proxy's settings: 1.87.0 to 1.90.x are reported although they are exposed only with `EXPERIMENTAL_UI_LOGIN` turned on, and so is a later release run with it set to false. A pre-release reads as its release, so 1.104.0rc1 and the 1.104.0 dev releases, which are affected, read as 1.104.0, which is fixed, and are not reported, while 1.101.0rc1, 1.102.0rc1 and 1.103.0rc1 read as their affected releases and are. The `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm` image tag is not read, in a compose file or in an MCP config that starts it with `docker run`, and npm's `litellm` (zya/litellmjs, a JavaScript port on its own 0.x line) is another package and is not read. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `litellm` to a fixed release and pin it: 1.100.4, 1.101.3, 1.102.2 or 1.103.1 on those release lines, or 1.104.0 or later. A lower bound below 1.103.1 still admits affected releases (`litellm>=1.100.4` admits 1.101.0 to 1.101.2, 1.102.0 to 1.102.1 and 1.103.0), so raise it to 1.103.1 or pin the exact version. Until you can upgrade, set `EXPERIMENTAL_UI_LOGIN=false`, which closes the path but also breaks CLI SSO and Claude Code gateway login.
rules.title: LiteLLM from 1.87.0 below its fixed releases: session tokens share the at-rest encryption context, so an internal user can become proxy admin

Both are fixed by 1.84.0. A project pinning `litellm` below 1.84.0 (or unpinned) is exposed. (CVSS not yet scored by NVD; auth bypass to MCP tooling.)
