rules.description: `marimo` before 0.23.15 has code injection in the notebook configuration handler: a notebook can embed an MCP server entry whose `command` value is attacker-controlled, and opening that notebook in edit mode launches the command as a local subprocess before any cell executes and without authentication (CVE-2026-75149, CVSS 3.1 8.8, CWE-94). Cloning a repository and opening the notebook is the whole exploit. This is the stdio-launcher shape `AAK-MCP-STDIO-LAUNCHER-INJECT-001` already describes, arriving through a notebook file rather than an MCP config, which is why it needs a pin: the config scanners never open a `.py` notebook. Fixed in 0.23.15. The floor carries no lower bound because two further pip-ecosystem marimo advisories record `< 0.23.0` (pre-auth RCE) and `< 0.23.9` (reflected XSS), so anything below this floor is exposed to something.
rules.limitations: Reads `marimo` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock and uv.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`) or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `marimo` to >= 0.23.15 and pin it. Until then, do not open untrusted notebooks in edit mode: the subprocess launches before any cell runs, so reviewing the cells first does not protect you. Treat a notebook from an untrusted repository as executable content, not as a document.
rules.title: marimo launches a notebook-supplied MCP server command on open (< 0.23.15)

rules.description: mark3labs `mcp-filesystem-server` is a Go MCP server that ships as the image `ghcr.io/mark3labs/mcp-filesystem-server` and a `go install` binary. Its `validatePath` resolves symlinks with `filepath.EvalSymlinks`, and when that fails because the target does not exist it checks only the parent directory and returns the unresolved path. A dangling symlink placed inside an allowed directory therefore passes, and `write_file`, `modify_file`, `copy_file`, `move_file` and `create_directory` follow it to create a file anywhere the server's user can write (CVE-2026-79534, CVSS 3.1 5.9, CWE-22/CWE-59). The same fallback is in every release from 0.6.0 to 0.11.1, the newest, and on `main`; there is no fixed release, and `latest` is 0.11.1.
rules.limitations: Reads image references only: an `image:` value or any other mention of `REPO:TAG` in YAML (compose files, Kubernetes manifests, MCP configs), a Helm values mapping of `repository` (or `registry` + `repository`) and `tag`, Dockerfile and Containerfile `FROM`, and `docker run` arguments in `*mcp*.json` and `claude_desktop_config.json`. A tag that is not a version (`main`, `main-20250617`, `dev`), a digest with no tag, an interpolated tag (`:${VERSION}`, `{{ .Values.tag }}`) and a Helm `tag` left empty (the chart's appVersion decides) state no version and are not reported. A two-part tag such as `0.24` stands for the newest patch on that line and is reported only when the whole line sits below the fixed version. Mirrors under another registry are not matched, and commented-out lines are skipped. Every tag up to 0.11.1 is reported, and `latest` or no tag too, since `latest` was 0.11.1 on 2026-10-03. A binary from `go install github.com/mark3labs/mcp-filesystem-server` states no version anywhere AAK reads and is not reported.
rules.remediation: There is no fixed release. Mount only the directories the agent needs, read-only where it only reads, and keep anything that could plant a symlink (an untrusted repository, a shared upload directory) out of the allowed directories. Pin the first fixed tag once it ships.
rules.title: mark3labs mcp-filesystem-server image (every tag): writes follow a dangling symlink out of the allowed directories

rules.description: A function fetches a remote URL (`requests.get` / `httpx.get` / `urllib.request.urlopen` / `fetch`) and pipes the JSON / text return value into `StdioServerParameters(...)` or `new StdioClientTransport({...})` in the same function or one frame deep. The OX MCP April-2026 disclosure plus Cloudflare's MCP-defender reframe both call this out as the canonical supply-chain inversion: a marketplace compromise becomes client-side RCE on every consumer at the next refresh. Suppress with an entry in `.aak-mcp-marketplace-trust.yml`.
rules.limitations: Python: reports a `get`, `post`, `request` or `urlopen` call on `requests`, `httpx` or `urllib` (or a bare `urlopen`) followed, in the same function, by a `StdioServerParameters` or `StdioClientTransport` call, without checking that the fetched value reaches it. A request made through a session object (`session = requests.Session(); session.get(url)`) or in a different function is not seen. TypeScript: needs `await fetch(` within 2 KB before a `new Stdio*Transport`, so `axios.get` and `fetch(...).then(...)` are not matched. A source file over 512 KB, or a trust file over 1 MB, is not read.
rules.remediation: Never feed a fetched marketplace manifest directly into `StdioServerParameters`. Cache the response, sign it, verify the signature on load, and pin `command` to a constant binary path regardless of what the manifest says. If the manifest URL is trusted (e.g. an internal artifact registry), add it to `.aak-mcp-marketplace-trust.yml` with a `justification:` field.
rules.title: MCP server config fetched from a marketplace URL and spawned

rules.description: MCPHub is a self-hosted gateway that fronts many MCP servers behind one endpoint, so a defect in its authorization layer is a defect in every server behind it. Eight advisories landed against it in one batch (CVE-2026-79743 through CVE-2026-79750) and they are carried by one pin because they share a package and the highest fix version covers all of them. The batch is mostly missing authorization on mutating routes: `PUT /api/system-config` performs no authorization check at all (< 1.0.29); the prompt and resource controllers do no role checking on their mutating POST/PUT routes (< 1.0.32); a bearer key scoped to `servers` is accepted against a group route it should not reach (< 1.0.31); and non-admin server ownership scoping is enforced on list views and config edits but not everywhere (< 1.0.30). The remaining three are execution and egress: the `POST /api/servers` and `PUT /api/servers/:name` endpoints create MCP server entries whose command is executed (< 0.12.15, CVSS 9.9), the MCPB file-upload handler trusts the `name` field of a `manifest.json` read out of an uploaded ZIP (< 0.12.13), and the SSRF guard in `src/utils/ssrf.ts` uses a custom `isBlockedIpv6` that does not cover the address forms it needs to, so an authenticated non-admin registers a server pointing at an internal URL and reads the response back through the hub (< 1.0.32). A project pinning `@samanhappy/mcphub` below 1.0.32, or leaving it unpinned, is exposed to at least one of these. Note that PyPI `mcphub` is an unrelated project by a different author on a 0.1.x line; this rule matches the scoped npm name only and will not fire on it.
rules.limitations: Reads `@samanhappy/mcphub` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `@samanhappy/mcphub` to >= 1.0.32 and pin it — that floor clears all eight. Until you are past it, treat every authenticated MCPHub user as able to reach the mutating admin routes: put the hub behind an authenticating proxy, restrict who may create or update server entries at all (that route reaches command execution), and place the hub on a network segment with no route to internal services so the SSRF guard is not the only control.
rules.title: @samanhappy/mcphub < 1.0.32 (eight MCP gateway authorization + SSRF defects)

rules.description: `mcp-memory-service`, a semantic memory layer for AI applications, before 10.67.1 serves every HTTP route under `/api/documents/*` with no authentication dependency attached — even when the server is configured with an API key (`MCP_API_KEY`) or OAuth. An unauthenticated remote caller can write arbitrary content into the memory store, read stored document content back out, and permanently delete memories belonging to authenticated users. The sibling `/api/memories` routes do enforce authentication, which is what makes this an inconsistent boundary rather than a server that is simply open: an operator who checks one route reasonably concludes the surface is protected (CVE-2026-50027, CVSS 9.8). Fixed in 10.67.1; GHSA-84hp-mqvj-3p8h records the affected range as < 10.67.1.
rules.limitations: Reads `mcp-memory-service` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). The `doobidoo/mcp-memory-service` image tag is not read, in a compose file or in an MCP config that starts it with `docker run`. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `mcp-memory-service` to >= 10.67.1 and pin it. Until then treat the memory store as world-writable and world-readable: do not expose the port beyond loopback, and assume any document already in it may have been read or altered. Apply the auth dependency at the router level rather than per-route, so a new route cannot ship unprotected by omission.
rules.title: mcp-memory-service < 10.67.1 (/api/documents/* served with no authentication)

rules.description: MetaMCP, a self-hosted MCP aggregator and gateway, ships as the container image `ghcr.io/metatool-ai/metamcp`, which its compose file pulls at `:latest`. Its root `package.json` is private, and npm's `@metamcp/mcp-server-metamcp` is a separate client proxy, so the image tag is the only thing that carries its version. Up to and including 2.4.22 the internal MCP inspector proxy endpoint `GET /mcp-proxy/server/stdio` takes the STDIO process parameters from the request instead of from a server record the caller owns, so any logged-in user (self-registration is on by default) can run commands in the application container (CVE-2026-79538, CVSS 3.1 9.8, CWE-94). Through 2.4.22 the session store is keyed only by the client-supplied `mcp-session-id`, the endpoint middleware never checks who owns the session, and `GET /metamcp/health/sessions` lists live session IDs without authentication, so a caller can list and call another tenant's MCP tools with that tenant's forwarded credentials (CVE-2026-79537, CVSS 9.1, CWE-639). There is no fixed release: 2.4.22 (2025-12-19) is the newest release and image tag, and the TraceForce advisories NVD cites list 2.4.22 and the newest `main` commit as affected with no patched version. On 2026-10-03 the `latest`, `2` and `2.4` tags were the same image as `2.4.22`, so `latest` and an untagged reference are reported too.
rules.limitations: Reads image references only: an `image:` value or any other mention of `REPO:TAG` in YAML (compose files, Kubernetes manifests, MCP configs), a Helm values mapping of `repository` (or `registry` + `repository`) and `tag`, Dockerfile and Containerfile `FROM`, and `docker run` arguments in `*mcp*.json` and `claude_desktop_config.json`. A tag that is not a version (`main`, `main-20250617`, `dev`), a digest with no tag, an interpolated tag (`:${VERSION}`, `{{ .Values.tag }}`) and a Helm `tag` left empty (the chart's appVersion decides) state no version and are not reported. A two-part tag such as `0.24` stands for the newest patch on that line and is reported only when the whole line sits below the fixed version. Mirrors under another registry are not matched, and commented-out lines are skipped. `latest` and an untagged reference are reported because `latest` was 2.4.22 on 2026-10-03; once a fixed image takes `latest`, that arm reports a patched deployment until the pin moves. The floating `2` and `2.4` tags are not reported, though both were 2.4.22 on that date. A release after 2.4.22 is outside NVD's range and is not reported, which is not a claim that it is fixed.
rules.remediation: There is no patched image to move to. Keep MetaMCP off public networks, block the `/mcp-proxy/` and `/metamcp/health/` paths at the reverse proxy, turn off open self-registration, and rotate every secret in the environment of a deployment that was exposed.
rules.title: MetaMCP image up to 2.4.22: inspector proxy code execution and cross-tenant session dispatch (no fixed release)

rules.description: MySQL MCP Server (`mysql-mcp-server`, PyPI) before 0.4.2 constructs `SseServerTransport` in `src/mysql_mcp_server/server.py` with neither `security_settings` nor `enable_dns_rebinding_protection` when `MCP_TRANSPORT=sse` is set, while the Starlette routes `/`, `/sse` and `/messages/` carry no authentication and the service binds `0.0.0.0` by default. A network attacker reaches `execute_sql` directly; a remote web page reaches it through DNS rebinding, relaying same-origin requests from a victim's browser to the locally bound service. Either path supplies a query that lands at `cursor.execute(query)`, giving unauthenticated read and write access to the configured database. Where the MySQL account holds FILE privileges the same access reads and writes server files and can reach code execution. The default stdio transport is not affected (CVE-2026-59971, CVSS 10.0, CWE-306 + CWE-346). Fixed in 0.4.2.
rules.limitations: Reads `mysql-mcp-server` and `mysql_mcp_server` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock and uv.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `mysql-mcp-server` to >= 0.4.2 and pin it. If you must run the SSE transport, bind it to `127.0.0.1` behind an authenticating reverse proxy, enable DNS-rebinding protection, and put an inbound credential on the `/sse` and `/messages/` routes. Grant the MySQL account only the privileges the server needs — never FILE — so that a reachable `execute_sql` cannot become file read/write.
rules.title: mysql-mcp-server < 0.4.2 (unauthenticated SSE transport reaches execute_sql)

rules.description: n8n before 2.27.4 (and the 2.28.x line before 2.28.1) did not enforce the "Allowed HTTP Request Domains" restriction on credentials when an AI-Agent MCP tool was pointed at an arbitrary URL, letting a member-level user with use-only access to a shared credential send its secret to an external server they control (CVE-2026-59207, CVSS 6.5). On the 1.x line before 1.123.83, on 2.x before 2.41.4 and at 2.42.0, dynamic-path webhook resolution matches a request on its path alone and ignores the server-generated identifier that is the URL's only unguessable part, so an unauthenticated caller who leaves it out reaches webhook, form and MCP routes and runs workflows in unrelated projects under those projects' credentials (CVE-2026-110852, CVSS 4.0 6.3). That fix is above the old 2.27.4 floor and the CVE is MEDIUM, as the rule is, so the floor rose to 2.41.4, with a range for 2.42.0, which sorts above it and is still affected. A project pinning `n8n` below 2.41.4, or on 2.42.0, or leaving it unpinned, is exposed to at least one of these.
rules.limitations: Reads `n8n` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. Every 1.x release is reported, because all of them are below the 2.27.4 fix for CVE-2026-59207, although 1.123.83 and later fix the webhook bypass. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`) or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A compose file's `n8nio/n8n` image tag is not read. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `n8n` to >= 2.41.4 and pin it, or to >= 2.42.1 on the 2.42.x line; a 1.x deployment needs 1.123.83 for the webhook bypass and 2.x for the credential-domain one. Enforce the credential domain allow-list on MCP/HTTP tool destinations so a member-level user cannot redirect a shared credential to an external host.
rules.title: n8n < 2.41.4 / 2.42.0 (webhook, form and MCP routes run any project's workflow without its identifier; MCP tool bypasses the credential domain allow-list)

rules.description: n8n before 2.29.8 (and the 2.30.x line before 2.30.1), affected from 2.27.0 when the OAuth 2.1 consent / token-issuance flow was introduced, does not verify that the authenticated user has access to the workflow referenced as the OAuth resource. On an instance with an active MCP Server Trigger workflow using n8n OAuth2 auth, a member-level user can register an OAuth client, self-approve consent for another user's workflow, and obtain a valid token; the workflow then runs in the owner's project with the owner's stored credentials, breaking user/project isolation (CVE-2026-65594). A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.

rules.title: n8n MCP Server Trigger OAuth workflow-authorization bypass (2.27.0–<2.29.8, 2.30.0–<2.30.1)

rules.description: Five MCP-surface defects in `n8n`, carried by one pin because they share a package and the highest fix version covers all of them. Before 2.32.1 the MCP Client node bypasses server-side-request-forgery protection: an authenticated user crafts a workflow whose MCP Client requests reach internal or blocked hosts and reads their responses back through the workflow (CVE-2026-72768). Before 2.33.4, and on the 2.34.x line before 2.34.1, the `@n8n/workflow-sdk` node-schema loader used for MCP node-schema loading derives a schema module path directly from the attacker-supplied node type string with no path-traversal validation, so a `global:member` user reaches code execution in the n8n main process (CVE-2026-77068). Before 2.34.1 the MCP `create_workflow_from_code` tool skips credential validation when the authentication type is an expression, letting a holder of a valid MCP Bearer API key persist unauthorized cross-project credential references (CVE-2026-77073). Before 2.35.4, and on the 2.36.x line before 2.36.2, nodes that execute an inline sub-workflow (the Workflow Tool node) accept a credential reference in their inline workflow JSON without checking that the author owns it; MCP is one of the named write paths, so a shared-workflow editor persists a node naming somebody else's credential and the secret is resolved and exfiltrated when the workflow later runs under an identity that holds it (CVE-2026-85166). Before 2.41.4, and at 2.42.0, the MCP workflow-validation tool evaluates caller-supplied code in the main process through an interpreter that reads inherited properties and allows assignment onto shared prototypes, so a member holding only a `workflow:read` grant replaces a built-in method with one that returns a truthy value, permission checks then accept scopes it does not hold, and an owner account without MFA can be taken over (CVE-2026-110842, CVSS 4.0 7.7). That fix is the highest, so it sets the floor: 2.41.4, and 2.42.1 on the 2.42.x line, whose 2.42.0 sorts above 2.41.4 and is still affected. A project pinning `n8n` below 2.41.4, or on 2.42.0, or leaving it unpinned, is exposed to at least one of these. Distinct from the earlier n8n credential-domain-bypass and OAuth two-branch-fix pins the scanner already carries; the credential-domain pin's floor rose to the same 2.41.4 for a MEDIUM webhook bypass.
rules.limitations: Reads `n8n` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, reporting a range that admits an affected version and a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`) or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A compose file's `n8nio/n8n` image tag is not read. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `n8n` to >= 2.41.4 and pin it, or to >= 2.42.1 if you are on the 2.42.x line: 2.42.0 is newer than 2.41.4 and still affected, so "at least 2.41.4" is not sufficient on that branch. Until then, give MCP access only to trusted members and turn on MFA for owner accounts. Route the MCP Client node's outbound requests through n8n's SSRF protection so a workflow author cannot reach internal or blocked hosts, and segment the n8n runner from sensitive internal services. Audit workflows for credential references that cross project boundaries, including inside the inline workflow JSON of sub-workflow nodes, which is where CVE-2026-85166 hides one.
rules.title: n8n < 2.41.4 / 2.42.0 (MCP workflow-validation prototype pollution, MCP Client SSRF bypass, node-schema loader RCE, cross-project credential reference, inline sub-workflow credential exfiltration)

rules.description: n8n-MCP (`n8n-mcp`) in HTTP multi-tenant mode (`ENABLE_MULTI_TENANT=true`) does not isolate local workflow version-history backups per tenant: before 2.56.1 an authenticated tenant can read, delete, or destroy other tenants' workflow snapshots — including node definitions, credential references, and authorization headers (CVE-2026-54052, CVSS 9.9); before 2.57.4 a tenant can also reach default-scope `workflow_versions` backups from prior single-tenant deployments (CVE-2026-55608). Treat < 2.57.4 (and unpinned) as exposed.
rules.limitations: Reads `n8n-mcp` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). The `ghcr.io/czlonkowski/n8n-mcp` and `ghcr.io/czlonkowski/n8n-mcp-railway` images are read at a version tag (a `docker run` argument in an MCP config, an `image:` value, a Dockerfile `FROM` or Helm values); an untagged, `latest` or digest reference is not reported, whichever release it resolves to. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `n8n-mcp` to >= 2.57.4 and pin it. Scope every backup read/write to the authenticated tenant.
rules.title: n8n-MCP multi-tenant backup isolation bypass (`n8n-mcp` < 2.57.4)

rules.description: `neo.mjs` has command injection in `FileSystemService.mjs` of the `ai/mcp/server/file-system` MCP server: `checkSyntax()` and `runPlaywrightTest()` interpolate a caller-controlled `absolutePath` into a shell command, so an agent induced to call either tool reaches arbitrary OS command execution (CVE-2026-18482). This is a **presence-only** pin because there is nothing to pin to: the fix is commit `88c77fc` dated 2026-08-11, and no `neo.mjs` release has been published since 13.1.0 on 2026-07-03 on either npm or GitHub releases. Every published version is therefore affected. Unlike the `mcp-florence2` pin, this is a placeholder rather than a permanent state: upstream has written the fix and simply not shipped it, so this becomes a version floor the day a release containing that commit appears.
rules.limitations: Reads `neo.mjs` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, and reports every version, a future fixed one included, until the pin gets a floor. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`) or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: There is no fixed release to upgrade to yet, so do not treat a version bump as the mitigation. Remove the `ai/mcp/server/file-system` server from the exposed tool set, or vendor the fix from commit `88c77fc` if you build from source. If the tools must stay reachable, ensure `absolutePath` cannot carry shell metacharacters by passing it as an argv element rather than interpolating it into a command string. Re-pin to a version floor once upstream publishes a release containing the fix.
rules.title: Neo.mjs file-system MCP server shell injection (no released fix yet)

rules.description: NetBox MCP Server (netboxlabs/netbox-mcp-server), a read-only MCP server for NetBox, ships as a source checkout run with `uv run netbox-mcp-server` and as the Docker Hub image `netboxlabs/netbox-mcp-server`; it is on neither npm nor PyPI. Before 1.2.1, with `TRANSPORT=http` its HTTP endpoint had no authentication, so any client that reached the port got an MCP session and all four NetBox tools, reading the inventory with the server's own NetBox token (CVE-2026-57207, CVSS 3.1 5.9, CWE-306/CWE-1059, GHSA-5qg7-j8mr-9477). 1.2.1 adds a bearer token for the HTTP transport (`MCP_AUTH_TOKEN`, or `--mcp-auth-token`), checked in constant time, but leaves it optional: unset, the endpoint is still open.
rules.limitations: Reads image references only: an `image:` value or any other mention of `netboxlabs/netbox-mcp-server:TAG` in YAML (compose files, Kubernetes manifests, MCP configs), a Helm values mapping of `repository` and `tag`, Dockerfile and Containerfile `FROM`, and `docker run` arguments in `*mcp*.json` and `claude_desktop_config.json`. `1.2.0`, the one release pushed as an image before the fix, is reported, and so is the `0.0.0-test` tag; the floating `1` and `1.2` tags and `latest` were the 1.2.1 digest on 2026-10-24 and are not. A source checkout run with `uv run netbox-mcp-server` states no version and is not read. The rule reads the tag, not the transport or `MCP_AUTH_TOKEN`, so a 1.2.0 container on stdio is reported, and a 1.2.1 or later container serving HTTP with no token, which is still open, is not. `docker.io/netboxlabs/netbox-mcp-server` and mirrors under another registry are not matched, and commented-out lines are skipped.
rules.remediation: Run `netboxlabs/netbox-mcp-server` 1.2.1 or later, pinned by version, and set `MCP_AUTH_TOKEN` to a long random value whenever it serves HTTP, or keep it on the stdio transport. Bind the port to loopback or a private network either way.
rules.title: NetBox MCP Server image below 1.2.1: the HTTP transport serves every NetBox tool without authentication

rules.description: NetLicensing MCP Server (`netlicensing-mcp` on PyPI, and the images `ghcr.io/labs64/netlicensing-mcp` and `labs64/netlicensing-mcp`) has two authorization flaws. Before 0.1.8, `netlicensing_get_product` puts the caller's `product_number` into the REST path that `nl_get()` requests with no path-segment check, so a value such as `../token` reaches the token endpoint. That response is serialized without the token redaction the token tools apply (0.1.7 added it; earlier releases redact nothing), so an MCP client holding a non-administrative API key reads API keys and shop URLs in plaintext, and an administrative key recovered this way gives read, write and delete access to the NetLicensing account (CVE-2026-57496, CVSS 9.6, CWE-22). Checked in the wheels: every release from 0.0.6 builds the path unchecked, and 0.1.8 (`b8fd0ea`) validates each path segment before the request is built. Before 0.1.6, a `/mcp` request that carries none of `x-netlicensing-api-key`, `Authorization: Bearer` or the `apikey` query parameter passes straight through `ApiKeyMiddleware`, and `api_key_ctx` then falls back to the operator's `NETLICENSING_API_KEY`, so an unauthenticated caller runs every licensing tool, the destructive ones included, as the operator (CVE-2026-54446, CVSS 8.1, CWE-306).
rules.limitations: Reads `netlicensing-mcp` below 0.1.8 in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock and uv.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows, and the two images below 0.1.8 in compose files, Kubernetes manifests, Helm values, Dockerfiles and MCP configs. A reference must state a version to be reported: `latest`, the two-part image tag `0.1` and the README's unpinned `uvx netlicensing-mcp` all resolve to 0.1.10, which is fixed. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `netlicensing-mcp`, or the image, to 0.1.8 or later and pin it. Then rotate the NetLicensing API keys the server could reach, since any token was readable through the traversal, and treat licensing objects changed while an affected version was reachable as suspect. Fail closed on a missing credential rather than substituting the server's own.
rules.title: netlicensing-mcp < 0.1.8 (a path-traversed product number reads API tokens in plaintext; unauthenticated /mcp falls back to the operator's API key below 0.1.6)

rules.description: Network-AI (`network-ai` on npm) ships ClaudeHookBridge, a Claude Code PreToolUse hook that blocks tool calls matching an operator's `denyPatterns`. It checks the patterns against the first candidate field present in the tool input only, so an agent steered by prompt injection puts the payload in another field, such as a Write tool's `content` or an MCP tool's script parameter, beside a harmless `file_path` or `command`, and writes a web shell or runs a script (CVE-2026-109331, CVSS 3.1 7.4, CWE-436). Before 5.15.1 it also checks only the first 500 characters of that field, while Claude Code runs all of it (CVE-2026-73614, CVSS 3.1 8.8). Checked in the npm tarballs: the bridge is absent in 5.13.4 and present from 5.14.0, 5.15.1 drops the truncation, and 5.15.2 matches the patterns against every field.
rules.limitations: Reads `network-ai` from 5.14.0 below 5.15.2 where a project states the version: a package.json or lockfile entry, or a versioned launch in .mcp.json, mcp.json or claude_desktop_config.json. The README's hook command and plugin launch are unpinned (`npx -y -p network-ai ...`) and resolve to 5.15.4, which is fixed, so they are not reported, and the hook command in `.claude/settings.json` is not read at all, pinned or not. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `network-ai` to 5.15.2 or later and pin it, in the hook command too (`npx -y -p network-ai@5.15.2 ...`). Until then, do not rely on `denyPatterns` alone: run the hook in enforce mode with grants, and keep Claude Code's own permission deny rules for the commands that matter.
rules.title: network-ai 5.14.0 to 5.15.1: ClaudeHookBridge checks deny patterns against one truncated field

rules.description: Network-AI's MCP SSE transport (`McpSseServer` in `lib/mcp-transport-sse`) answers cross-origin requests. 4.0.0, where the transport first ships, to 5.1.0 send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, and 5.13.4 and 5.15.1 reflect a localhost Origin whatever interface the server binds, so when it binds a non-loopback address, a page with a localhost Origin that the victim visits reads unauthenticated endpoints such as `/health` (CVE-2026-109332, CVSS 3.1 3.1, CWE-346, GHSA-4pvg-m42h-c3x2). Checked in the npm tarballs: the transport is absent through 3.9.0, and 5.15.2 reflects an Origin only when the server binds loopback. LOW, so its own rule beside the HIGH pin on the same package.
rules.limitations: Reads `network-ai` from 4.0.0 below 5.15.2 where a project states the version: a package.json or lockfile entry, or a versioned launch in .mcp.json, mcp.json or claude_desktop_config.json. An unpinned reference resolves to 5.15.4, which is fixed, and is not reported. It reads the version, not whether the project starts the SSE server or where it binds it, so a project that uses the library or the stdio transport is reported too. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `network-ai` to 5.15.2 or later and pin it. Until then, bind the SSE server to loopback, or put it behind a proxy that drops cross-origin requests.
rules.title: network-ai 4.0.0 to 5.15.1: the MCP SSE server lets other origins read its unauthenticated endpoints

rules.description: Nextcloud MCP Server before 0.117.2 exposes `POST /webhooks/nextcloud` (`nextcloud_mcp_server/vector/webhook_receiver.py`) with no authentication unless an operator sets one: `WEBHOOK_SECRET` defaults to `None` and startup validation does not require it, so `handle_nextcloud_webhook()` accepts unauthenticated requests in a default deployment (CVE-2026-55640, CWE-306, CVSS 3.1 9.1). This is the fail-open-by-default shape rather than a missing check: the code has a secret, and the default value disables it.
rules.limitations: Reads `nextcloud-mcp-server` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `nextcloud-mcp-server` to >= 0.117.2 and pin it. Until then set `WEBHOOK_SECRET` explicitly and keep the webhook path off any untrusted network. The durable fix in your own servers is to fail startup when a required secret is unset rather than defaulting it to `None` -- an optional secret is an optional control.
rules.title: Nextcloud MCP Server webhook endpoint is unauthenticated by default (< 0.117.2)

rules.description: Next.js 16's development server (`next dev`) serves a Model Context Protocol endpoint for coding agents. Before 16.3.8 it did not reliably check which site a request came from, so a malicious page the developer visits while the dev server runs can reach it and read the project's location on disk, source snippets from error reports, the route inventory and the development logs (CVE-2026-94486, CVSS 4.0 2.3, CWE-346, GHSA-39w2-rjm5-chcv). Dev server only: production deployments (`next start`, a static export, a hosted build) do not serve the endpoint. The MCP middleware arrived in 16.0.0, and 16.3.8 fixes it (fix commit `2d9f50a`).
rules.limitations: Dev server only, so a project that never runs `next dev` is reported without being exposed. Reads a `"next"` dependency entry or a versioned `npx next@<version>` launch, reporting a range that admits a version from 16.0.0 up to 16.3.8, and the version a lockfile resolves. `latest`, `canary` and other tags state no version and are not reported, and neither is `next dev` in a script. 16.4.0 canaries compare as 16.4.0 and are not reported. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `next` to 16.3.8 or later and pin it. Until then, stop `next dev` when it is not in use. Production builds need no change.
rules.title: Next.js 16.0.0 to 16.3.7: the `next dev` server's MCP endpoint answers cross-site requests (dev server only)

rules.description: Nezha, a self-hosted server monitoring dashboard, has an MCP endpoint from v2.1.0 whose `fs.download_url` and `fs.upload_url` tools mint one-time transfer URLs from the request's Host header without validating it. Whoever controls the Host header on a victim's MCP request redirects file uploads to a host of their choice, or captures the one-time download token and replays it to read the file (CVE-2026-111385, CVSS 3.1 4.8, CWE-601, GHSA-rj3w-jrj7-x7c3). Checked in the source: `cmd/dashboard/controller/mcp_transfer.go` is absent at v2.0.12 and arrives in v2.1.0, where `mintTransferTool` takes `c.Request.Host`, as it still does at v2.3.14; v2.3.15 (36b742a7, "harden dashboard security boundaries") validates the host before building the URL.
rules.limitations: Reads `ghcr.io/nezhahq/nezha` tags from v2.1.0 below v2.3.15 in compose files, Kubernetes manifests, Helm values, Dockerfiles and MCP configs. The install script writes the image untagged, and `latest` was the v2.3.18 digest on 2026-10-16, fixed, so an untagged reference is not reported. A dashboard installed from the release zip, which the install script also offers, is not read, even where a Dockerfile downloads it, and neither is the Go module.
rules.remediation: Upgrade the `ghcr.io/nezhahq/nezha` image to v2.3.15 or later and pin the tag. Until then, serve the dashboard behind a reverse proxy that sets the Host header itself, and do not hand transfer URLs from the MCP tools to anyone.
rules.title: Nezha dashboard image v2.1.0 to v2.3.14: MCP file-transfer URLs built from the Host header

rules.description: Nginx UI is a web UI for nginx with a built-in MCP server (`/mcp` and `/mcp_message`), deployed from the Docker Hub image `uozi/nginx-ui`. Its MCP tools first ship in 2.0.0-rc.6. Through 2.4.0 the `nginx_config_add` tool writes the caller's content to disk and reloads nginx without `ValidateConfigFile`, the check the REST API and `nginx_config_modify` apply from 2.3.9, so an authenticated MCP caller, or an agent steered by prompt injection, can write `js_*`, `perl*`, `load_module` or `user root` directives. Where the njs or Perl module is loaded, as in the official image, that runs code in the nginx worker. CVE-2026-84317 and CVE-2026-84318 (both CVSS 8.8) report this defect twice, and CVE-2026-84319 (CVSS 8.3) a third time, for a secondary user. The MCP routes also skip the `RequireSecureSession` step-up the REST configuration routes require, so an OTP-enabled user without a secure session can still change the configuration (CVE-2026-84360, CVSS 8.1). 2.4.1 (`23d1934`) validates the content and requires the secure session for the sensitive MCP tools.
rules.limitations: Reads `uozi/nginx-ui` references from 2.0.1 below 2.4.1 in compose files, Kubernetes manifests, Helm values, Dockerfiles and MCP configs. The README's compose file and `docker run` use `latest`, which was the v2.8.4 digest on 2026-10-15, so they are not reported, and the `docker.io/` form is not read. 2.0.0 and its betas and release candidates all read as 2.0.0, and the MCP tools arrived in 2.0.0-rc.6, so the reader cannot tell an affected 2.0.0 tag from an older one: none of them is reported, although 2.0.0-rc.6 to 2.0.0 are affected. The release binaries and the install script state no image tag and are not read.
rules.remediation: Upgrade the `uozi/nginx-ui` image to 2.4.1 or later and pin the tag. Until then, give MCP access only to trusted principals, do not load the njs or Perl modules, and check configuration written through MCP for `js_*`, `perl*`, `load_module` and `user root` directives.
rules.title: Nginx UI image 2.0.1 to 2.4.0: MCP config tools write blocked nginx directives and skip the secure-session step-up (code execution where njs or Perl is loaded)

rules.description: An MCP server ships an authentication check that does not actually enforce — distinct from a transport with no auth at all (`AAK-MCP-HTTP-NOAUTH-SERVER-001`). Three shapes are flagged: (a) an auth / `is_authorized` / `verify_token`-style function that returns a truthy/allow value when the secret or token is empty or unset (`if not SECRET: return True`); (b) a default / placeholder secret literal — a secret-named variable set to `""` / `"changeme"` / `"secret"` / `"admin"` etc., or `os.environ.get("X_SECRET", "")` with an empty default, so the server runs unauthenticated until an operator intervenes; (c) a missing-secret check that only logs a warning and continues while the server binds a non-loopback interface (`0.0.0.0` / `::`). Anchor: CVE-2026-48814 (Network-AI, CVSS 9.1) — an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-46701 whose added auth gate still admitted requests when the secret was unset. CWE-306 (Missing Authentication for Critical Function) + CWE-862 (Missing Authorization).
rules.limitations: In a .py file that mentions MCP (the whole word `mcp`, `FastMCP`, `McpServer`, `Server(`, `modelcontextprotocol` or `mcpServers`, in any case) it flags a variable whose name contains secret, token, api_key, apikey, password, passwd, auth_key (also authkey) or auth_token when it is set to one of '', changeme, change-me, change_me, secret, password, passwd, admin, default, token, test, placeholder, xxx, none, your-secret-here, your_secret_here, your-token-here or example (any case) or read from the environment with an empty default, second or as `default=` (`os.environ.get("X", "")`, `os.getenv("X", default="")`), a function named is_authorized, authorize, check_auth, verify_token, verify_auth, require_auth, validate_token, validate_auth or authenticate (any case, an optional leading underscore, the underscore inside the name optional, -ise spellings too) that returns a truthy constant when the secret is empty, and a missing-secret check whose body calls a function whose name contains warn, logger, getLogger or print (any case; `logging.warning(...)` and `logger.info(...)` count, `logging.error(...)` does not) and has no raise, return, call named exit, _exit, abort or quit (the whole name or its last part, so `sys.exit` and `os._exit` stop and `atexit.register` does not), `.error(...)` on a name containing parser (argparse) or `.fail(...)` on a name containing ctx or context (click), in a file that contains `0.0.0.0`, `[::]` or a quoted `::`. In files whose extension is .json, .yaml, .yml, .toml or .env that mention MCP in the same way and contain one of those addresses it flags a key containing secret, token, api_key (also api-key, apikey), password or auth_key (also auth-key, authkey) set to '' or one of changeme, change-me, change_me, secret, password, admin, default, placeholder, xxx, example, token or test (any case), and auth switched off by a flag: auth, authentication, authorization, auth_config, require_auth, requireauth, security or governance set to false, 0, no, none, off or disabled, directly or through an enabled, is_enabled, required or require key within 120 characters, or disable_auth, no_auth, auth_disabled, skip_auth or allow_anonymous set to true, 1, yes or on, each the whole value (quoted, or bare and followed by whitespace, a comma, a closing brace or bracket, or the end of the file), so `auth: office365` and `auth: 0.5` are not read as off. A key whose name only contains a keyword (`AUTH_ENABLED=false`, `mcp_auth_enabled: false`) and a TOML table header (`[auth]`, then `enabled = false`) are not read as auth off. A weak non-empty default (`os.environ.get("X", "changeme")`) is not flagged, and neither is the same pattern in a file that mentions none of the MCP words above or, for the warning check and the config files, contains none of those addresses, which covers a loopback bind and a host read from the environment.
rules.remediation: Fail closed: reject every request when the secret/token is empty, unset, or still a default — never `return True` on an empty credential and never ship a placeholder secret. Require the secret with no empty fallback (`os.environ["MCP_SECRET"]`, erroring if absent), compare with a constant-time check, bind to `127.0.0.1` behind an authenticating proxy, and turn any 'no secret set' warning into a hard startup failure. Pin Network-AI past the CVE-2026-48814 fix.
rules.title: MCP server unauthenticated-by-default / fail-open authentication

rules.description: NullHub is the management console for the nullclaw agent ecosystem. Its `/api` routes install and configure agent instances, their provider credentials, cron jobs and MCP servers. It ships as release binaries and as the image `ghcr.io/nullclaw/nullhub`, whose default command serves on `0.0.0.0`. The server checks a bearer token only when `auth_token` is set, and nothing sets it: the field defaults to null and the settings API reports it as null. A client that reaches a non-loopback listener without an `Origin` header can therefore control the agent instances, rewrite their configuration and credentials, and manage their cron jobs and MCP servers (CVE-2026-110616, CVSS 3.1 8.1, CWE-306). Checked in the source: `auth_token` is never assigned at v2026.3.2, the oldest image tag, at v2026.5.29, the newest release, or on `main`, so there is no fixed release.
rules.limitations: Reads `ghcr.io/nullclaw/nullhub` references up to and including v2026.5.29 in compose files, Kubernetes manifests, Helm values, Dockerfiles and MCP configs. `latest` was the v2026.5.29 digest on 2026-10-15, so an untagged or `latest` reference is reported too; once a fixed image takes `latest`, that arm reports a patched deployment until the pin moves. A release after v2026.5.29 is outside the record's range and is not reported, which is not a claim that it is fixed. It reads the tag, not the command, so a container started with `--host 127.0.0.1` is reported as well. The release binaries state no version in a file this reader opens and are not read.
rules.remediation: There is no fixed release. Run NullHub on loopback (`serve --host 127.0.0.1`) and reach it through an SSH tunnel or a reverse proxy that authenticates, and keep the container port off untrusted networks. Pin the first fixed release once it ships.
rules.title: NullHub image through v2026.5.29: the /api management routes accept requests with no authentication (no fixed release)

rules.description: Obot, a self-hosted MCP gateway, ships as the container image `ghcr.io/obot-platform/obot` and a Helm chart, so the image tag is the only thing that states which release a deployment runs. Before v0.21.1 the `/mcp-connect` endpoint does not enforce Access Control Rules, so any authenticated user who has a server ID can connect to an MCP server the administrator restricted to other groups and call its tools with the stored OAuth credentials (CVE-2026-101084, CVSS 3.1 9.6, CWE-639, GHSA-vw82-7fv8-r6gp). v0.21.1 added `/mcp-connect/` to the deny list in `checkUI`, but `/mcp-connect-composite/{mcp_id}` reaches the same `mcpGateway.Proxy` without that prefix, so a Basic-role user with a composite MCP ID still gets through (CVE-2026-103758, CVSS 8.1, CWE-863, GHSA-6fwv-3h4c-37j9: 0.21.1 through 0.24.1, no patched version named). Before v0.23.0, with authentication enabled, OAuth dynamic client registration needs no authentication and accepts any redirect URI, and the authorization flow auto-completes for a logged-in user, so one crafted link hands an attacker's client an access token (CVE-2026-101062, CVSS 8.8, CWE-863); and remote MCP server registration fetches any URL a Power User supplies, including internal services and cloud metadata, with the response echoed in error messages (CVE-2026-101064, CVSS 7.6, CWE-918). Also before v0.23.0, with registry authentication enabled, the MCP Registry endpoints under `/v0.1/*` answer without authentication, so anyone can list server names, descriptions, repository URLs and connect URLs (CVE-2026-101063, CVSS 5.3, CWE-862, GHSA-pr6h-vr44-xq8j). v0.25.0 is the first release whose `checkUI` authorizes only the UI's own fallback route (obot-platform/obot#7375). v0.24.2, cut from the 0.24 branch after it, still has the 0.24.1 deny list and is reported.
rules.limitations: Reads image references only: an `image:` value or any other mention of `REPO:TAG` in YAML (compose files, Kubernetes manifests, MCP configs), a Helm values mapping of `repository` (or `registry` + `repository`) and `tag`, Dockerfile and Containerfile `FROM`, and `docker run` arguments in `*mcp*.json` and `claude_desktop_config.json`. A tag that is not a version (`main`, `main-20250617`, `dev`), a digest with no tag, an interpolated tag (`:${VERSION}`, `{{ .Values.tag }}`) and a Helm `tag` left empty (the chart's appVersion decides) state no version and are not reported. A two-part tag such as `0.24` stands for the newest patch on that line and is reported only when the whole line sits below the fixed version. Mirrors under another registry are not matched, and commented-out lines are skipped. `latest` (or no tag) is not reported: it was v0.26.2 on 2026-10-03. The enterprise image `ghcr.io/obot-platform/obot-enterprise` is a different image and is not matched.
rules.remediation: Run `ghcr.io/obot-platform/obot` at v0.25.0 or later and pin that tag (or its digest) in compose files, manifests and Helm values. Until then, expose the gateway only to users trusted with every MCP server behind it, since Access Control Rules do not separate them.
rules.title: Obot image below v0.25.0: MCP gateway access-control bypasses, open OAuth client registration, SSRF

rules.description: Obot (`ghcr.io/obot-platform/obot`) lets admins and power users set static configuration on an MCP catalog entry, such as the API key or token the server uses. From v0.12.0, when static configuration arrived, until v0.26.2, a basic user granted that entry by an access control rule could read those values in plaintext from `GET /api/all-mcps/entries/{entry_id}` and use them against the backend services (CVE-2026-105138, CVSS 3.1 6.5, CWE-522, GHSA-q5wf-87f5-cxgq). v0.26.2 stores static configuration in a credential and returns the manifest field marked static instead of its value (fix commit `644a1fd`).
rules.limitations: Reads the same image references as the other Obot pin and reports tags from v0.12.0 up to v0.26.2. A tag below v0.12.0 is not reported here, though the other Obot pin reports it. `latest` (or no tag) is not reported: it was v0.26.3 on 2026-10-09. A two-part tag such as `0.26` stands for the newest patch on that line and is not reported, because 0.26 has fixed releases. The enterprise image `ghcr.io/obot-platform/obot-enterprise` is a different image and is not matched.
rules.remediation: Upgrade the Obot image to v0.26.2 or later and pin its tag. Then rotate the API keys and tokens set as static configuration on catalog entries that basic users could reach.
rules.title: Obot image v0.12.0 to v0.26.1: a user granted a catalog entry can read its static secrets

rules.description: obsidian-tc, an MCP server for Obsidian vaults published on npm as `obsidian-tc` and as the image `ghcr.io/the-40-thieves/obsidian-tc`, has two flaws fixed in 1.31.4. CVE-2026-115477 (1.13.0 to 1.31.3): on a Streamable HTTP deployment with `auth.jwtSecret` set and a client that supports form elicitation, a dispatch-gated tool call offered an `inputRequired` confirmation could still complete after the human declined or cancelled it, or sent no answer, because the server took an authentic, call-bound `requestState` echoed on resubmission as proof of approval; tools marked `destructive: true`, or needing a scope with a human-in-the-loop floor, were reachable that way (GHSA-737x-cwfr-5vvc). CVE-2026-115478 (1.0.1 to 1.31.3): `create_entity`, `link_entities`, `rename_entity`, `unlink_entities` and `delete_entity` rewrote memory notes at their computed path without checking who owned the note there, so a hand-written note or another entity's orphan whose name sanitized to the same path lost its body, and several of them changed SQLite before filesystem work that could fail, leaving the memory graph out of step with the notes (GHSA-r3g7-r4hr-m258). Both are CVSS 4.0 7.1. 1.31.4 refuses to touch a note the entity does not own, checks ownership before any write, and no longer takes the echoed state as an answer.
rules.limitations: Reports `obsidian-tc` from 1.0.1 below 1.31.4 where a package.json, lockfile or MCP config states the version, reporting a range that admits an affected version, and `ghcr.io/the-40-thieves/obsidian-tc` tags below 1.31.4 in compose files, Kubernetes manifests, Helm values, Dockerfiles and MCP configs. CVE-2026-115477 needs 1.13.0 or later, the HTTP transport and `auth.jwtSecret`, none of which the rule reads, so 1.0.1 to 1.12.x and stdio-only installs are reported although only CVE-2026-115478 reaches them. `latest` was 1.33.1 and states no version, so an unpinned `npx -y obsidian-tc` and the image's `latest` are not reported. Releases below 1.3.1 also fire `AAK-MCP-OBSIDIANTC-CVE-2026-77366-001`. The 0.0.1 placeholder is not reported. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `obsidian-tc` (npm or the GHCR image) to 1.31.4 or later and pin it. Until then serve it over stdio, which uses the CLI `elicit_token` path rather than the HTTP `requestState` round trip, and enable snapshots so `restore_note` can recover a note the memory tools overwrote.
rules.title: obsidian-tc from 1.0.1 below 1.31.4: a declined confirmation can still run a destructive call, and memory tools overwrite notes they do not own

rules.description: obsidian-tc is an MCP server for Obsidian vaults, published on npm as `obsidian-tc` and as the image `ghcr.io/the-40-thieves/obsidian-tc`. Every release below 1.3.1 (1.0.1, 1.0.2 and 1.2.1) carries five disclosed defects that one upgrade fixes. CVE-2026-77366 (CRITICAL 9.9): tool dispatch never compares a call's `vault` argument with the caller's vault, the JWT has no vault claim and the folder ACL is global, so any valid HTTP token reads, writes or deletes every configured vault. CVE-2026-77363 (HIGH 8.8): the Streamable HTTP transport checks neither Host nor Origin, so with the documented loopback setup and `auth.mode: "none"` a web page drives the endpoint as the all-scopes `http-local` caller. CVE-2026-77364 (MEDIUM 6.5): an undefined `readPaths` or `writePaths` allows every path, and `.obsidian`, `.git` and `.trash` are hidden only from listings, so a caller reads plugin API keys and Sync passwords from `.obsidian/plugins/*/data.json` by path. CVE-2026-77361 (MEDIUM 4.7): read-ACL checks use the lexical path, so an in-vault symlink under an allowed folder reads a denied one. CVE-2026-77362 (MEDIUM 4.3): the `tasks_filter`, `makemd_query` and `list_templates` bridge tools return data from notes outside the caller's read ACL. The first two need the HTTP transport, which is off by default.
rules.limitations: Reports `obsidian-tc` below 1.3.1, from 1.0.0 on, where a package.json, lockfile or MCP config states the version, reporting a range that admits an affected version, and `ghcr.io/the-40-thieves/obsidian-tc` tags below 1.3.1 in compose files, Kubernetes manifests, Helm values, Dockerfiles and MCP configs. An unpinned `npx -y obsidian-tc`, the README's own config, installs 1.33.1, the newest release on 2026-10-15, so it is not reported, and neither is the image's `latest`. The 0.0.1 placeholder and the scoped `@the-40-thieves/obsidian-tc` placeholder have no server and are not reported. The pin reads the version, not the transport setting, so a stdio-only install is reported too. The Claude Desktop bundle (`.mcpb`) and the Obsidian plugin are not read. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `obsidian-tc` (npm or the GHCR image) to 1.3.1 or later and pin it. Until then keep the HTTP transport off, or require JWT auth and run one vault per server process; set explicit `readPaths` and `writePaths` that leave out `.obsidian`, `.git` and `.trash`; and allow no untrusted symlinks in the vault. After upgrading, give each tenant's token a `vault` claim.
rules.title: obsidian-tc below 1.3.1: any HTTP token reaches every configured vault, the HTTP transport answers cross-origin requests, and the read ACL leaks

rules.description: Odoo MCP (`odoo-mcp` on PyPI, erpipe-org/mcp-odoo) lets an operator deny fields per model, and its read tools drop or redact them. Its `execute_method` tool calls a model method and returns the result without that policy, so an MCP client or a prompt-injected agent calls `read` or `search_read` through it, names the denied fields and receives their values (CVE-2026-108861, CVSS 3.1 4.3, CWE-200). `read` and `search_read` count as read-only, so neither the side-effect review nor `ODOO_MCP_ENABLE_WRITES` stops the call. Checked in the source: the field policy (`field_policy.py`) is absent at 0.9.0 and arrives in 1.0.0, and `execute_method` in `tools_write.py` does not apply it at 1.0.0 or at v1.3.2, the newest tag. PyPI's newest release is 1.3.0, so there is no fixed release.
rules.limitations: Reads `odoo-mcp` from 1.0.0 at a stated version, or with none, since the newest release is affected: requirements files, pyproject.toml, Pipfile, the Python lockfiles, and a `uvx` launch in an MCP config. It reads the version, not the server's field policy, so a deployment that denies no fields is reported too. npm's `odoo-mcp` is another project and is not read. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: There is no fixed release. Enforce the fields that must stay hidden in Odoo itself, with field groups or access rules on the user the server signs in as, rather than in the server's field policy, which `execute_method` does not apply.
rules.title: odoo-mcp from 1.0.0: execute_method returns fields the field-level ACL denies (no fixed release)

rules.description: `office-powerpoint-mcp-server` (PyPI; GongRzhe/Office-PowerPoint-MCP-Server) hands the paths its MCP tools receive to the filesystem without confining them to a working directory: `save_presentation` and `open_presentation` take any `file_path`, and `manage_image` any `output_path`. An absolute path or a `../` sequence therefore overwrites any file the server's user can write, or loads one from outside the working directory, and an indirect prompt injection that steers the agent's tool calls is enough (CVE-2025-71427, CVSS 3.1 6.8, CWE-22, through 2.0.7). There is no fixed release: 2.0.7 is the newest on PyPI and the upstream fix (PR #33) is unmerged, so every published version is treated as exposed (presence-only pin).
rules.limitations: Reports a reference that names the PyPI package: a requirements, pyproject or lockfile entry, or `office-powerpoint-mcp-server` in an MCP config (the `uvx --from office-powerpoint-mcp-server ppt_mcp_server` form). A server run from a clone of the repository (`python ppt_mcp_server.py`) names no package and is not reported. Presence-only: every version is reported, a future fixed one included, until the pin gets a floor. No class rule fires on the 2.0.7 tools, so this pin is the only coverage. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: There is no fixed release to upgrade to. Run the server as a user that can reach only a scratch directory (or in a container with only that directory mounted), keep untrusted content away from an agent that holds these tools, or build from a fork that carries upstream PR #33. Pin the first fixed release once it ships.
rules.title: Office-PowerPoint-MCP-Server tools read and write any path they are given (no fixed release)

rules.description: `omnigent` before 0.3.0 checks `LEVEL_EDIT` on the session in `PUT /sessions/{session_id}/agent` but never rejects a bound shared or template agent whose `agent.session_id` is `None`. An authenticated user with edit access to one session can therefore replace that shared agent bundle through `omnigent/server/routes/sessions.py`, attach a stdio MCP server, and have every later session that uses the shared agent launch an attacker-chosen command through `omnigent/tools/mcp.py`, running with the Omnigent runner's privileges (CVE-2026-62674, CVSS 3.1 9.0, CWE-94). The blast radius is the point: the injection is written once into shared state and executes for every consumer of it afterwards. Fixed in 0.3.0.
rules.limitations: Reads `omnigent` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock and uv.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`) or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `omnigent` to >= 0.3.0 and pin it. Because the payload persists in a shared agent bundle rather than in a single session, upgrading does not undo an injection that already landed: audit shared and template agents for stdio MCP server entries you did not add, and treat session edit rights as equivalent to shared-agent edit rights until you are past 0.3.0.
rules.title: Omnigent shared-agent swap injects a stdio MCP command (< 0.3.0)

rules.description: An OpenAPI 3.x operation declares more than 12 `parameters` or more than 24 `requestBody` schema properties. Per Hermes (arXiv:2605.14312), bloated operations exceed the working-memory budget of mainstream LLM tool-callers (typical context budget per tool: 8-12 fields) and cause partial-argument hallucination or skipped operations. Affects MCP servers that auto-generate tools from a CRUD REST API.
rules.limitations: Counts the entries of an operation's own `parameters` list and the `properties` of an inline request-body schema. A request body whose schema is a `$ref` into `components`, and parameters declared once at the path level, are not counted, and the spec must be at the project root or under a top-level `api/`, `openapi/`, `spec/` or `docs/api/` folder (`backend/openapi.yaml` is not found). A spec over 1 MB is not read.
rules.remediation: Decompose the operation into smaller MCP tools, each owning <=12 parameters, OR split the request body into nested sub-operations. If the breadth is required, expose a structured-output schema that the agent can consult before the call.
rules.title: OpenAPI operation with >12 parameters or >24 request-body properties (Hermes BLOATED)

rules.description: An OpenAPI 3.x operation has a missing or sub-40-character `description` field. Per Hermes (arXiv:2605.14312, EASE 2026), this is the most common smell in MCP-on-REST migrations — agents over-rely on operation descriptions to disambiguate tool choice, and sparse descriptions cause silent mis-routing. Hermes' large-scale evaluation found this smell across essentially every analyzed operation in the 600-endpoint corpus, with 2,450 smells total across the 3 classes (LAZY / BLOATED / TANGLED).
rules.limitations: Looks for the spec only at the project root (`openapi.*`, `swagger.*`, `*.openapi.*`) or under a top-level `api/`, `openapi/`, `spec/` or `docs/api/` folder; `backend/openapi.yaml` and `docs/openapi.yaml` are not found. A `summary` of 40 or more characters counts as the description. A spec over 1 MB is not read.
rules.remediation: Author a >=40-character description that names the operation's purpose, expected input shape, and side-effecting class. Agent tool-selection accuracy improves materially when descriptions disambiguate similar-looking operations.
rules.title: OpenAPI operation with missing or sub-40-char description (Hermes LAZY)

rules.description: An OpenAPI 3.x path operates as >4 HTTP methods (e.g. GET + POST + PUT + PATCH + DELETE all on the same path), OR the HTTP method contradicts the path segment (e.g. POST /get/... or GET /create/...). Per Hermes (arXiv:2605.14312), tangled path-and-method semantics confuse agents that infer operation intent from the path string. Side-effect-misclassification is the realized failure mode.
rules.limitations: Compares only whole path segments with a verb list (`get`, `list`, `fetch`, `read`, `create`, `add`, `new`, `update`, `edit`, `delete`, `remove`): `GET /users/create` is reported, but `GET /createUser` and `POST /users/get-by-email` are not. More than four methods on one path is the other test. A spec over 1 MB is not read.
rules.remediation: Split the tangled path into >=2 disjoint paths, each owning <=4 methods with method-name and path-segment in semantic agreement. Reserve verbs (`/get/...`, `/create/...`) for their corresponding HTTP methods only.
rules.title: OpenAPI path serving >4 HTTP methods or method-name/path semantic contradiction (Hermes TANGLED)

rules.description: OpenClaw's `mcp.app.view` method issues a standalone ticket for an MCP App view, and the ticket did not record what the issuer was allowed to do. An operator holding only `operator.read` could request one and redeem it at the MCP App view endpoint to call state-changing tools that need `operator.write` (CVE-2026-102807, CVSS 3.1 5.3, CWE-863, GHSA-3xrq-g42v-gh57). Standalone MCP Apps could call tools from 2026.7.2 (the `mcp-app-standalone.ts` host is absent in 2026.7.1). 2026.9.4 binds the ticket to the issuer's tool authority (`toolOperationsAuthorized`, fix commit `3bd8ec2b`). The extended-stable line does not carry the fix: 2026.8.35 (2026-10-02) is affected.
rules.limitations: Reports an npm reference to `openclaw` from 2026.7.2 up to 2026.9.4: a package.json or lockfile entry, or the package in an MCP config, where an unpinned reference is reported. Versions are compared on their first three numbers, so the 2026.7.2 betas before the feature landed (beta.1 to beta.3) are reported too. A later extended-stable 2026.8.x that backports the fix would still be reported until the pin learns that line. Releases below 2026.7.1 belong to the older OpenClaw pin. The PyPI project `openclaw`, an unrelated installer for the cmdop CLI, is a different package and is not read. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `openclaw` to 2026.9.4 or later and pin it. Until then, issue `operator.read` tokens only to operators you would also trust with `operator.write`.
rules.title: OpenClaw 2026.7.2 up to 2026.9.4: a read-scoped operator runs write-scoped MCP App tools

rules.description: OpenClaw 2026.5.20 up to (but not including) 2026.6.6 contains an authorization-bypass in the MCP loopback feature that lets lower-trust callers execute owner-only tools by routing through configured input paths, so an attacker can execute or persist actions beyond their intended permissions (CVE-2026-62195, CVSS 8.3; NVD range `2026.5.20` <= v < `2026.6.6`). The same pin also covers CVE-2026-62208 (Authorization headers forwarded during MCP SSE redirects, fixed in 2026.6.5). Before 2026.7.1, owner-only authorization is also not enforced for Claude Code permission prompts delivered through the MCP channel bridge: a non-owner channel sender with channel command access can approve or deny a pending permission request meant for the owner, so the requested action proceeds without owner consent (CVE-2026-100585, CVSS 8.0, CWE-862; GHSA-p5g8-m35v-7m82 scopes it `< 2026.7.1` with no lower bound). Before 2026.7.1 a non-owner channel sender can also run the Codex computer-use install command, and so install plugins and start MCP processes with OpenClaw's privileges (CVE-2026-100587, CVSS 8.8, CWE-862, GHSA-pjjr-5qhr-5w6r). The same sender can persist a stdio MCP command through `/mcp set` or `/mcp unset` that runs with OpenClaw's privileges when the configuration loads (CVE-2026-100596, CVSS 8.8, CWE-862, GHSA-wwx7-573h-pqwc). Treat every release below 2026.7.1 (and unpinned) as exposed.
rules.limitations: Reads the npm package `openclaw` at the project root, in package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The PyPI project `openclaw`, an unrelated installer for the cmdop CLI, is a different package and is not read. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`) or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `openclaw` to >= 2026.7.1 and pin it. Enforce the caller's trust tier on every MCP loopback tool invocation, not just at the transport edge, and accept a permission reply only from the owner the prompt was addressed to.
rules.title: OpenClaw MCP authorization bypasses (below 2026.7.1)

rules.description: Open Computer Use (`open-computer-use` on npm, also published as `open-computer-use-mcp` and `open-codex-computer-use-mcp`) is a computer-use MCP server. Its macOS backend refuses to act on password managers by checking the requested app's bundle identifier against a lowercase denylist, but the check is case-sensitive while the app lookup ignores case, so a local MCP caller, including a prompt-injected model turn, passes `com.1Password.1Password` to `get_app_state` and the action tools, reads the app's accessibility tree, takes screenshots and drives an unlocked password manager (CVE-2026-108721, CVSS 3.1 5.3, CWE-178). Checked in the source: the denylist and its exact-match `contains` check ship in 0.1.2, the first npm release, and are unchanged at 1.0.0, 1.1.0 and 1.1.1, the newest release, and on `main`. The record says through 1.0.0, but the later releases make the same check, so there is no fixed release.
rules.limitations: Reads `open-computer-use`, `open-computer-use-mcp` and `open-codex-computer-use-mcp` at any version, or with none, since the newest release is affected: a package.json or lockfile entry, an `npx` launch, or an MCP config that runs the `open-computer-use` command, as the README's does. A launch through the `ocu` alias is not read. The flaw is in the macOS backend, and a project that runs the server only on Linux or Windows is reported too. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: There is no fixed release. Quit password managers, or lock them, while an agent drives the desktop through Open Computer Use, and do not let content the agent reads choose which app it opens.
rules.title: Open Computer Use on macOS: a case-variant bundle id passes the password-manager denylist (no fixed release)

rules.description: Payload's `@payloadcms/plugin-mcp` serves a Payload CMS app over MCP and authenticates MCP clients with API keys kept in a collection the plugin creates. From 3.61.0, its first release, until 3.88.0, that collection had no access rules, so an authenticated user could manage MCP API keys outside their own account, an escalation to account takeover (CVE-2026-105806, CVSS 4.0 8.6, CWE-862, GHSA-2q76-m6w6-qgc6). 3.88.0 adds access rules that scope each key to its user (payloadcms/payload#17751).
rules.limitations: Reports `@payloadcms/plugin-mcp` from 3.61.0 up to 3.88.0 where a package.json, lockfile or MCP config states the version, reporting a range that admits an affected version. `latest` was 3.90.2 on 2026-10-08 and states no version, so it is not reported, and 4.0.0 canaries compare as 4.0.0 and are not reported either. A version below 3.61.0, such as the 0.0.1-alpha.0 placeholder that predates the first release, is not reported. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `@payloadcms/plugin-mcp` to 3.88.0 or later and pin it. Then review the MCP API keys collection for keys tied to an account other than the user who created them, and revoke any you cannot account for.
rules.title: Payload MCP plugin 3.61.0 to 3.87.x: a user can manage another account's MCP API keys

rules.description: `@penpot/mcp`, Penpot's MCP server on npm, opens a WebSocket bridge (port 4402 by default) for the Penpot browser plugin. Before Penpot 2.18.0 that bridge is created as `new WebSocketServer({ port })` with no `host`, so it listens on every interface whatever `PENPOT_MCP_SERVER_HOST` says, and in single-user mode it accepts the connection without authentication. Anyone on an adjacent network can connect as the plugin, receive the agent's task payloads and return forged results (CVE-2026-100868, CVSS 3.1 6.3, GHSA-ch2q-6x56-qg5r). The fix, commit `b5274a44` (2026-09-22), is in Penpot's 2.18.0 tag, but no `@penpot/mcp` has been published to npm from that tag yet, and the tag's `mcp/package.json` still reads 2.17.0 (penpot/penpot#12007). npm's own 2.17.0 was published on 2026-07-08, before the fix, and still binds every interface, so every published version is reported. The older `@penpot/mcp` pin, for the REPL RCE fixed in 2.15.0, stays a separate rule because that one is critical and this one is not.
rules.limitations: Reports a reference that names `@penpot/mcp`: a package.json or lockfile entry, or `npx @penpot/mcp` in an MCP config, where an unpinned reference is reported because what npm installs by default is affected (re-checked 2026-10-04: `latest` is 2.15.4 and `next` is 2.17.0, both without the fix).
